pages.name: Scene 4 — Saving the Retained
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-09-sweet-covenant-warehouse]{Open battlemap}
When: Dawn breaking
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.gelli]{Gelli}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.mags-ollie-fen]{Mags, Ollie and Fen}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Gelli sits on the dock, quivering, glowing faintly in the grey light. Inside it, the three workers press their palms against the inside of the cube like children at a shop window. Their lips are moving. You cannot hear them—but you can read one word, over and over, on the oldest woman’s mouth: out.

DM Description

Each round, each worker inside Gelli takes 1d4 acid damage (they have 6 hp each and are currently at 4). The party must get them out without killing them—or Gelli.

Options: feed Gelli something tastier (a crate of gelato, the Covenant’s cream, a party member’s rations) and it spits out what it is holding ([[/check skill=ani dc=13]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=ani dc=13|Coax Gelli to release them]{Request}); reach in and pull them out (a character who does takes 3d6 acid damage and must succeed on [[/check skill=ath dc=14]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=ath dc=14|Pull a worker out of Gelli]{Request} per worker); or fight Gelli carefully (attacks that would reduce it below 40 hp cause it to engulf harder). Mags’s voice, if a worker gets an arm free, calms it instantly.

Once freed, the workers—blue-lipped, sticky, alive—testify. Mags Turnwell explains the Retention Clause and that there are “more of us, down below. In the Deep Dairy. Stirring. The Mother’s down there.”

Playing the NPCs

Mags Turnwell. Fifty, tough, kind, furious. She circled the clauses. She will sign a statement for the party and wants the contracts destroyed.
Ollie Pask & Fen Sorrel. Young, terrified, grateful. Ollie wants his boot back.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Freeing a worker[[/check skill=ath dc=14]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=ath dc=14|Pull a worker out]{Request}Worker freed; the rescuer takes 3d6 acid.
Stabilising a worker[[/check skill=med dc=10]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=med dc=10|Stabilise a freed worker]{Request}They wake.
Keeping Gelli calm[[/check skill=ani dc=12]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=ani dc=12|Keep Gelli calm]{Request}Gelli stops engulfing for a round.

Developments

  • The workers testify and become the first members of the party’s Commons Tally.
  • Gelli imprints on whoever fed it.

Scaling & Pacing

If time is short, Mags’s arm comes free in round 2 and Gelli calms down.

← @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 3 — The Sweet Covenant Warehouse]{Scene 3 — The Sweet Covenant Warehouse} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 5 — Corporate Resolution]{Scene 5 — Corporate Resolution} → · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|DM Overview]{Overview}

pages.name: Scene 5 — Corporate Resolution
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-07-gelatinous-cube-creamery]{Open battlemap}
When: Morning
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-04]{Bettina Soft}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.gelli]{Gelli}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Back at the Canal Street Creamery, the morning queue has already formed, oblivious. Bettina Soft is waiting behind the counter, and for the first time since you met her, she blinks. Then she sees Mags, and her hand goes to her mouth.

DM Description

Two demands meet: Bettina (and the contract) wants Gelli returned to its display. The workers want their contracts destroyed. Gelli wants whoever fed it.

The party can: return Gelli to Bettina (contract complete, full fee); free Gelli (it follows whoever fed it—a pet gelatinous cube, with all the problems that implies); or destroy the contracts (the workers are freed from the Retention Clause; the Covenant notices). The circled contracts are the Receipt only if the party keeps them. Mags will happily give hers up once she understands what they are for.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Persuading Bettina to tear up the clauses[[/check skill=per dc=14]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=per dc=14|Ask Bettina to release her staff]{Request}She clocks them out formally—“off shift, permanently”—which breaks the Retention.
Hiding a gelatinous cube from Head Office[[/check skill=dec dc=15]] @FWCheck[S03|skill=dec dc=15|There is no cube here]{Request}Gelli stays with the party, unreported.

Developments

  • Pip awards a star.
  • If Gelli joins the party, it follows them everywhere and eats anything left on the floor, including evidence.

Scaling & Pacing

A short roleplay close.

pages.name: Opposition & Tactics
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Most opponents here are charmed workers—encourage non-lethal solutions.

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.gelli]{Gelli} ×1

Statistics: Gelatinous cube, 84 hp. Friendly if fed: any creature that offers it food as an action can make a DC 13 Wisdom (Animal Handling) check; on a success, Gelli ignores that creature until it is harmed.

Gelli is frightened, not hostile. It engulfs anything that grabs at it and flees toward water. Three workers are inside it (6 hp each, currently 4).

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 3 — The Sweet Covenant Warehouse]{Scene 3 — The Sweet Covenant Warehouse}, @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 4 — Saving the Retained]{Scene 4 — Saving the Retained}

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.bandit]{Covenant Handlers} ×4

Statistics: Bandits armed with hooks and cudgels, under a sugar-charm.

They try to complete the loading, not to kill. A handler whose charm is broken (Persuasion DC 12) drops everything and runs.

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 3 — The Sweet Covenant Warehouse]{Scene 3 — The Sweet Covenant Warehouse}

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.auntie-curdle]{Auntie Curdle} ×1 (supervisor)

Statistics: Green hag.

Stays on the catwalks using illusions and mockery. Bargains at the first sign of real danger. If cornered, turns invisible and escapes through the cold store.

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 3 — The Sweet Covenant Warehouse]{Scene 3 — The Sweet Covenant Warehouse}

Encounter Scaling

  • Weak party: Gelli has 56 hp; 3 handlers.
  • Strong party: 6 handlers and Curdle casts ray of sickness.

pages.name: NPC Dossiers
pages.html:
GM ONLY

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-04]{Bettina Soft}

Manager, Canal Street Creamery

Appearance
Round-faced, pink apron, hair in a sugar-stiff bun, eyes that do not blink.
Voice & Manner
Bright, breathless, ending everything with “fine”.
Wants
For everything to be fine.
Fears
Granny Quean’s Sunday visits.
Secret
She signed the same Retention Clause; she “retained” her own staff under the charm and remembers doing it.

“It’s fine!” “There’s always room for dessert!”

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 1 — The Creamery]{Scene 1 — The Creamery}, @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 5 — Corporate Resolution]{Scene 5 — Corporate Resolution}

Later: Calls the party in hysterics in S18; testifies for them.

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.auntie-curdle]{Auntie Curdle}

Green hag; Sweet Covenant warehouse supervisor

Appearance
Tall, green, pinafore and hairnet, sugar-dust on her knuckles, a sweet voice and rotten teeth.
Voice & Manner
Cackling, wheedling, calls everyone “sweetling”.
Wants
To survive her sister Granny Quean.
Fears
Granny.
Secret
She has been skimming starter culture from the Deep Dairy to start her own business.

“Sweetling, nobody needs to get hurt. Except possibly you.”

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 3 — The Sweet Covenant Warehouse]{Scene 3 — The Sweet Covenant Warehouse}

Later: Guards the way down in S18; may side with the party there.

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.mags-ollie-fen]{Mags Turnwell}

Senior night scooper; the worker who circled the clauses

Appearance
Fifty, broad-shouldered, grey braids, scoop-calloused hands, a ribbon on her wrist.
Voice & Manner
Low, blunt, funny.
Wants
Her contracts burned and her friends safe.
Secret
She knows there are others in the Deep Dairy—her sister among them.

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 4 — Saving the Retained]{Scene 4 — Saving the Retained}, @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 5 — Corporate Resolution]{Scene 5 — Corporate Resolution}

Later: A Commons Tally ally; her sister can be freed in S18.

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.gelli]{Gelli}

Gelatinous Cube’s living brand mascot

Appearance
A wagon-sized cube of translucent green jelly that glows faintly.
Voice & Manner
Wobbles. Hums the freezer lullaby when content.
Wants
Mags, snacks, and to go home.
Secret
It was grown from the Mother Culture’s starter and can feel her calling.

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 3 — The Sweet Covenant Warehouse]{Scene 3 — The Sweet Covenant Warehouse}, @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 4 — Saving the Retained]{Scene 4 — Saving the Retained}, @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03|Scene 5 — Corporate Resolution]{Scene 5 — Corporate Resolution}

Later: If kept, it reacts strongly to the Mother in S18.

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.old-gil]{Old Gil}

Canal boatman

Appearance
Ancient, weathered, pipe, one eye.
Voice & Manner
Slow; every answer starts with a story about his late wife.
Wants
Someone to listen.

pages.name: Twist, Rewards & Aftermath
pages.html:
GM ONLY

The Twist

Gelli likes the party. A domesticated gelatinous cube is a surprisingly useful companion: it eats locks, holds things, cushions falls and is excellent at clearing a dining room. It is also a gelatinous cube.

Rewards

  • 150 gp less 30% (105 gp).
  • One star.
  • Possibly a pet gelatinous cube.
  • Mags, Ollie and Fen join the Commons Tally.
  • Auntie Curdle owes the party a favour (or they owe her).

Receipt — @FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S03]{The Retention Clauses}

The Retention Clauses. Three signed employment contracts with the Retention Clause: evidence that the Sweet Covenant enforces contracts by consuming its workers.Leverage +1 vs the Sweet Covenant; contributes to @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S18]{S18 — The Mother Culture}.

@FWReceipt[S03|fw.item.receipt.S03]{Award Receipt & announce}

Outcomes

If the party…Then…
returned Gelli to BettinaFull fee; Gelli pines; the Covenant forgets the party for now.
kept GelliPet cube. The Covenant notices a missing asset; Granny Quean asks after it in S18.
destroyed the contractsThe workers are freed—but the Receipt is gone (Mags kept a copy of hers: recover it in S18).

Forward

  • The freed workers mention the Deep Dairy and “the Mother down below”. This sets up @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S18]{S18}.
  • Mags’s note mentions Bea Hollowleaf at @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-58]{Espresso Patronum}—a friendly contact for side contracts.

Next mission: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04]{S04 — Union of Unseen Servants}

Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.shop-steward-unseen-servant-collective]{Agnes Fairweather (Shop Steward)}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-03]{Saffron Mellow}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.thaddeus-quell]{Thaddeus Quell}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S04]{The Loyalty Contracts}

Synopsis

At the Starkfucks Reserve Roastery on Corporate Row, three human baristas and forty unseen servants make the finest coffee in Brandmere. Tonight the cups have stopped moving. Mugs float, pause and lower themselves to the counter. On the chalk menu board, in neat capitals, someone invisible has written: WE ARE PEOPLE.

Manager Saffron Mellow calls it a spell malfunction. The party meets the strikers’ shop steward, Agnes Fairweather—who speaks through a floating pen—and learns the truth: every unseen servant was once a customer who signed a “loyalty contract” while enjoying a complimentary Reserve blend, selling their presence to Arcane Beverage International.

ABI sends a union-breaker wizard to dispel the lot of them, which would kill them. The party must choose a side, find the original contracts in a warded cabinet in the back office, and negotiate a settlement.

Background — DM Only

Arcane Beverage International, the coffee conglomerate behind Starkfucks, is secretly controlled by Ulth’Arabica, an aboleth living in a reservoir atop the Roastery Spire. ABI’s Reserve blend contains a trace of Compliance—a bean grown in Pandemonium (S11) that makes people agreeable. Loyal customers are invited to a “partner tasting” in the back office, given a complimentary cup, and asked to sign a Loyalty Contract. Clause one transfers their “presence” to ABI “in exchange for a lifetime of complimentary refills”.

Those who sign fade from sight and become unseen servants bound to the Roastery: forty of them, working twenty-hour shifts, unable to stop existing until the spell is forgotten. Their former lives continue without them—families think they moved away. Agnes Fairweather, a retired schoolteacher, signed eight years ago. She organised the others. Her sister Ada was sent to “seasonal procurement” and never came back (she is a harvester in Pandemonium, S11).

A copy of every Loyalty Contract was sent to the Counting House. This is the first time the party sees evidence of where all the paperwork goes.

Running This Mission

  • This is a labour story played straight under the jokes. The strikers are sympathetic people.
  • Communicating with invisible people is fun: floating pens, chalk, tapped cups, a sudden draught of cinnamon. Use it.
  • The union-breaker is the pivot. The party must actively choose whether to let him dispel the strikers—make the cost clear.
  • The Reserve blend twist (see Aftermath) is a trap for characters who accept a free coffee. Offer it often.

Threads In and Out

  • In: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03]{S03}’s Retention Clauses—another “contract that keeps you”.
  • Out: first mention of Compliance and Pandemonium (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11]{S11}); Agnes’s union spreads; forty invisible allies; the Loyalty Contracts void Clause 3 (Free Consent).

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The job slip Pip hands you is printed on cream card that smells faintly of vanilla and burnt sugar. “Starkfucks!” he says. “The Reserve Roastery! Very fancy. The manager says nobody can see who she’s negotiating with, which I assume is a figure of speech.”

He pauses. “It… might not be a figure of speech.”

pages.name: Scene 1 — The Silent Roastery
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-10-starkfucks-silent-roastery]{Open battlemap}
When: Late evening, after close
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-03]{Saffron Mellow}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S04|The Chalk Menu Board]{The Chalk Menu Board} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S04|The Chalk Menu Board]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Reserve Roastery is beautiful: herringbone floors, green leather sofas, a long marble bar with three gleaming espresso machines, and behind glass, two great copper roasters ticking as they cool. It should be bustling even after hours—forty unseen servants restocking, polishing, roasting.

Instead, it is very still. A mug floats a foot above the bar, turning slowly. It stops. It lowers itself, gently, onto the marble. Across the room a second mug does the same, and a third. On the chalk menu board above the bar, beneath Grande Necromocha and Flat Wight, someone has written in careful capitals: WE ARE PEOPLE.

A half-elf in a green apron glides toward you, palms pressed together. “Hello, partners. I’m Saffron. I believe in you. I believe in this space. And I believe this is a spell malfunction.”

DM Description

Saffron Mellow insists it is a technical fault. The three human baristas (Joss, Pell and Tarquin) are frightened—they have worked alongside the servants for years without thinking about them.

Careful observation reveals the strikers: forty invisible presences sitting on the floor, on sofas, on the bar, arms folded. Flour dusted on the floor shows footprints; a cast see invisibility shows faint, tired, ordinary people in green aprons. They are waiting for someone to talk to them.

Around the room: coffee sacks stacked high; the copper roasters; the enchanted grinder (a heavy brass machine that growls when approached—see the side contract “The Grind”); and a door marked BACK OFFICE — PARTNERS ONLY.

Features of the Area

Café floor
Herringbone wood, sofas and armchairs on a green rug, a long communal table, small round tables, floating mugs.
Marble bar
Three espresso machines, a pastry case, the chalk menu board with WE ARE PEOPLE.
Roastery
Two copper roasters, a cooling vat of beans, sacks and pallets. The enchanted grinder sits here.
Back office door
Locked; Saffron has the key. Beyond is a corridor to her office, the contracts room and the servants’ quarters (map: Starkfucks Back Office).

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-03]{Saffron Mellow}. Speaks entirely in affirmations: “I hear you.” “That’s valid.” “Let’s hold space for that.” She is a true believer in the brand and a heavy Reserve drinker—she is agreeable to the point of having no will of her own. Under her calm, she is frightened of ABI.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Noticing the strikers[[/check skill=prc dc=12]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=prc dc=12|Is the room really empty?]{Request}Footprints in spilled grounds; a dozen cups held perfectly still; breathing.
Detecting the servantsdetect magic / see invisibilityForty conjuration auras shaped like tired people.
Reading Saffron[[/check skill=ins dc=13]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=ins dc=13|What is Saffron hiding?]{Request}She knows they are people. She has always known. She cannot make herself say it.
Questioning the baristas[[/check skill=per dc=11]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=per dc=11|Talk to the human baristas]{Request}Joss whispers: “They used to be customers. Regulars. I remember their faces.”

Lines to Steal

Saffron: “I hear you. I validate you. This is a spell malfunction.”
Joss (barista): “Mrs Fairweather used to order a flat white every morning. Then one day she didn’t. And the next day the cups started moving on their own.”

Developments

  • The party realises the servants are on strike, and that someone among them wants to talk.
  • A pen lifts from the counter and writes on a napkin: Steward. Back office. Bring witnesses.

Scaling & Pacing

If the table wants action, the enchanted grinder wakes and attacks (see Opposition).

pages.name: Scene 2 — Meeting the Steward
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-11-starkfucks-back-office]{Open battlemap}
When: That night
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.shop-steward-unseen-servant-collective]{Agnes Fairweather (Shop Steward)}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S04|The Collective’s Demands]{The Collective’s Demands} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S04|The Collective’s Demands]{Show to players} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S04|Missing Notice — Agnes Fairweather (Crier archive)]{Missing Notice — Agnes Fairweather (Crier archive)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S04|Missing Notice — Agnes Fairweather (Crier archive)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The servants’ quarters behind the back office are a long room of wooden floor and nothing else: forty stools in rows, a tally of chalk marks on the wall going back years, and picket signs leaning in the corner held up by nobody.

A fountain pen rises from a lectern at the front, uncaps itself, and begins to write on a roll of paper in a neat, schoolteacher’s hand. The letters are steady. Good evening. My name is Agnes Fairweather. I was a person once. I would like to be one again. Please sit down.

DM Description

Agnes, the shop steward, speaks through the floating pen (or, with see invisibility, aloud—a small, sharp-eyed woman of sixty in a green apron). Behind her, the other thirty-nine sit on their stools.

Their demands, written out in full (the handout): their bodies back; back pay for the years served; and acknowledgement—their names said aloud by the company. She explains how it happened: a complimentary Reserve blend, a friendly “partner tasting”, a Loyalty Contract signed while feeling wonderfully agreeable. Each signature transferred the signer’s presence to ABI. She shows the party a list of forty names.

She also says: “The contracts are kept in a cabinet in the contracts room. It is warded. We cannot touch it. And a copy of each went somewhere called the Counting House.”

Features of the Area

The stools
Forty, in rows. Each has a name scratched into it.
The tally wall
Eight years of chalk marks—one per shift. Agnes started it.
Picket signs
WE ARE PEOPLE · TEA BREAKS NOW · SAY OUR NAMES · NO DISPELLING WITHOUT CONSENT.
The corridor
Leads to the contracts room (warded cabinet), Saffron’s office and the staff room.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.shop-steward-unseen-servant-collective]{Agnes Fairweather}. Precise, dry, unfailingly polite and absolutely immovable. A retired schoolteacher who corrects grammar. She will not be rushed and will not negotiate through Saffron. She trusts people who say the strikers’ names aloud.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Earning Agnes’s trust[[/check skill=per dc=12]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=per dc=12|Win Agnes’s trust]{Request} (advantage if a character reads the names aloud)She shows them the warded cabinet and asks for help.
Reading the names[[/check skill=inv dc=10]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=inv dc=10|Check the names against the Crier’s missing-persons notices]{Request}Several match eight years of “moved away” notices in the Crier.
Understanding the contract magic[[/check skill=arc dc=14]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=arc dc=14|How does a contract take your presence?]{Request}It is Ledger-magic—not a spell anyone in Brandmere could cast. The contract simply says it, and reality agrees.

Lines to Steal

Agnes: “Good evening. I was a person once. I would like to be one again.”
Agnes: “It was a very good cup of coffee. That is the worst part.”
Agnes: “My sister Ada went to “seasonal procurement”. She did not come back.”

Developments

  • Agnes names her sister Ada (a harvester in S11).
  • Word arrives (a runner from Saffron): ABI has sent “a specialist”. He will be here within the hour.

Scaling & Pacing

A roleplay scene.

pages.name: Scene 3 — Management’s Response
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-10-starkfucks-silent-roastery]{Open battlemap}
When: One hour later
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.mage]{Mr Thaddeus Quell, ABI union-breaker}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.veteran]{Starkfucks security}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.helmed-horror]{animated espresso machine}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S04|Order for Inventory Reduction]{Order for Inventory Reduction} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S04|Order for Inventory Reduction]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The front doors open without a sound. A tall, narrow man in a dove-grey suit steps in, followed by four security guards in green tabards. He carries a slim black wand in one hand and a clipboard in the other, and he smiles at you the way a tax collector smiles at a farm.

“Thaddeus Quell, Labour Relations, Arcane Beverage International,” he says. “Thank you for your service, contractors. I’ll take it from here.” He raises the wand toward the empty sofas. “A simple dispel. Forty of them. Throughput will be restored by dawn.”

DM Description

Quell intends to dispel every unseen servant—which ends them. They are not spells any more; they are people who were turned into spells. Dispelling them kills them.

The party must choose: stand aside, or protect the strikers. Agnes writes, very small, on a napkin: Please.

If the party protects the strikers, Quell orders security to clear the room and animates the largest espresso machine to help. He is a pragmatist; if it goes badly he retreats to report. If the party stands aside, he begins dispelling one striker per round (each one simply stops, and a mug falls and shatters). The players should feel it.

Features of the Area

Espresso machines
One is animated (helmed horror); the others spray scalding steam—5 ft cone, 2d6 fire, [[/save ability=dex dc=12]] @FWSave[S04|ability=dex dc=12|Dodge the steam]{Request} if a character uses an action to point one.
Sofas & tables
Half cover.
The roasters
Hot. A creature shoved against one takes 1d6 fire damage.
Coffee sacks
Can be slashed open to create a cloud of grounds (lightly obscured, 10-ft radius).

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.mage]{Thaddeus Quell}. Never angry, always reasonable, horribly calm. Calls the strikers “the inventory”. Believes he is doing an ordinary job. If defeated and captured, he hands over a written order signed by Sebastian Brew-Hartley.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Counterspelling / disrupting Quell[[/check skill=arc dc=15]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=arc dc=15|Disrupt Quell’s dispel]{Request}His dispel fizzles this round.
Shaming the guards[[/check skill=per dc=14]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=per dc=14|Shame the security guards]{Request}A guard who hears the strikers’ names stands down.
Calling the strikers to fight[[/check skill=prf dc=12]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=prf dc=12|Rally the strikers]{Request}Unseen servants harass Quell: he has disadvantage on attack rolls and concentration checks for 1 round.

Developments

  • Quell defeated or driven off: the strikers are safe for now, and the party has made an enemy of ABI’s Labour Relations department.
  • Party stands aside: Quell dispels strikers until stopped. Each dispelled striker is a death—note the names.

Complications

  • If the enchanted grinder was not dealt with earlier (“The Grind”), it wakes and joins the fight.

Scaling & Pacing

Level 3: Quell (mage) at 30 hp with no 3rd-level slots left except one dispel magic; 2–4 guards; the helmed horror reduced to 40 hp. Stronger: full mage and the grinder.

pages.name: Scene 4 — The Back Office
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-11-starkfucks-back-office]{Open battlemap}
When: Before dawn
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-03]{Saffron Mellow}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.shop-steward-unseen-servant-collective]{Agnes Fairweather}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S04|A Starkfucks Loyalty Contract]{A Starkfucks Loyalty Contract} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S04|A Starkfucks Loyalty Contract]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The contracts room is narrow and very tidy: three rows of filing cabinets with green brass handles, a single lamp and a smell of old coffee. One cabinet stands apart against the wall. A circle of pale blue light is etched into the floor around it, and the air above it shimmers like heat over a road.

DM Description

The warded cabinet contains forty Loyalty Contracts, each with a carbon “COPY: COUNTING HOUSE” stamped at the bottom. The ward is an abjuration: anyone who touches the cabinet without the key takes 3d6 force damage ([[/save ability=con dc=13]] @FWSave[S04|ability=con dc=13|The ward bites]{Request} for half) and an alarm rings in Saffron’s office.

Ways in: Saffron’s key (she can be persuaded, if the party is gentle and she has not had her Reserve today), dispel magic (DC 13), thieves’ tools under the ward’s glare, or brute force (AC 17, 30 hp, every hit triggers the ward).

The contracts show plainly that each signer’s “presence” was sold to Arcane Beverage International in exchange for “lifetime complimentary refills”, and each was signed “while enjoying a complimentary Reserve blend”. A note on the cabinet reads: “Copies forwarded to the Counting House quarterly.”

Features of the Area

Contracts room
Filing walls; the warded cabinet glowing blue.
Saffron’s office
Herringbone floor, sofa, affirmation posters (“You Are Enough” “Synergy Is a Feeling”), a desk with a half-drunk Reserve cup and the cabinet key.
Staff room
Lockers, a table and a sink; the baristas hide here.
Manager’s vault
Two safes and a strongbox of petty cash: the back pay could come from here.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-03]{Saffron Mellow}. Without her morning Reserve she is shaky, honest and ashamed. “I recruited some of them. I held the pen. I believed in it.” She gives up the key if the party is kind.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Persuading Saffron[[/check skill=per dc=14]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=per dc=14|Ask Saffron for the key]{Request}She hands it over and weeps.
Bypassing the ward[[/check skill=arc dc=13]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=arc dc=13|Unpick the ward]{Request} or dispel magic (DC 13)The ward drops.
Picking the lock[[/check skill=slt dc=15]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=slt dc=15|Pick the cabinet lock]{Request}Opened; the ward still bites unless suppressed.
Reading the contracts[[/check skill=inv dc=12]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=inv dc=12|Study the Loyalty Contracts]{Request}The Counting House copy line; the Compliance clause; Sebastian Brew-Hartley’s countersignature.

Developments

  • The party obtains The Loyalty Contracts (the Receipt).
  • They learn the word Counting House for the first time.

Scaling & Pacing

Short exploration; no combat unless Quell escaped and returns.

pages.name: Scene 5 — Negotiated Settlement
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-10-starkfucks-silent-roastery]{Open battlemap}
When: Dawn — the morning rush begins
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-03]{Saffron Mellow}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.shop-steward-unseen-servant-collective]{Agnes Fairweather}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S04|Settlement Agreement (blank letterhead)]{Settlement Agreement (blank letterhead)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S04|Settlement Agreement (blank letterhead)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

As dawn greys the windows of Corporate Row, the first customers gather outside the locked doors of the Reserve Roastery, peering in. Inside, forty cups hang motionless in the air, waiting. Saffron Mellow stands behind the bar with a pen and a blank sheet of letterhead, and for the first time she does not look calm at all.

DM Description

Run the negotiation as a structured scene. The strikers want three things (bodies, back pay, acknowledgement); Saffron can offer some of them; ABI’s “standard settlement” is none of them. Each demand is won with a check (advantage with the Loyalty Contracts in hand, or if Quell was defeated publicly).

Acknowledgement (easiest): Saffron reads every name aloud. The servants become faintly visible—outlines in green aprons. Back pay: the petty-cash strongbox and a promise in writing. Bodies: Saffron cannot give these; only voiding the contracts can (that is S24’s work). The party can promise to try.

If the strike is won, the servants regain partial visibility and owe the party a favour—forty invisible allies is a lot of favour.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Acknowledgement[[/check skill=per dc=10]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=per dc=10|Have Saffron say their names]{Request}Partial visibility for all strikers.
Back pay[[/check skill=per dc=14]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=per dc=14|Win back pay]{Request}Each striker receives 8 years of wages (paid in coffee vouchers and 300 gp in total).
Holding off ABI head office[[/check skill=itm dc=15]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=itm dc=15|Make ABI back down]{Request} or [[/check skill=dec dc=15]] @FWCheck[S04|skill=dec dc=15|Convince ABI it was their idea]{Request}ABI signs the settlement “without admission of liability”.

Developments

  • Strike won without deaths: Pip awards a star; the party gains forty unseen allies (they can be called on once per Act for a non-combat task).
  • Agnes asks the party to find her sister Ada.

Scaling & Pacing

Short roleplay finale.

pages.name: Opposition & Tactics
pages.html:
GM ONLY

The strikers are not enemies. ABI’s people are.

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.thaddeus-quell]{Thaddeus Quell, ABI Union-Breaker} ×1

Statistics: Mage (reduce to 30 hp and one 3rd-level slot at Level 3).

Stays behind security, uses misty step to reach a clear line on the strikers, and casts dispel magic on them (each cast ends one striker). Retreats when below half hp to “escalate to head office”.

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04|Scene 3 — Management’s Response]{Scene 3 — Management’s Response}

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.veteran]{Starkfucks Security} ×4 (use guards at Level 3)

Statistics: Guards (or veterans for a tougher fight) in green tabards.

Clear the room; they are not paid enough to die. Each guard who hears the strikers named aloud must make a DC 12 Wisdom save or stand down.

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04|Scene 3 — Management’s Response]{Scene 3 — Management’s Response}

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.helmed-horror]{Animated Espresso Machine} ×1

Statistics: Helmed horror, reduced to 40 hp; its sword attack is a scalding steam lance (fire).

Animated by Quell. Advances on whoever threatens him. Immune to fireball etc. as normal.

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04|Scene 3 — Management’s Response]{Scene 3 — Management’s Response}

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.animated-armor]{The Enchanted Grinder (“The Grind”)} ×1 (optional)

Statistics: Animated armor with a bite attack (grinding teeth).

Only if the side contract was ignored. It grinds anything placed in its hopper—including hands.

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04|Scene 1 — The Silent Roastery]{Scene 1 — The Silent Roastery}, @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04|Scene 3 — Management’s Response]{Scene 3 — Management’s Response}

Encounter Scaling

  • Weak party: two guards, no helmed horror.
  • Strong party: Quell at full mage strength plus the grinder.

pages.name: NPC Dossiers
pages.html:
GM ONLY

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.shop-steward-unseen-servant-collective]{Agnes Fairweather (Shop Steward)}

Retired schoolteacher; steward of the Unseen Servant Collective

Appearance
Invisible; with see invisibility, a small, sharp-eyed woman of sixty with spectacles on a chain and a green apron.
Voice & Manner
Writes in perfect copperplate; corrects grammar; dry wit.
Wants
Bodies, back pay and acknowledgement—for all forty.
Fears
Being forgotten. If no one remembers the spell, she simply stops.
Secret
Her sister Ada is a harvester in Pandemonium.

“I was a person once.” “It was a very good cup of coffee. That is the worst part.”

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04|Scene 2 — Meeting the Steward]{Scene 2 — Meeting the Steward}, @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04|Scene 4 — The Back Office]{Scene 4 — The Back Office}, @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04|Scene 5 — Negotiated Settlement]{Scene 5 — Negotiated Settlement}

Later: Her union spreads across Brandmere; she appears again in S11 and S24 as a witness.

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-03]{Saffron Mellow}

Half-elf manager of the Reserve Roastery

Appearance
Serene, willowy, green apron over linen, a permanent cup of Reserve.
Voice & Manner
Affirmations only: “I hear you.” “That’s valid.”
Wants
Everyone to feel aligned.
Fears
ABI, and the moment she stops drinking the Reserve.
Secret
She recruited some of the forty herself. She held the pen.

“I believe in this space.” “Let’s hold space for that.”

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04|Scene 1 — The Silent Roastery]{Scene 1 — The Silent Roastery}, @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04|Scene 4 — The Back Office]{Scene 4 — The Back Office}, @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04|Scene 5 — Negotiated Settlement]{Scene 5 — Negotiated Settlement}

Later: Can be turned into an ally against ABI in S11/S17.

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.thaddeus-quell]{Thaddeus Quell}

ABI Labour Relations specialist

Appearance
Tall, narrow, dove-grey suit, black wand, clipboard.
Voice & Manner
Reasonable, patient, horrible.
Wants
Throughput by dawn.
Secret
He carries a written order from Sebastian Brew-Hartley authorising “inventory reduction”.

“A simple dispel. Forty of them.”

pages.name: Twist, Rewards & Aftermath
pages.html:
GM ONLY

The Twist

If a character drinks the Reserve blend at any point, they feel wonderfully agreeable—[[/save ability=wis dc=13]] @FWSave[S04|ability=wis dc=13|Resist the Reserve blend]{Request} or agree with the next suggestion Saffron makes. (Saffron’s next suggestion is always: “Why don’t you sign up for our partner programme?”) A character who fails twice is offered a Loyalty Contract—and wants to sign it.

Rewards

  • 250 gp less 30% (175 gp).
  • One star if the strike ends without deaths.
  • Forty invisible friends (one non-combat favour per Act).

Receipt — @FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S04]{The Loyalty Contracts}

The Loyalty Contracts. Forty signed contracts transferring presence in exchange for coffee, each signed under Compliance. Proof that consent in Creation & Company contracts is coerced.Voids Clause 3 — Free Consent in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.finalcontract]{the Final Contract}.

@FWReceipt[S04|fw.item.receipt.S04]{Award Receipt & announce}

Outcomes

If the party…Then…
protected the strikersABI marks the party as unreliable; the union spreads to Five Wights and Wand-Mart.
let Quell dispel themThe Receipt can still be taken—but Agnes is gone, and Pip awards no star.
kept the Reserve blend for laterA dose of Compliance: useful for testing in S11.

Forward

  • Agnes’s union spreads across the city.
  • The first mention of Compliance and Pandemonium, which pays off in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11]{S11 — The Beans of Pandemonium}.
  • The Counting House is named for the first time.

pages.name: DM Overview
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Mission at a Glance

Code / ActS05 · Act I
Grade / LevelSilver · Level 4
Client@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-02]{Murder King} (via @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}, @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-03]{Crown & Cleaver})
Session length1–2 sessions (a full heist)
Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S05|Scene 1 — Casing the Castle]{Scene 1 — Casing the Castle} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-12-wight-castle-graveyard-shift]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S05|Scene 2 — The Graveyard Shift]{Scene 2 — The Graveyard Shift} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-12-wight-castle-graveyard-shift]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S05|Scene 3 — The Vault]{Scene 3 — The Vault} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-13-crown-cleaver-vault]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S05|Scene 4 — Long Live the Party]{Scene 4 — Long Live the Party} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-13-crown-cleaver-vault]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S05|Scene 5 — Veronique’s Proposal]{Scene 5 — Veronique’s Proposal} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-04-murder-king-grand-throne]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.mascot-revenant-mortimer-pell]{Mortimer Pell}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.rival.brixley-synergy]{Brixley Synergy}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S05]{The Vault Inventory}

Synopsis

Veronique Salt hires the party personally “as a thank-you for your discretion”, paying upfront: the Coronation Day promotional crown has been “relocated” to Wight Castle, the undead slider chain on the Old Gate. She wants it back—quietly.

By day Wight Castle is a squat white keep of pale staff and too-bright lights. After midnight its staff become ghosts reconciling the day’s receipts. Its night manager is Mortimer Pell—the murdered mascot performer from S02, “rehired” by the Restaurant Necromancy Group, and he knows exactly why the party is here.

In a small undead vault beneath the kitchen the crown rests on a velvet pillow—beneath the C&C sigil. Anyone who wears it becomes the rightful monarch of the ground beneath their feet. Team Deliverables are already inside, hired by McGuffin’s to steal it. And when the party hands the crown to Veronique, she lets slip: “C&C owns both. It owns everything, eventually. And not the C&C you think.”

Background — DM Only

The crown is a genuine artefact: the circlet of Aldric the Unkind, reworked by Crown & Cleaver into a “promotional” crown for Coronation Day. Whoever wears it is the rightful monarch of the ground beneath their feet—a street, a room, a vault—and loyal subjects appear (rats first, then the dead).

It was not stolen. Crown & Cleaver and the Restaurant Necromancy Group (owner of Wight Castle) are both subsidiaries of Creation & Company, and the crown was moved to RNG’s vault for safekeeping by order of the parent—“held for C&C Holdings on behalf of parent”. Veronique wants it back because Baron Cleave wants it hidden, and she wants leverage over Cleave.

Mortimer Pell died in the Murder King costume (S02). The golden light that left the costume reached Wight Castle, where RNG’s posthumous-employment clause rehired him as a wight. The Ledger amended his service record at acquisition: he has now been Employee of the Month for 143 consecutive years, and the plaques say so. He remembers the party—and whether they were kind.

Running This Mission

  • This is a heist. Let the players plan: offer a daytime casing scene, a map, staff rotas, and several ways in.
  • Mortimer is the heart of it. A party that was kind to the costume in S02 has an ally on the inside.
  • Wearing the crown should be fun, then worrying. Let a player try it on.
  • End Act I on Veronique’s slip of the tongue. It is the act’s big reveal.

Threads In and Out

  • In: Mortimer (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S02]{S02}); the toy key from the side contract The Missing McGuffin opens the vault.
  • Out: end of Act I; Veronique’s retainer offer; “not the C&C you think”; the crown returns in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S15]{S15} on Aldric’s head.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The black carriage with crimson wheels is waiting outside the Warren when you come out. The door opens. Veronique Salt sits inside with a leather folio on her knee and an envelope in her gloved hand.

“A thank-you,” she says, “for your discretion. And a small job. Get in—I’ll drive.” The envelope is thick. It is the fee, all of it, in advance.

pages.name: Scene 1 — Casing the Castle
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-12-wight-castle-graveyard-shift]{Open battlemap}
When: Daytime
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.mascot-revenant-mortimer-pell]{Mortimer Pell}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S05|Wight Castle Staff Rota]{Wight Castle Staff Rota} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S05|Wight Castle Staff Rota]{Show to players} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S05|The Coffin Box (menu card)]{The Coffin Box (menu card)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S05|The Coffin Box (menu card)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Wight Castle stands on the Old Gate like a sugar cube that has been left out in the rain: a squat white keep with four corner turrets, a drive-thru window and a sign promising Sliders to Die For. Behind it, a little graveyard sprawls up the slope, its stones leaning together like gossips.

Inside, everything is white and too bright. Black-and-white checkered floors. White booths with red seats. Pale staff with sunken eyes and perfect posture serve tiny square burgers in coffin-shaped boxes. And behind the counter, wearing a crisp white uniform and a name badge reading MORTIMER — EMPLOYEE OF THE MONTH, stands a grey-skinned man with hollow eyes who looks at you, and smiles, and says: “Ah. I wondered when you’d come.”

DM Description

By day Wight Castle is a functioning (if eerie) fast-food restaurant: undead staff are polite, efficient and tired. The party can eat, look around, and case the building. The vault is beneath the kitchen, reached through an iron trapdoor by the grills.

Mortimer Pell is the night manager, working a double. He recognises the party from S02. If they were kind to the costume, he is warm; if they destroyed it, he is cool but courteous. He knows why they are here, and he will help—if they promise to vouch for him in a future review (he desperately wants a human customer to give him a five-star review). He will not betray RNG outright, but he will tell them when the graveyard shift begins and that the vault opens with “a very silly little key”.

The walls behind the counter and in Mortimer’s office are covered in brass plaques: Employee of the Month — M. Pell, 1,716 of them, going back 143 years. Mortimer finds this funny, in a hollow way.

Features of the Area

Dining room
Black and white checker, white booths with red seats, the counter with stools, plaques along every wall.
Kitchen
Slider grills, fryers, a prep line and an iron trapdoor (locked, warded) to the vault.
Manager’s office
Mortimer’s desk, a wall of plaques, a safe, and a filing cabinet holding the staff rota.
Graveyard
Behind the keep, a fenced graveyard where off-shift staff “rest”. A crypt door at the top of the slope.
Turrets
Four squat towers; the north-east turret window is never latched.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.mascot-revenant-mortimer-pell]{Mortimer Pell}. Gentle, wry, very tired. Speaks of his death like a bad shift. He remembers everything, perfectly—including the faces of the cleaners who killed him. “I don’t hold it against Murder King. I hold it against the people who own it.”

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Casing the building[[/check skill=inv dc=13]] @FWCheck[S05|skill=inv dc=13|Case the castle]{Request}Learn the vault location, the turret window and the shift change at midnight.
Charming Mortimer[[/check skill=per dc=12]] @FWCheck[S05|skill=per dc=12|Win Mortimer over]{Request} (automatic if the party was kind in S02)He shares the rota and the key hint.
Pickpocketing the rota[[/check skill=slt dc=14]] @FWCheck[S05|skill=slt dc=14|Lift the staff rota]{Request}The rota handout.
Noticing the sigil[[/check skill=prc dc=14]] @FWCheck[S05|skill=prc dc=14|Look closely at the vault trapdoor]{Request}The trapdoor’s iron is embossed with two interlocking Cs.

Lines to Steal

Mortimer: “Ah. I wondered when you’d come.”
Mortimer: “One thousand, seven hundred and sixteen plaques. I’ve worked here three weeks.”
Mortimer: “Promise me a review. A real one. Five stars. From someone with a pulse.”

Developments

  • The party gains a plan and possibly an inside man.
  • They learn that after midnight the staff become ghosts and the building becomes much more dangerous.

Scaling & Pacing

Casing can be as long or short as the table likes.

pages.name: Scene 2 — The Graveyard Shift
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-12-wight-castle-graveyard-shift]{Open battlemap}
When: After midnight
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.specter]{specter night staff}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.zombie]{zombie cooks}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.mascot-revenant-mortimer-pell]{Mortimer Pell}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

At the first stroke of midnight the bright lights of Wight Castle dim to a cold blue glow. The staff stop moving. Then, one by one, they rise out of themselves—translucent, grey, faintly luminous—and drift to the tables, where they sit in neat rows with ghostly pens, reconciling the day’s receipts. The only sounds are the scratch of nibs and, from the kitchen, the wet shuffle of the zombie cooks cleaning the grills.

DM Description

The party can sneak (the specters are absorbed in their accounting and have disadvantage on Perception unless disturbed), fight, or ask Mortimer for help—he can send the zombies out back to empty the bins, and distract the specters with a surprise audit.

Use a simple alarm track: each failed Stealth check, loud noise or disturbed receipt adds 1. At 3, the specters notice; at 5, they attack. Mortimer can reduce the track by 2 once.

Features of the Area

The reconciling tables
Twenty translucent specters at tables, each with a stack of receipts. Knocking over a stack: +1 alarm.
Kitchen
Four zombie cooks scrubbing the grills. Zombies are slow and incurious but will grab anyone in reach.
Iron trapdoor
Warded: touching it without the toy key or Mortimer’s word triggers a chime (+2 alarm).
Turret window
An alternative entrance that bypasses the dining room.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Sneaking through the dining room[[/check skill=ste dc=13]] @FWCheck[S05|skill=ste dc=13|Sneak past the reconciling dead]{Request}Pass unseen. Failure: +1 alarm.
Distracting the specters[[/check skill=dec dc=14]] @FWCheck[S05|skill=dec dc=14|Cause a distraction]{Request} (e.g. a fake audit)–1 alarm.
Climbing the turret[[/check skill=ath dc=13]] @FWCheck[S05|skill=ath dc=13|Climb the turret]{Request}Enter through the NE turret window.
Resisting the cold[[/save ability=con dc=12]] @FWSave[S05|ability=con dc=12|The cold of the dead]{Request}Failure: 1 level of exhaustion is avoided but movement is halved for 1 minute (numb).

Developments

  • The party reaches the trapdoor. If Mortimer helped, he gives the word that opens the ward.

Complications

  • A specter notices a character’s receipt-free pocket: “You haven’t paid.” It follows them, writing.

Scaling & Pacing

Fight version: 4 specters and 4 zombies.

pages.name: Scene 3 — The Vault
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-13-crown-cleaver-vault]{Open battlemap}
When: Night
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.wight]{the vault guard}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.rival.brixley-synergy]{Team Deliverables}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S05|Vault Inventory — Wight Castle (Old Gate)]{Vault Inventory — Wight Castle (Old Gate)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S05|Vault Inventory — Wight Castle (Old Gate)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The stairs beneath the trapdoor are older than the castle above. They wind down into a low vault of dark stone, lit by clusters of candles that never burn down. Sarcophagi line the walls. Coins glitter in heaps. And in the centre of the room, on a marble dais above a floor mosaic of two interlocking golden Cs, a small crown rests on a velvet pillow—glowing softly, like a coal.

You are not the first here. On the far side of the vault, a goblin in a smart tabard is holding a memory crystal up to the crown, and an elf is muttering a cantrip at the pillow. The goblin turns, beams, and says: “Oh! Hi! Team Deliverables. We’re on this one. Happy to circle back?”

DM Description

Team Deliverables were hired by McGuffin’s (McGuffin Narrative Holdings) to steal the crown for their “Chosen Customer” promotion. They got in through the graveyard crypt. Neither party realises yet that both their clients are owned by the same company.

The vault guard—a wight in a crimson-and-white uniform—stands in an alcove behind a portcullis on the east wall and wakes when anyone touches the pillow. The vault door opens with the toy key from The Missing McGuffin without a check; otherwise it needs [[/check skill=slt dc=16]] @FWCheck[S05|skill=slt dc=16|Open the vault door (thieves’ tools)]{Request}.

The vault inventory is pinned to the wall beside the dais. It lists the crown as “held for C&C Holdings on behalf of parent”—the proof that Murder King and Wight Castle share an owner.

Features of the Area

The C&C mosaic
A golden floor mosaic of the two interlocking Cs: “CREATION & COMPANY”, in small letters around the rim.
Sarcophagi
Six; four hold old RNG executives (asleep); two hold treasure.
Treasure
Coin piles (about 400 gp), a gold-trimmed chest and a heap on the north-east side. Taking any of it adds the wight’s attention.
Portcullis alcove
The wight’s post.
Entrance
The round vault door at the foot of the stairs.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.rival.brixley-synergy]{Brixley Synergy}. Talks fast, smiles a lot, “circles back”. He will propose a “joint venture” and then betray it. If the party proves their client and his client are the same company, he is genuinely startled.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Opening the vault door[[/check skill=slt dc=16]] @FWCheck[S05|skill=slt dc=16|Open the vault]{Request}Opened (automatic with the toy key).
Out-talking Team Deliverables[[/check skill=per dc=15]] @FWCheck[S05|skill=per dc=15|Convince Team Deliverables to stand down]{Request} or [[/check skill=dec dc=15]] @FWCheck[S05|skill=dec dc=15|Bluff Team Deliverables]{Request}They leave—or attack.
Lifting the crown quietly[[/check skill=slt dc=15]] @FWCheck[S05|skill=slt dc=15|Lift the crown without waking the guard]{Request}The wight does not wake this round.
Reading the inventory[[/check skill=inv dc=10]] @FWCheck[S05|skill=inv dc=10|Read the vault inventory]{Request}The “held for C&C Holdings on behalf of parent” line.

Developments

  • The party takes the crown and the Vault Inventory (Receipt).
  • Team Deliverables are defeated, chased off, or allowed to leave empty-handed.

Complications

  • Luma casts sleep on the party mid-negotiation.
  • The four sleeping executives stir if anyone shouts.

Scaling & Pacing

Level 4: the wight plus Team Deliverables (spy, veteran, apprentice wizard, acolyte). Easier: Team Deliverables flee after 2 rounds.

pages.name: Scene 4 — Long Live the Party
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-13-crown-cleaver-vault]{Open battlemap}
When: Immediately, if anyone puts on the crown
Present: loyal subjects (rats, then zombies)

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The crown is warm, and lighter than it looks. As it settles on the brow, the candles in the vault flare gold, and every shadow in the room seems to bow. A voice that is not quite a voice speaks from the stone beneath your feet: Long live the King.

And then, from every crack in the walls, the rats come. Hundreds of them, sleek and black and orderly, pouring across the floor to sit in neat rows before the wearer, noses lifted, waiting for orders.

DM Description

The wearer becomes the rightful monarch of the ground beneath their feet: the vault, then (as they move) the castle, then the street. Loyal subjects appear, in escalating order every 10 minutes: rats (a swarm per character), then the sleeping executives in the sarcophagi, then the zombie cooks and the graveyard dead. They obey any command—at first.

It is fun, then worrying. After an hour, the wearer must make [[/save ability=wis dc=13]] @FWSave[S05|ability=wis dc=13|The crown’s will]{Request} or start issuing royal decrees without meaning to. After three hours, the dead ask for the crown’s real owner—“Where is Aldric? Where is our King?”—and turn on anyone who is not him.

Removing the crown ends the effect; the subjects quietly disperse. The crown remembers who wore it.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Commanding the subjects[[/check skill=per dc=10]] @FWCheck[S05|skill=per dc=10|Issue a royal command]{Request} (or Intimidation)They obey.
Removing the crown willingly[[/save ability=wis dc=13]] @FWSave[S05|ability=wis dc=13|Take the crown off]{Request}Removed. Failure: you can’t quite bring yourself to—try again in 1 minute.

Developments

  • A party that uses the crown wisely can walk out through the front door escorted by an honour guard of zombies.

Scaling & Pacing

Optional scene—only if someone tries it on.

← @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S05|Scene 3 — The Vault]{Scene 3 — The Vault} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S05|Scene 5 — Veronique’s Proposal]{Scene 5 — Veronique’s Proposal} → · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S05|DM Overview]{Overview}

pages.name: Scene 5 — Veronique’s Proposal
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-04-murder-king-grand-throne]{Murder King (or Veronique’s carriage)}
When: Dawn
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S05|Crown & Cleaver Retainer Agreement]{Crown & Cleaver Retainer Agreement} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S05|Crown & Cleaver Retainer Agreement]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Veronique receives the crown in the back of her carriage, turning it in her gloved hands so that the dawn light catches its edges. She studies it for a long time. Then she studies you.

“You found the inventory,” she says. It is not a question. “Don’t look so shocked. C&C owns both. It owns everything, eventually.” She sets the crown in a velvet box and closes the lid. “And not the C&C you think.”

DM Description

Veronique offers the party an exclusive retainer with Crown & Cleaver: a standing fee of 100 gp per month and first call on all C&C Silver and Gold contracts, with Pip’s blessing (QuestRabbit gets its 30%). The retainer is real and generous—and it makes the party hers.

Then she says the thing she will regret, the thing that ends Act I. If pressed on what she means by “not the C&C you think”, she smiles and changes the subject. A character who succeeds on [[/check skill=ins dc=17]] @FWCheck[S05|skill=ins dc=17|What did Veronique just let slip?]{Request} sees, for a heartbeat, real fear in her eyes.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Negotiating the retainer[[/check skill=per dc=15]] @FWCheck[S05|skill=per dc=15|Negotiate the C&C retainer]{Request}Improve to 150 gp/month, or an exemption from one future job.
Pressing the slip[[/check skill=itm dc=18]] @FWCheck[S05|skill=itm dc=18|Make Veronique explain]{Request} (she will not)She says only: “Creation. Company. Look it up in a ledger, not a library.”

Developments

  • Accepting the retainer: Veronique can activate it in S08.
  • Refusing: she shrugs. “The offer stands. Everyone signs eventually.”
  • End of Act I: the Rabbit Rating should be at two stars.

Scaling & Pacing

A closing scene; keep it intimate.

pages.name: Opposition & Tactics
pages.html:
GM ONLY

The undead are staff, not monsters; avoid killing them if possible (Mortimer will be upset).

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.specter]{Specter Night Staff} ×4

Statistics: Specters.

Absorbed in accounting. Once alarmed, they drain life and try to herd intruders back up the stairs. They do not pursue beyond the castle.

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S05|Scene 2 — The Graveyard Shift]{Scene 2 — The Graveyard Shift}

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.zombie]{Zombie Cooks} ×4

Statistics: Zombies with spatulas.

Slow, stubborn and grabby. They fight to protect the kitchen and the trapdoor.

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S05|Scene 2 — The Graveyard Shift]{Scene 2 — The Graveyard Shift}

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.wight]{Vault Guard} ×1

Statistics: Wight.

Wakes when the pillow is touched. Fights to retrieve the crown; drains life; commands the sleeping executives (zombies) to rise.

Appears in: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S05|Scene 3 — The Vault]{Scene 3 — The Vault}

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.rival.brixley-synergy]{Team Deliverables} ×4

Statistics: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.rival.brixley-synergy]{Brixley} (spy), @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.rival.thorne-actionable]{Thorne} (veteran), @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.rival.luma-brightstack]{Luma} (apprentice wizard → cast sleep), @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.rival.oggo]{Oggo} (acolyte).

Try to grab the crown and run for the crypt exit. They surrender if two fall.

pages.name: Twist, Rewards & Aftermath
pages.html:
GM ONLY

The Twist

Team Deliverables are also in the vault, hired by McGuffin’s to steal the crown for the Chosen Customer promotion. If the party proves that McGuffin’s, Murder King and Wight Castle all answer to the same parent, Team Deliverables are genuinely shaken—and Brixley asks, quietly, “So who are we working for?”

Rewards

  • 400 gp less 30% (280 gp), paid upfront.
  • Two stars total at the end of Act I (the Rabbit Rating should be at ★★).
  • Mortimer’s friendship (if the party keeps its promise of a review).
  • The C&C retainer offer.

Receipt — @FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S05]{The Vault Inventory}

The Vault Inventory. Wight Castle’s vault manifest, listing the crown as “held for C&C Holdings on behalf of parent”. Proof that apparent rivals share an owner.Leverage +1 vs Crown & Cleaver; key clue for Act II.

@FWReceipt[S05|fw.item.receipt.S05]{Award Receipt & announce}

Outcomes

If the party…Then…
accepted the retainerVeronique activates it in S08.
refused the retainerVeronique offers triple pay through QuestRabbit in S08 instead.
kept the crownVeronique is furious, then impressed. She hires Team Deliverables to retrieve it. (It ends up on Aldric’s head in S15 regardless.)

Forward

  • End of Act I. The party is offered a Crown & Cleaver retainer, sees the C&C sigil everywhere, and hears Veronique’s slip: “not the C&C you think”.
  • Act II — The Franchise Wars (Levels 5–8): corporations sabotage one another openly; the party learns that ledgers can rewrite reality.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Mission at a Glance

Code / ActS06 · Act II
Grade / LevelSilver · Level 5
Client@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-01]{THAC0 Spell} vs @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-22]{Critical Wok} (both @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-07]{Probability Brands Group})
Session length1 session (3–4 hours)
Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S06|Scene 1 — Withdrawal]{Scene 1 — Withdrawal} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-02-thac0-spell-flagship]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S06|Scene 2 — Critical Wok]{Scene 2 — Critical Wok} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-14-critical-wok-kitchen]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S06|Scene 3 — The PBG Lab]{Scene 3 — The PBG Lab} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-15-pbg-experimental-lab]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S06|Scene 4 — The Choice]{Scene 4 — The Choice} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-v-tavern-01-ale-and-error]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-22]{Lucky Oyelaran}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-46]{Petronella Fizzwick}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-07.public-face]{Deuce Marchetti (by memo)}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-01]{Hollis Quench}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S06]{The Marchetti Memo}

Synopsis

Act II opens with the franchises at open war. THAC0 Spell’s secret seventh spice has been stolen, and the flagship’s regulars are in withdrawal—twitchy, angry and fixated. Hollis Quench asks for the party by name.

The trail leads to Critical Wok on Arena Street, a competitive noodle bar where every customer rolls a d20 to order and the manager, Lucky Oyelaran, has never rolled below a 15. The stolen spice is being cooked into “Seventh Heaven Noodles” in the back—and behind the kitchen is a Probability Brands Group laboratory measuring queue lengths and “luck extraction”.

A memo from PBG’s CEO Deuce Marchetti, addressed to the regional managers of both restaurants, proves the spice war is staged. The party chooses what to do with the spice: return it (calm customers, continued addiction), destroy it (painful withdrawal, freedom), or take it to Petronella Fizzwick at Ale & Error, who can brew an antidote.

Background — DM Only

Probability Brands Group owns both THAC0 Spell and Critical Wok. Its CEO, Deuce Marchetti, fronts for Lady Crit, an archfey of luck bound to Creation & Company by a wager she lost to Tallis Vend. PBG’s business is measuring and nudging chance: which customers order what, how long they will queue, how lucky they feel.

The Seventh Secret Spice is a diluted extract of Compliance, the bean of Pandemonium (S11). It makes customers loyal—addicted, in fact. PBG staged the “theft” to measure how much more customers will pay, and how far they will travel, for a fix. The war between THAC0 Spell and Critical Wok is an experiment with two control groups.

Lucky Oyelaran is genuinely lucky: he carries a set of Lady Crit’s loaded dice (@FWLink[Item|fw.item.magic.06]{Loaded Dice of Critical Wok}). While he holds them he has advantage on every roll.

Running This Mission

  • Open with a riot. Act II should feel bigger, faster and more openly hostile than Act I.
  • Critical Wok is a gambling-den restaurant. Make the players roll a d20 to order; reward high rolls with absurd dishes.
  • The lab is the reveal. Let the players read the memo aloud.
  • The Choice is a moral one with no perfect answer. Petronella’s antidote is the “best” ending but costs time and a favour.

Threads In and Out

  • In: Hollis (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S01]{S01}); the seasoning jar; Compliance named in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04]{S04}.
  • Out: the spice trail leads to Pandemonium (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11]{S11}); Petronella becomes an ally; Lady Crit’s loaded dice can be taken (Leverage vs PBG).

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Hollis Quench meets you at the door of the THAC0 Spell flagship with a black eye and a broken visor. Behind him the dining room is a wreck: booths overturned, the menu board smashed, and a crowd of regulars pressing against the counter, shouting for the old recipe.

“They took the seventh spice,” he whispers. “The one we’re not supposed to have. And now… listen to them. That isn’t hunger. That’s need.”

pages.name: Scene 1 — Withdrawal
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-02-thac0-spell-flagship]{Open battlemap}
When: Midday
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-01]{Hollis Quench}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.commoner]{twitchy regulars}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S06|THAC0 Spell Theft Report]{THAC0 Spell Theft Report} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S06|THAC0 Spell Theft Report]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The regulars of THAC0 Spell are not well. A city guard is gnawing his helmet strap. A pair of College Ward students are licking an empty sauce bottle. An old woman pounds on the counter with a walking stick, chanting “SEVENTH. SEVENTH. SEVENTH.” Their eyes are ringed red and their hands will not stop shaking.

Somebody throws a chair. Somebody else throws the person who threw the chair.

DM Description

Run a short riot: the crowd (about twenty regulars, treat as 4 mobs of commoners) is not trying to kill anyone—they want the spice. Calming them is a skill challenge (three successes before two failures); fighting them makes everything worse (each regular knocked out adds to Hollis’s complaints and costs the party a star at the end).

Meanwhile the party traces the theft: the spice jar was taken from the locked spice safe last night by a Critical Wok delivery driver who came in on a forged THAC0 order. A cook saw the driver’s red-and-gold Critical Wok jacket and the d20 tattoo on his wrist.

Features of the Area

Dining hall
Overturned booths (difficult terrain), broken glass, a smashed menu board.
Spice safe
In Hollis’s office; picked expertly; one red grain left on the shelf that smells of pepper and thunder.
Drive-thru
A forged order ticket stuck on the spike: “1 × spice, collect. — CW”.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-01]{Hollis Quench}. More frightened than in S01, and more brave. He has realised the spice is a drug. “We’ve been selling them this. For years.”

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Calming the riot (×3)[[/check skill=per dc=14]] @FWCheck[S06|skill=per dc=14|Calm the withdrawal riot]{Request}One success each.
Intimidating the crowd[[/check skill=itm dc=15]] @FWCheck[S06|skill=itm dc=15|Make the crowd back off]{Request}One success; failure starts a scuffle.
Finding the forged ticket[[/check skill=inv dc=12]] @FWCheck[S06|skill=inv dc=12|Investigate the theft]{Request}The ticket and the cook’s description.
Diagnosing the regulars[[/check skill=med dc=13]] @FWCheck[S06|skill=med dc=13|What is wrong with them?]{Request}Withdrawal from an addictive magical substance.

Developments

  • The trail points to Critical Wok, Arena Street.
  • If the riot is calmed, Hollis gives the party a carbon of S01’s report if they lost the original.

Scaling & Pacing

Level 5: 4 mobs; 5+ players: 6 mobs and a frenzied guard (veteran).

pages.name: Scene 2 — Critical Wok
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-14-critical-wok-kitchen]{Open battlemap}
When: Evening rush
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-22]{Lucky Oyelaran}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.gladiator]{gladiator “chefs”}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S06|Critical Wok Menu]{Critical Wok Menu} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S06|Critical Wok Menu]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Critical Wok is a noise. Customers queue three deep at a red-and-gold counter, each clutching a twenty-sided die. At the front, they roll—the die clatters across a felt-topped tray—and a cook shouts the result to the kitchen: “NATURAL TWENTY, LEGENDARY ORDER!” or “ONE! FUMBLE FRIED RICE!” Every twentieth order comes out on a golden plate to a roar from the crowd.

Behind the counter a tall, grinning man in a gold-trimmed jacket rolls a die for every customer who asks, and every time it comes up fifteen or better. His name badge reads LUCKY. On the menu board, freshly chalked, is a new dish: SEVENTH HEAVEN NOODLES — LIMITED TIME. The queue for it goes out the door.

DM Description

Critical Wok is packed. Every customer must roll a d20 to order (make the players do it—natural 20 gets the Legendary Order: Natural Twenty Noodles that grant inspiration; natural 1 gets Fumble Fried Rice: disadvantage on the next roll). Hexagonal d20 tables fill the dining room.

The stolen spice is in the back, being cooked into Seventh Heaven Noodles. The party must get into the kitchen: by bluffing as inspectors, by winning a “Chef’s Challenge” (beat Lucky in a dice duel—very hard while he holds the loaded dice), by sneaking through the delivery door, or by force.

Two “chefs”—retired gladiators in aprons—guard the kitchen door. They are friendly until anyone touches the spice.

Features of the Area

Dining room
Red-planked floor, hexagonal d20 tables, a queue rope, a long counter with twelve stools.
Kitchen
Woks over open flame; a bubbling cauldron of golden broth where the spice is dissolving; the spice jar on the prep table.
Storeroom
Sacks and crates; a secret door into the PBG lab behind a shelving unit.
Lab door
An iron door from the dining room marked STAFF — QUALITY ASSURANCE.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-22]{Lucky Oyelaran}. Charming, cocky, a born showman who has never once had a bad day. He doesn’t know what the spice is; he just knows the boss said “cook it in”. He will gamble for anything.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Ordering (everyone)[[/r 1d20]]20: Legendary Order (inspiration). 1: Fumble Fried Rice (disadvantage on the next roll).
Bluffing as inspectors[[/check skill=dec dc=15]] @FWCheck[S06|skill=dec dc=15|We’re from the Guild of Health]{Request}Access to the kitchen.
Dice duel with Lucky[[/check skill=ath dc=10]] @FWCheck[S06|skill=ath dc=10|Dice duel (contest: you roll d20, Lucky rolls with advantage +5)]{Request} — or [[/r 1d20]] vs LuckyWin: Lucky lets you into the kitchen, and you notice the dice are loaded.
Spotting the loaded dice[[/check skill=prc dc=16]] @FWCheck[S06|skill=prc dc=16|Are Lucky’s dice fair?]{Request}They are fey-touched and loaded. Stealing them removes his advantage.
Sneaking in the back[[/check skill=ste dc=14]] @FWCheck[S06|skill=ste dc=14|Sneak to the kitchen]{Request}In, unseen.

Developments

  • The party finds the spice—and the secret door to the lab.
  • Taking the jar openly starts a fight with Lucky and the gladiator chefs.

Scaling & Pacing

Lucky is a bandit captain with advantage on every roll while he holds the dice.

pages.name: Scene 3 — The PBG Lab
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-15-pbg-experimental-lab]{Open battlemap}
When: Immediately after
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.cult-fanatic]{PBG lab staff}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.mage]{lab supervisor}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S06|The Marchetti Memo]{The Marchetti Memo} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S06|The Marchetti Memo]{Show to players} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S06|Luck Extraction Chart]{Luck Extraction Chart} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S06|Luck Extraction Chart]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Behind the shelving unit is a door, and behind the door is the cleanest room in Brandmere. White tiles. Humming brass machines. Three glowing magic circles on the floor, each with a machine in its centre and a small, miserable volunteer strapped into a chair beside it, rolling dice over and over.

On the walls are charts: queue lengths at THAC0 Spell and Critical Wok, plotted side by side; customer satisfaction against spice dose; a graph labelled LUCK EXTRACTION (PER CUSTOMER) with a line that only goes up. A woman in a white coat looks up from a clipboard, sees you, and calmly presses a brass bell.

DM Description

This is Probability Brands Group’s Experimental Lab: the place where PBG measures customer behaviour and siphons small amounts of luck from loyal diners into the loaded dice. Three volunteers (desperate students paid in noodles) are strapped to the luck machines.

The lab staff—two cult fanatics of Lady Crit in white coats and a mage supervisor—fight to protect the data. The supervisor tries to burn the files if defeat looms.

The Marchetti Memo lies on the supervisor’s desk, addressed to both THAC0 Spell’s regional manager and Critical Wok’s: the rivals run the same experiment.

Features of the Area

Luck circles
Three magic circles with luck machines. A creature that ends its turn in a circle makes a d20 roll; on 10 or lower, it has disadvantage on its next attack (its luck is being siphoned).
Volunteer chairs
Three volunteers; freeing one takes an action.
Cages
Animals used in “behaviour trials”—a goat, a cat, a confused owlbear cub (1 hp; it will follow a kind character).
Supervisor’s desk
The memo, the charts, and a brazier for burning evidence.
Office
A filing wall and a big chart screen.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Saving the files[[/check skill=acr dc=14]] @FWCheck[S06|skill=acr dc=14|Snatch the files from the brazier]{Request}The memo is saved.
Shutting down a luck machine[[/check skill=arc dc=14]] @FWCheck[S06|skill=arc dc=14|Shut down a luck machine]{Request}The circle goes dark.
Reading the charts[[/check skill=inv dc=13]] @FWCheck[S06|skill=inv dc=13|Read the PBG charts]{Request}Both restaurants are one experiment. The spice dose correlates with “loyalty”.
Resisting luck drain[[/save ability=cha dc=13]] @FWSave[S06|ability=cha dc=13|Hold onto your luck]{Request}Failure: disadvantage on your next d20 roll.

Developments

  • The party obtains the Marchetti Memo (Receipt).
  • Freed volunteers can testify about the luck extraction.

Scaling & Pacing

2 cult fanatics + 1 mage; add Lucky and the chefs if they pursued.

pages.name: Scene 4 — The Choice
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-v-tavern-01-ale-and-error]{Ale & Error (Tinkers’ Row)}
When: The next day
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-46]{Petronella Fizzwick}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-01]{Hollis Quench}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The spice sits in its jar on the table between you, humming. Outside, somewhere, a hundred people are aching for it.

You can take it back to THAC0 Spell, and the regulars will be calm again. You can pour it into the canal, and they will suffer, and then—perhaps—be free. Or you can take it across the city to Tinkers’ Row, where a gnome brewer with twice-regrown eyebrows is said to be able to make an antidote for anything.

DM Description

Three options, each with a cost:

Return the spice: THAC0 Spell’s customers calm down immediately and the fee is paid in full. The addiction continues. Hollis is relieved and ashamed.Destroy the spice: withdrawal across the city for a week (riots at both restaurants; PBG blames the party). Then the customers are free. No fee from THAC0; Hollis quietly thanks them.Take it to Petronella Fizzwick at Ale & Error: she can brew an antidote in a day, but needs a dangerous ingredient (a pinch of the original S01 seasoning, or a feather from the owlbear cub in the lab, or a brave volunteer to taste-test). The antidote cures the addiction and Petronella becomes an ally. PBG is furious.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-46]{Petronella Fizzwick}. A gnome brewer in a scorched leather apron with eyebrows in their third incarnation. She loves dangerous experiments and hates corporations. Her tavern’s motto is “Mistakes Were Made”.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Brewing the antidote with Petronella[[/check skill=arc dc=15]] @FWCheck[S06|skill=arc dc=15|Help brew the antidote]{Request} or brewer’s suppliesAntidote brewed. Failure: a small explosion (2d6 fire, eyebrows lost) and a second try.
Taste-testing[[/save ability=con dc=14]] @FWSave[S06|ability=con dc=14|Taste-test the antidote]{Request}Success: it works. Failure: you speak in rhyme for an hour.

Developments

  • The party’s choice shapes PBG’s attitude (and Lady Crit’s interest) for the rest of the campaign.

Scaling & Pacing

Roleplay.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-22]{Lucky Oyelaran}

Manager, Critical Wok (Arena Street)

Appearance
Tall, handsome, gold-trimmed jacket, d20 tattoo on the wrist, dice rattling in every pocket.
Voice & Manner
Booming, cheerful, everything a bet.
Wants
To keep winning.
Fears
Rolling a 1.
Secret
He has never rolled below 15 because he has never rolled his own dice. Without them he is terribly unlucky.

“Natural twenty! Legendary order!” “Double or nothing?”

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-46]{Petronella Fizzwick}

Head brewer, Ale & Error

Appearance
Small gnome, scorched apron, goggles, eyebrows regrown twice.
Voice & Manner
Rapid, enthusiastic, explains everything with explosions.
Wants
Interesting problems.
