pages.html:
PLAYER SAFE

SilverExecutive Plot DeviceS07 · Level 5–6 · Client: Big McGuffin’s

BIG McGUFFIN’S SECURE LOGISTICS REQUEST

Transport one (1) briefcase from Midnight Plotline to the listed delivery address. Opening the briefcase constitutes a termination event. Contractor is advised that interested parties may express interest.

Contract gradeSilver (Level 5–6)
Pick-upThe Midnight Plotline, Big McGuffin’s
DeliveryAddress supplied on collection
Fee750 gp, less 30% (525 gp)
DeliverableOne briefcase, unopened
Small print“Interested parties” may include, without limitation: four.
A briefcase must cross the city. Every faction wants it. Inside is the Quill of Consideration—the pen that signs the Grand Ledger.

Show this page, or send it to chat, when Pip hands over the job slip. @FWChat[cover]{Send contract to chat}

pages.name: DM Overview
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Mission at a Glance

Code / ActS07 · Act II
Grade / LevelSilver · Level 5–6
Client@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-18]{Big McGuffin’s} (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-11]{McGuffin Narrative Holdings})
Session length1 session; a chase-heavy action night
Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S07|Scene 1 — Pick-Up]{Scene 1 — Pick-Up} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-v-food-11-big-mcguffins]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S07|Scene 2 — The Chase]{Scene 2 — The Chase} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-16-brandmere-city-chase]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S07|Scene 3 — The Temptation]{Scene 3 — The Temptation}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S07|Scene 4 — The Delivery]{Scene 4 — The Delivery} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-03-thac0-cellar]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-18]{Maxim Knell}, The Hand in the Grey Sleeve, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.rival.brixley-synergy]{Team Deliverables}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S07]{Delivery Receipt}

Synopsis

At the Midnight Plotline—the flagship of Big McGuffin’s, where the jukebox plays ominous strings—manager Maxim Knell hands the party a locked black briefcase and a delivery address, murmuring, “And so the heroes take the burden…” Three other parties watch the handover.

What follows is a city-wide chase: Crown & Cleaver cleaners on the rooftops, Planar Hospitality Group invisible stalkers in the alleys, a Hoard Syndicate kobold ambush in the sewers, and Team Deliverables in a hired carriage. The briefcase whispers. Inside is a golden quill that can write one line in any document—and make it true.

The delivery address is THAC0 Spell’s cellar. The iron door is ajar. A hand in a grey sleeve reaches out, takes the case, and closes the door. A receipt prints itself: Received: Consideration. From: Representatives of the Commons.

Background — DM Only

The briefcase holds the @FWLink[Item|fw.item.magic.02]{Quill of Consideration}—the original pen with which entries are made in the Grand Ledger. It has been “on loan” to McGuffin Narrative Holdings, whose director Deus Maxwell (a fallen deva who sells prophecies) used it to write destinies for promotional toys. Tallis Vend has recalled it: it is needed in the Counting House for the Final Contract.

Every faction on the Board wants the quill for itself, and each has sent agents: Crown & Cleaver (Baron Cleave wants leverage over Vend), the Planar Hospitality Group (Zafirah wants to control the supply chain), the Hoard Syndicate (Auntie Vermillia wants it for her hoard) and GigGoblin’s Team Deliverables (they just want the credit).

Why the party? Because the Counting House’s own paperwork insists the quill be delivered by “Representatives of the Commons”—Clause 77-B. The party doesn’t know it yet, but they are the only people who can legally carry it. The receipt they are given has their names on it.

Running This Mission

  • This is an action film. Keep it moving. Use the chase rules (DMG) with complications every round.
  • The briefcase whispers to whoever holds it. Make the temptation real.
  • If anyone opens the case and uses the quill, write down exactly what they wrote. It is permanently true.
  • End on the hand in the grey sleeve. Let it be the most unsettling moment of Act II.

Threads In and Out

  • In: the THAC0 cellar iron door (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S01]{S01}).
  • Out: the Quill returns in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S24]{S24}; the receipt names “Representatives of the Commons”—the same phrase as Clause 77-B.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Midnight Plotline is the most dramatic fast-food restaurant you have ever seen. Low blue lights, booths like confessionals, a jukebox in the corner playing something with too many violins. Behind the counter, a tiefling in an immaculate black uniform is narrating his own actions under his breath: “…he turns, slowly, to face the heroes…”

He turns, slowly, to face you. On the counter in front of him sits a black leather briefcase. “And so,” Maxim Knell says, “the heroes take the burden.”

pages.name: Scene 1 — Pick-Up
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-v-food-11-big-mcguffins]{Big McGuffin’s — The Midnight Plotline}
When: Midnight
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-18]{Maxim Knell}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.rival.brixley-synergy]{Team Deliverables}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.thug]{C&C cleaners}, a PHG “guest”, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.kobold]{a Hoard kobold}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S07|Big McGuffin’s Delivery Slip]{Big McGuffin’s Delivery Slip} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S07|Big McGuffin’s Delivery Slip]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The case is heavier than it looks, cold to the touch, and locked with a clasp shaped like an open book. As your hand closes on the handle, the jukebox changes song by itself—something urgent, all drums.

You become aware of three other tables. A trio in crimson-trimmed grey uniforms by the window, not eating. A woman in a turban of flame-coloured silk who has ordered nothing and whose chair has no shadow. And, in the corner booth, four familiar faces in matching tabards, waving. A goblin mouths: circle back? Under a table near the door, something small and scaly licks its lips.

DM Description

Maxim gives the party a delivery slip with an address: THAC0 Spell, Drive-Thru Row — Cellar, Door 2. He narrates their departure. The other parties will follow them out.

The party can try to identify the watchers before they leave: the C&C cleaners (Crown & Cleaver), the turbaned woman (an efreeti’s agent of the Planar Hospitality Group, with two invisible stalkers on retainer), the kobold scout (Hoard Syndicate), and Team Deliverables.

Clever parties may try decoys, back doors, disguises or simply ordering dessert and waiting. Reward cunning with a head start in the chase.

Features of the Area

Booths
Confessional-style booths with curtains—good for hiding or ambushes.
Jukebox
Plays music that fits the moment. It is McGuffin Narrative Holdings’ property and slightly prophetic.
Mystery display
A row of glowing pedestals holding “@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-16.happy-quest]{Happy Quest}” toys, each with a tiny destiny tag.
Back office
Maxim’s narrative charts on the walls: story arcs plotted like sales figures.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-18]{Maxim Knell}. Narrates everything under his breath, in the third person, in a gravelly trailer voice. He knows the case’s contents are important but not what they are. He is rooting for the party—“every story needs heroes”.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Identifying the watchers[[/check skill=prc dc=14]] @FWCheck[S07|skill=prc dc=14|Who is watching the handover?]{Request}Identify the factions (one per 5 points over 10).
Slipping out unseen[[/check skill=ste dc=15]] @FWCheck[S07|skill=ste dc=15|Slip out the back]{Request}A two-round head start in the chase.
Questioning Maxim[[/check skill=per dc=12]] @FWCheck[S07|skill=per dc=12|What’s in the case, Maxim?]{Request}“…he does not know, and he is glad…” He mentions the client is “very old money”.
Examining the case[[/check skill=arc dc=15]] @FWCheck[S07|skill=arc dc=15|Examine the briefcase]{Request}Powerful old magic; it is warded to alert someone if opened.

Developments

  • The chase begins as soon as the party leaves.

Scaling & Pacing

pages.name: Scene 2 — The Chase
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-16-brandmere-city-chase]{Open battlemap}
When: Through the night
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.thug]{C&C cleaners}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.invisible-stalker]{PHG invisible stalkers}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.kobold]{Hoard kobolds}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.rival.brixley-synergy]{Team Deliverables}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Brandmere at night is a maze: rooftops of slate and tile, alleys that narrow to nothing, a carriage road roaring with late traffic, and beneath it all, the sewers. Behind you, a door bangs. Above you, boots scrape on slate. Somewhere, an invisible something brushes past your shoulder. And from the carriage road comes the crack of a whip and a cheerful voice shouting, “On your left!”

DM Description

Run a chase (DMG chase rules) from the Midnight Plotline to Drive-Thru Row, about a mile. Four waves of pursuit hit the party in turn; the order is up to you but suggested:

1. Rooftops — Crown & Cleaver cleaners (4 thugs) try to tackle the case-carrier off the roof. 2. Alleys — PHG invisible stalkers (2, weakened) snatch at the case; their handler offers to buy it for “a room on any plane, forever”. 3. Sewers — Hoard kobolds (6) spring an ambush with nets and a guard drake. 4. Carriage road — Team Deliverables in a hired carriage try to swipe the case with a hook.

Each round, roll on the chase complications table, and have each pursuer roll to close the distance. The party can fight, flee, hide, trade, or set pursuers against one another (C&C and the Hoard hate each other).

Features of the Area

Rooftops
Gaps of 5–10 feet (Athletics DC 12 to jump); slippery slate; chimneys for cover.
Alleys
Dumpsters, washing lines, dead ends.
Sewers
Brick tunnels, a murky channel, an iron trapdoor up to the street.
Carriage road
Fast-moving carriages; jumping onto one requires Acrobatics DC 14.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Leaping roof gaps[[/check skill=ath dc=12]] @FWCheck[S07|skill=ath dc=12|Leap the gap]{Request}Across. Failure: fall 20 ft (2d6) into the alley.
Losing pursuers in the alleys[[/check skill=ste dc=14]] @FWCheck[S07|skill=ste dc=14|Lose them in the alleys]{Request}One pursuer loses track.
Spotting invisible stalkers[[/check skill=prc dc=16]] @FWCheck[S07|skill=prc dc=16|Something invisible is here]{Request}You can target it without disadvantage this round.
Avoiding the kobold nets[[/save ability=dex dc=13]] @FWSave[S07|ability=dex dc=13|Dodge the nets]{Request}Failure: restrained (escape DC 12).
Boarding a carriage[[/check skill=acr dc=14]] @FWCheck[S07|skill=acr dc=14|Jump onto the carriage]{Request}Aboard.

Chase Complications ([[/r 1d10]])

  • 1. A washing line catches you: Dexterity DC 12 or fall prone.
  • 2. A crowd leaving a tavern blocks the alley: difficult terrain for 10 ft.
  • 3. A Murder King delivery boat in the canal—jump on (Acrobatics DC 13) for a free 30 ft.
  • 4. Rotten slates: Dexterity DC 12 or fall through into an attic.
  • 5. A Lord Mayor’s parade: Persuasion DC 13 to get through.
  • 6. A cat. It is fine.
  • 7. A rival pursuer runs into another pursuer; both lose a round.
  • 8. A guard patrol demands to see papers.
  • 9. The case whispers: Wisdom DC 13 or stop and listen.
  • 10. A shortcut! Gain a round.

Developments

  • The party arrives at THAC0 Spell with or without the case. If the case was lost, they can recover it from the faction that took it (that faction’s Leverage goes up—and the quill’s eventual delivery happens anyway, a day late).

Complications

  • If the case is opened (Scene 3), a Compliance Officer appears at the end of the next round and joins the chase.

Scaling & Pacing

Level 5: as written. Level 6 or strong party: run waves 2 and 3 together.

pages.name: Scene 3 — The Temptation
pages.html:
GM ONLY

When: At any point during the chase
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.compliance-officer]{a Compliance Officer (if opened)}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S07|The Quill’s Whisper]{The Quill’s Whisper} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S07|The Quill’s Whisper]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The case is whispering. It has been whispering since you picked it up, too softly to hear—but now, in a quiet moment, you hear it clearly. A voice like a pen nib on good paper: Write something. Anything. It will be true.

The clasp, shaped like an open book, has come undone by itself.

DM Description

Inside, on a bed of grey velvet, lies a long golden quill with a nib of black iron. Anyone who touches it knows what it is: the Quill of Consideration. It can write one line in any document, and that line becomes binding—truly, permanently. (It has one line of ink left for a mortal hand; then it must return to its owner.)

Opening the case triggers the Counting House’s alarm: a Compliance Officer arrives at the end of the next round, walking calmly out of the nearest shadow. It wants the case closed and delivered. It does not hurry. It does not stop.

If a character writes a line, record it exactly. It should be meaningful and limited: “The Rabbit Rating shall not exceed four stars”, “Agnes Fairweather is a person”, “The party may not be compelled to sign”. You decide how literally the Ledger interprets it. It counts in S24.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Resisting the whisper[[/save ability=wis dc=14]] @FWSave[S07|ability=wis dc=14|Resist the Quill’s whisper]{Request}You can keep the case closed. Failure: you open it.
Understanding the quill[[/check skill=arc dc=16]] @FWCheck[S07|skill=arc dc=16|What is the Quill of Consideration?]{Request}The pen that signs the Grand Ledger. It is not meant to be here.

Developments

  • Opened and used: the line is permanent. Opened and not used: the Compliance Officer still comes.
  • Closed: no alarm.

Scaling & Pacing

A single Compliance Officer is CR 7—dangerous at level 5. Encourage the party to close the case and run.

pages.name: Scene 4 — The Delivery
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a1-03-thac0-cellar]{Open battlemap}
When: Before dawn
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-01]{Hollis Quench}, a hand in a grey sleeve
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S07|Delivery Receipt (Franchise Below)]{Delivery Receipt (Franchise Below)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S07|Delivery Receipt (Franchise Below)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Hollis lets you in through the back without a word and leads you down to the cellar. He is shaking. The iron door in the old alcove—the door that would not open for anyone—stands ajar, a single finger’s width, and through the gap you can hear a till ringing, steady as a heartbeat.

As you approach, a hand emerges from the gap: long, pale, in a grey sleeve, with ink-stained fingers. It waits, palm up. When the case is placed in it, the hand closes, withdraws, and the door swings shut with a soft, final click.

From somewhere—from nowhere—a slip of paper flutters down and lands at your feet.

DM Description

The delivery is complete. The receipt reads: Received: Consideration. From: Representatives of the Commons. Beneath, in neat clerical script, are the party’s full names.

Hollis reads it over their shoulders and goes white. “That’s what the clause says. In my contract. And yours.” If the party has the S01 report, the connection to Clause 77-B is now obvious.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Following the hand—Impossible; the door is shut again.
Studying the receipt[[/check skill=inv dc=13]] @FWCheck[S07|skill=inv dc=13|Study the delivery receipt]{Request}The paper is the same grey stock as the courier’s book (S01) and the Loyalty Contracts’ copies (S04).

Developments

  • The party has the Delivery Receipt (key clue).
  • Pip pays and adds a star.

Scaling & Pacing

A quiet, eerie finale.

Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S08|Scene 1 — The List]{Scene 1 — The List} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-18-old-independents-quarter]{map}

@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S08|Scene 4 — The Choice]{Scene 4 — The Choice} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-17-tallow-lane-tankard]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S08|Scene 5 — The Siege of Tallow Lane]{Scene 5 — The Siege of Tallow Lane} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-17b-tallow-lane-siege]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-13.public-face]{Marda Hobb}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-43]{Centurion Marcus Crustus}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.hettie-gourd]{Hettie Gourd}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S08]{The Unsigned Deeds}

Synopsis

Veronique Salt activates the party’s Crown & Cleaver retainer (or offers triple pay through QuestRabbit): fourteen independent taverns in the Old Independents’ Quarter must sign franchise agreements. Three already have—and they no longer exist. Where they stood are Murder Kings, and nobody remembers they were ever anything else.

The party works the Quarter as a sandbox, tavern by tavern: charm, threat, bribery or conscience. Then Marda Hobb, sixty years behind the bar of the Tankard & Tallow, invites them in. She has no contract to offer—only a handshake and the truth about what signing does.

The party can sign the taverns, refuse, or sabotage the paperwork. If they side with Marda, Veronique retaliates: Little Caesars Legion marches on Tallow Lane, and the Siege of Tallow Lane begins.

Background — DM Only

A Creation & Company franchise agreement is a Ledger instrument. When a business signs, it is not merely bought—it is rewritten: its history, name and memory are replaced by the brand. That is why signed taverns vanish and nobody remembers them. Their old owners wander the streets, unable to recall where they live.

The Last Independents are the businesses that have never signed anything they did not write themselves. Their handshake agreements are invisible to the Ledger; it cannot see, count or acquire them. Marda Hobb keeps the original deeds of every tavern that refused, and her network of handshakes is the beginning of the Commons Tally.

Veronique does not actually want to win. She wants to see what the party does. If they defy her, she quietly marks them as a possible ally against Baron Cleave (and later offers them “@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.CO-03.succession-planning]{Succession Planning}”).

Running This Mission

  • Prepare a few taverns in detail (below) and improvise the rest; each should be a two-minute scene with a proprietor, a history and a reason to refuse.
  • The vanished tavern is the horror beat. Play it straight.
  • Marda Hobb is one of the campaign’s moral anchors. Give her time.
  • QuestRabbit counts completion, not outcome: the party gets a star either way. Point this out; it matters later.

Threads In and Out

  • In: the C&C retainer (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S05]{S05}); Deacon Hobb at Saving Throw Subs is Marda’s cousin.
  • Out: the Last Independents become the resistance; the Commons Tally begins; the Tankard & Tallow is the war room in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S21]{S21}.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Veronique’s note arrives folded inside a Murder King crown: Fourteen taverns in the Old Independents’ Quarter. I need their signatures by the end of the week. You are on retainer, darling—or, if you prefer, I have arranged triple pay through your rabbit. — V.

Pip reads it over your shoulder and his ears droop. “The Old Quarter,” he says. “My nan used to take me to the Tankard & Tallow. Are they… are they all signing?”

pages.name: Scene 1 — The List
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-18-old-independents-quarter]{Open battlemap}
When: Over several days
Present: fourteen proprietors
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S08|The List — Fourteen Taverns]{The List — Fourteen Taverns} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S08|The List — Fourteen Taverns]{Show to players} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S08|C&C Franchise Agreement (Clause 9)]{C&C Franchise Agreement (Clause 9)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S08|C&C Franchise Agreement (Clause 9)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Old Independents’ Quarter is the oldest corner of Brandmere: crooked streets, overhanging upper storeys, cobbles worn into hollows by centuries of boots. Every other doorway is a tavern, and every tavern has a sign hand-painted by someone who meant it—a goat with a limp, three ravens, a bent spoon, a lantern burning low.

Here there are no purple-and-orange awnings, no golden tusks, no drive-thru moats. Only smoke from chimneys, the smell of stew and old beer, and people who look up when you pass and do not smile.

DM Description

The party has a list of fourteen taverns (the handout). Run it as a sandbox; each visit is a short scene of charm, threat or bribery. Track signatures. Detailed examples:

The Hobbled Goat — Old Nan Pertwee, ninety, deaf in one ear; refuses because her late husband built the bar. Will sign if told it will “keep the place in the family” (it won’t).The Three Ravens — Corvin and Wyn, married innkeepers; debt-ridden. Would sign for the money; terrified to. A bribe works—or paying their debt.The Bent Spoon — Silas Crook, ex-mercenary; will fight anyone who asks him to sign.The Old Copper Kettle — run by three gnome sisters who want to see the small print. Reading it aloud makes them throw the party out.The Salted Oar — a sailors’ bar; proprietor Ma Dree trades only in handshakes.The Last Lantern — a temple-tavern; the priest says the Lantern has burned for 300 years and will not be franchised.

The other eight: Widow’s Cask, the Rusty Hook, Mother Owl, the Leaning Post, Bramble & Barrel, the Quiet Fox, the Dancing Dwarf, the Gilded Gourd. Three of the fourteen—the Gilded Gourd, Widow’s Cask and the Quiet Fox—have already signed.

Features of the Area

Tallow Lane
The Quarter’s heart, with the Tankard & Tallow at the top.
The fountain square
Market stalls, a well, gossip.
Former taverns
Three new Murder Kings, smelling of fresh paint, with drive-thru windows cut into ancient walls.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Persuading a proprietor[[/check skill=per dc=15]] @FWCheck[S08|skill=per dc=15|Persuade a proprietor to sign]{Request}They sign. (Note it; they will vanish.)
Threatening a proprietor[[/check skill=itm dc=14]] @FWCheck[S08|skill=itm dc=14|Lean on a proprietor]{Request}They sign in fear—and tell Marda.
Bribing(gold)Some will sign for 100–500 gp of debt relief.
Reading the agreement properly[[/check skill=inv dc=16]] @FWCheck[S08|skill=inv dc=16|Read the franchise agreement]{Request}Clause 9: “Upon execution the Business shall be the Brand, and shall have always been the Brand.”

Developments

  • Each signing is recorded; each refusal brings the party closer to Marda.
  • By the third visit, rumours reach the Tankard & Tallow.

Scaling & Pacing

Run as many or as few taverns as the table enjoys; summarise the rest.

pages.name: Scene 2 — The Vanished
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-18-old-independents-quarter]{Open battlemap}
When: During the sandbox
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.hettie-gourd]{Hettie Gourd, former owner of the Gilded Gourd}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Gilded Gourd is on the list as “signed”. When you reach its address, you find a Murder King: red roof, gold trim, a drive-thru window cut through a wall of stone four centuries old. Inside, everything is new and bright and smells of paint. The staff have never heard of the Gilded Gourd. Nobody has.

Out back, beside the bins, lies a wooden sign: a fat golden gourd, hand-painted, split down the middle. And on the corner, an elderly woman in a good coat is stopping strangers, one after another, asking the same question in a reasonable, frightened voice: “Excuse me. I’m so sorry. Do you know where I live?”

DM Description

Hettie Gourd ran the Gilded Gourd for forty years. She signed last week. The Ledger rewrote her tavern into a Murder King and, with it, her home above the bar—and her place in the world. She cannot remember where she lives, because she no longer lives anywhere.

The party can help her: the old sign triggers a flicker of memory; Marda Hobb knows her; Deacon Hobb (Marda’s cousin, who sold his tavern and regrets it) can take her in. A remove curse or greater restoration restores her memories but not her tavern.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Comforting Hettie[[/check skill=per dc=12]] @FWCheck[S08|skill=per dc=12|Comfort Hettie Gourd]{Request}She calms and follows you.
Restoring a memory with the sign[[/check skill=ins dc=13]] @FWCheck[S08|skill=ins dc=13|Show Hettie her sign]{Request}She remembers her name, and Marda’s.
Investigating the Murder King[[/check skill=his dc=15]] @FWCheck[S08|skill=his dc=15|Is anything left of the old tavern?]{Request}One wall still has the original carved lintel: “The Gilded Gourd — est. by hand”.

Developments

  • The party learns what signing really does.

Scaling & Pacing

A short, haunting scene.

pages.name: Scene 3 — Marda Hobb
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-17-tallow-lane-tankard]{Open battlemap}
When: Evening
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-13.public-face]{Marda Hobb}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.gideon-tumble]{Gideon Tumble (if he lived)}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S08|The Last Independents (Marda’s note)]{The Last Independents (Marda’s note)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S08|The Last Independents (Marda’s note)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Tankard & Tallow is everything a tavern should be: low beams black with smoke, a fire that has never been allowed to go out, long tables polished by elbows, and a bar of oak as thick as a castle door. Behind it stands a dwarf with iron-grey braids and forearms like ship’s timbers, drying a tankard with slow, deliberate care.

“So you’re Veronique’s contractors,” she says, without looking up. “Sit. Eat. I’m Marda. I’ve been behind this bar sixty years, and I’ve never signed a contract I didn’t write myself.” She sets down the tankard and finally looks at you. “I won’t sign yours. But I’ll tell you what it does.”

DM Description

Marda explains plainly: signing means the tavern becomes the brand and always was; the Ledger takes the history, the name, the memory. Her handshake agreements are invisible to it. She shows the party the original deeds of every tavern that ever refused—kept in a strongbox behind the bar—and Hettie Gourd’s, too late.

She has no contract to offer. Only a handshake. If a character shakes it honestly, they join the Last Independents’ network—the Commons Tally begins.

Features of the Area

The bar
Oak, ancient, with the deed box beneath.
The hearth
A fire burning for 300 years.
The back room
Marda’s private snug with a round table—where the Last Independents meet.
The cellar
Kegs and a trapdoor to old smugglers’ tunnels (useful in S21).

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-13.public-face]{Marda Hobb}. Plain-spoken, slow to anger, impossible to rush. She does not threaten; she does not plead. She simply explains, pours another drink, and waits. Her handshake is a bargain: she will do what she says, and expects the same.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Earning Marda’s trust[[/check skill=ins dc=12]] @FWCheck[S08|skill=ins dc=12|Understand what Marda is offering]{Request}She shows the deeds.
Shaking on it—No roll. A handshake is a choice.

Lines to Steal

Marda: “A contract tells you what you’ve lost. A handshake tells you what you’ve got.”
Marda: “I won’t sign yours. But I’ll tell you what it does.”

Developments

  • The party can join the Commons Tally.
  • Gideon Tumble is sheltering here if he survived S02.

Scaling & Pacing

Roleplay.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The deadline arrives with a crimson-wheeled carriage at the top of Tallow Lane. A courier in grey steps down and asks, pleasantly, for the signed agreements.

DM Description

The party chooses: sign the taverns (they vanish; full fee; the Quarter hates the party), refuse (no fee; Marda’s table), or sabotage the paperwork (forge signatures in invisible ink, write the deeds in Marda’s favour, swap the agreements for copies of the menu). Each unsigned deed kept safe counts toward the Receipt.

Veronique does not protest. She sends a second message by courier: “Disappointing. Expect a delivery.” Little Caesars Legion marches by nightfall.

pages.name: Scene 5 — The Siege of Tallow Lane
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-17b-tallow-lane-siege]{Open battlemap}
When: Nightfall
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-43]{Centurion Marcus Crustus}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.veteran]{Legion legionnaires}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-13.public-face]{Marda Hobb}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt (if openly defied)}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S08|Legion Delivery Order]{Legion Delivery Order} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S08|Legion Delivery Order]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

They come at dusk, in step: forty boots on old cobbles, a drum beating time, torches and red cloaks and great square shields painted with a pizza slice. At their head marches a man with a plume on his helmet and a pizza peel slung across his back like a sword. He raises a gauntleted fist, and the Legion halts at the bottom of Tallow Lane.

“By order of Crown & Cleaver,” Centurion Marcus Crustus bellows, “this Quarter is to receive a delivery. Clear the road!”

Behind you, the Quarter answers. Barricades of kegs and carts go up. Old Nan Pertwee hands out frying pans. Silas Crook straps on a sword he has not used in twenty years. And Marda Hobb rolls up her sleeves.

DM Description

A street battle. The Legion (8 legionnaires and a centurion) advances in formation up Tallow Lane toward the Tankard & Tallow. The Quarter’s defenders hold barricades; the party leads.

Objectives: hold the barricades for 6 rounds, break the Legion’s formation, or defeat the centurion. Kegs can be rolled down the hill; fires can be set (and must be controlled—the Quarter is old timber). If the party is openly defiant, Veronique arrives in round 4 to watch from her carriage. She does not fight unless attacked. If the Legion is beaten, she applauds.

Features of the Area

Barricades
Kegs, crates and carts: half cover; 20 hp per 5-ft section.
Rolling kegs
An action to roll a keg downhill: each creature in a 5-ft line makes [[/save ability=dex dc=13]] @FWSave[S08|ability=dex dc=13|Dodge the rolling keg]{Request} or takes 2d6 bludgeoning and falls prone.
Fires
Braziers and torches. Spreading fire: each round roll [[/r 1d6]]; on 1, an adjacent building catches.
The well
Water for firefighting.
Rooftops
Overhanging storeys—drop onto the Legion from above.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-43]{Centurion Marcus Crustus}. Treats pizza as a supply line and the city as a front. He is honourable in a ridiculous way: he will accept a formal challenge and abide by the result.
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-13.public-face]{Marda Hobb}. Fights with a cudgel and a bung-mallet; she will not leave the Tankard.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Rallying the defenders[[/check skill=prf dc=13]] @FWCheck[S08|skill=prf dc=13|Rally the Quarter]{Request}Defenders gain advantage on attacks for a round.
Challenging Crustus to single combat[[/check skill=per dc=14]] @FWCheck[S08|skill=per dc=14|Challenge the centurion]{Request} (or Intimidation)He accepts; if he loses, the Legion withdraws.
Breaking the formation[[/check skill=ath dc=15]] @FWCheck[S08|skill=ath dc=15|Break the shield wall]{Request}The Legion loses its formation bonus.
Putting out a fire[[/check skill=ath dc=10]] @FWCheck[S08|skill=ath dc=10|Douse the flames]{Request}The fire is out.

Developments

  • Victory: the Last Independents become the resistance; Marda keeps the unsigned deeds safe; the party is welcome at her table forever.
  • Defeat: the Tankard & Tallow survives (Marda will not leave) but several taverns burn; Marda gives the deeds to the party for safekeeping.

Scaling & Pacing

Level 6: 8 veterans + 1 gladiator. Weak party: 6 veterans and defenders deal 2 damage per round to the Legion. Strong party: add Veronique’s cleaners (4 thugs) on the rooftops.

pages.name: Twist, Rewards & Aftermath
pages.html:
GM ONLY

The Twist

Veronique doesn’t want to win this. She wants to see what the party does. If they defy her, she offers them a secret deal later (Succession Planning): help her replace Baron Cleave.

Rewards

  • 1,000 gp less 30% if the taverns sign.
  • A place at Marda’s table if they refuse.
  • One star either way (QuestRabbit counts completion, not outcome—note this).

Receipt — @FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S08]{The Unsigned Deeds}

The Unsigned Deeds. The original deeds of every tavern that refused, kept by Marda Hobb. Proof that the Material Plane’s “subsidiaries” were never wholly acquired.Voids Clause 5 — Title to Subsidiaries in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.finalcontract]{the Final Contract}.

@FWReceipt[S08|fw.item.receipt.S08]{Award Receipt & announce}

Outcomes

If the party…Then…
signed all fourteenThe Quarter vanishes into Murder Kings. No Receipt unless the party saved at least one deed. Marda will not speak to them until S21.
refusedThe Siege; the Commons Tally begins.
sabotagedThe Siege; Veronique is quietly impressed.

Forward

  • The Last Independents become the resistance. Their handshake network is invisible to the Ledger. Commons Tally begins.
  • The Tankard & Tallow is the war room in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S21]{S21}.

Synopsis

The five Harrow brothers swore an oath—in life, and again in death—to be in every Five Wights kitchen at once. Now Four is gone, and the oath is failing: fries flicker, customers repeat sentences, and the brothers finish each other’s sentences with Four’s missing words.

The brothers feel where Four is: “north, cold, stacked.” They lead the party to the CostCo-op warehouse depot, where membership is required to enter (and signing up binds your descendants). Inside, aisles stretch for miles and staff in vests hand out free samples of something sweet and alive.

In the executive vault, guarded by the dragons’ kobolds and a Compliance Officer, Four lies dormant in a box tagged COLLATERAL. The party must carry him out while the vault wakes up behind them.

Background — DM Only

When the Restaurant Necromancy Group borrowed from Creation & Company to expand, it pledged collateral: one of the Five Wights. Four Harrow was boxed, tagged and stored in the CostCo-op executive vault, which serves as the Counting House’s “cold storage” for collateral. Because the brothers’ oath binds all five to every kitchen, removing one makes reality itself thinner wherever a Five Wights stands.

The vault holds other collateral too: a king’s soul, a city’s river, a whole year (the Year Without Spring, which nobody remembers). Taking more than Four will be noticed by the Ledger.

CostCo-op is the Hoard Syndicate’s warehouse chain, run by seven ancient dragons who have never attended a board meeting. Its Membership Manager, Hal Grundy, is a harried, decent man trapped by his own contract.

Running This Mission

  • The glitch kitchen is weird-fun: repeating dialogue, flickering props, doubled NPCs. Lean in.
  • The membership card is a real dilemma. A real sign-up binds the character’s descendants; make that clear.
  • The vault escape is a chase in reverse: the vault wakes up behind the party.
  • Four is a witness in S24. Make him memorable.

Threads In and Out

  • In: Restaurant Necromancy Group (Wight Castle, @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S05]{S05}); the Union side contract “@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-67.membership-drive]{Membership Drive}” provides membership cards.
  • Out: the CostCo-op vault and its seven dragon directors return in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S19]{S19}; Four is a witness in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S24]{S24}.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

You walk into the Five Wights on Corporate Row for lunch—and so do you. For a moment, there are two of each of you at the door, then one. The fries on the counter flicker like candle flames. A customer at the till says, “One stack, please,” and then says it again, exactly the same, and again.

Behind the counter, four pale brothers in identical paper hats look up together. “We need,” says One. “You,” says Two. “To find,” says Three. Then a long, empty pause, where a fourth voice should be. “…Four,” finishes Five, very quietly.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-19-five-wights-glitch-kitchen]{Open battlemap}
When: Lunchtime
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-06]{One, Two, Three and Five Harrow}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S09|The Oath of the Five Wights]{The Oath of the Five Wights} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S09|The Oath of the Five Wights]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The kitchen of Five Wights is the same kitchen in every branch—and right now it is several of them at once. A grill flickers between steel and iron. A prep table is briefly two prep tables. Through the pass, you glimpse other kitchens, other dining rooms, other customers, like reflections in a broken mirror.

DM Description

Each Five Wights branch is a single, oath-bound kitchen experienced in many places at once. With Four missing, the oath is failing. Glitches: menu items “exist slightly less” (a fry passes through a hand), customers repeat sentences, the brothers finish one another’s sentences but leave gaps where Four’s words belong.

The brothers explain: they swore to be in every kitchen, always, together. Four vanished three nights ago from every branch at once. They can feel where he is—“north, cold, stacked”—and will lead the party there.

Features of the Area

The glitch
Each round in the kitchen, roll [[/r 1d6]]: 1 — a character is duplicated for a moment (an echo that copies their last action); 2 — an item flickers out of existence for a round; 3–6 — nothing.
The pass
A window into other branches.
Four’s station
An empty grill where the hat hangs on its hook, unworn.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-06]{The Harrow Brothers}. They speak in sequence, one word or phrase each, in order: One, Two, Three, [gap], Five. They are polite, solemn and frightened. They will remember every order the party has ever placed.

SituationRollResult

Tracing Four[[/check skill=inv dc=13]] @FWCheck[S09|skill=inv dc=13|Find where Four went]{Request}A delivery slip in the pass: “Collateral collection — CostCo-op, Warehouse District.”
Resisting the glitch[[/save ability=cha dc=13]] @FWSave[S09|ability=cha dc=13|Stay yourself]{Request}Failure: you repeat your last sentence involuntarily for a minute.

The brothers walk in a line, one behind the other, heads turned north like compass needles. As you pass each Five Wights on the way, the glitches grow worse: a whole branch flickers out for a heartbeat and back. People in the street repeat themselves. A pigeon lands twice.

A short travel scene. The brothers feel “north, cold, stacked” more strongly the closer they get—cold storage, stacked pallets. They stop outside the CostCo-op depot in the Warehouse District: a vast windowless box with a painted sign, MEMBERS ONLY. MEMBERS FOREVER.

pages.name: Scene 3 — The Warehouse
pages.html:
GM ONLY

When: Evening
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-67]{Hal Grundy}, sample staff
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S09|CostCo-op Membership Agreement]{CostCo-op Membership Agreement} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S09|CostCo-op Membership Agreement]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The doors slide open with a sigh of cold air. Inside, the warehouse goes on further than the building outside should allow: aisles of steel shelving forty feet high, stacked with pallets of everything, lit by lanterns that buzz. Staff in red vests drive mechanical pallet-lifters along the aisles. Near the entrance, a smiling woman at a sample table holds out a tiny paper cup of something pale and sweet that moves very slightly in the cup.

“Free sample?”

DM Description

A membership card is required to go past the entrance (Hal Grundy enforces it, miserably). Options: Membership Drive’s cards (from the side contract), a forgery (Deception or forgery kit DC 16), or a real sign-up—which binds the signer and all their descendants to CostCo-op membership forever (a real, permanent Ledger entry; note it).

The free samples are the Mother Culture (S18): eating one is harmless, delicious and makes the character feel briefly watched by something vast and slow. Gelli (if with the party) quivers violently near them.

The executive vault is at the back, beyond the bulk aisles, past a door marked EXECUTIVE MEMBERS ONLY.

Features of the Area

Bulk aisles
Endless pallets. Getting lost: [[/check skill=sur dc=13]] @FWCheck[S09|skill=sur dc=13|Navigate the infinite aisles]{Request}.
Sample tables
Mother Culture samples, roast owlbear chunks, potion shots.
Membership desk
Hal Grundy and a ledger.
Loading bays
Carriages and the way out.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-67]{Hal Grundy}. A sweating, decent middle manager with a clipboard and a membership lanyard that has become part of his neck. He will look the other way if the party is kind and convincing; he dreads the dragons.

pages.name: Scene 4 — The Executive Vault
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-20-executive-collateral-vault]{Open battlemap}
When: Night
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.compliance-officer]{a Compliance Officer}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.kobold]{Hoard kobolds}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.guard-drake]{guard drakes}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.mimic]{mimic pallets}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S09|Four’s Collateral Tag]{Four’s Collateral Tag} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S09|Four’s Collateral Tag]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The executive vault is cold enough to see your breath. Steel floors, steel walls, rows of steel cages, each holding a single crate with a single tag. Some tags you can read from here: A KING’S SOUL. THE RIVER BRANDE (UPPER). ONE (1) YEAR — SPRING, UNUSED.

In the centre of the vault, under a lamp, sits a long crate the size of a coffin. Through the slats, a pale face in a paper hat lies very still. The tag reads: COLLATERAL — RNG — PARTNER No. 4.

Between you and the crate stands a figure in a grey suit, with a grey face and a lanyard with no name. It is reading a clipboard. It does not look up. “Membership number?”

DM Description

The vault is guarded by a Compliance Officer, six kobolds of the Hoard, two guard drakes and four mimics disguised as pallets. Opening Four’s box without the Ledger’s permission sounds an alarm.

Other collateral can be taken—one item more—but the Ledger will notice (and the Hoard will want it back in S19).

Features of the Area

Cages
Steel cages holding collateral crates; picking a cage lock: thieves’ tools DC 15.
Four’s crate
Under the lamp. Alarmed.
Guard post
A kobold card table and bunk.
Drake pen
Straw, bones, a trough; two guard drakes.
The mimic pallets
Four of the pallets near the exit are mimics.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Opening Four’s crate quietly[[/check skill=slt dc=17]] @FWCheck[S09|skill=slt dc=17|Open the collateral crate without the alarm]{Request}Opened silently. Otherwise the alarm sounds.
Reasoning with the Compliance Officer[[/check skill=per dc=18]] @FWCheck[S09|skill=per dc=18|Present a valid claim to the Compliance Officer]{Request}It steps aside if shown a document that “releases” the collateral (e.g. Five Wights’ franchise agreement, read cleverly).
Spotting mimics[[/check skill=prc dc=15]] @FWCheck[S09|skill=prc dc=15|Which pallets are wrong?]{Request}You spot them.
Calming the drakes[[/check skill=ani dc=14]] @FWCheck[S09|skill=ani dc=14|Calm the guard drakes]{Request}They do not attack.

Developments

  • The party takes Four and the tag (Receipt).

Scaling & Pacing

Level 7: as written. Weak: 1 drake, 2 mimics.

pages.name: Scene 5 — Collateral Recovery
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-20-executive-collateral-vault]{Open battlemap}
When: Immediately
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-06]{Four Harrow}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

As the lid comes off, the vault wakes. Lamps flare red along the ceiling. Cages rattle. Somewhere deep in the warehouse, something very large shifts its weight, and the floor shivers. Four Harrow opens his eyes, looks at you, and says, very simply, the word his brothers have been missing: “Four.”

DM Description

A reverse chase out of the warehouse: the vault doors close one by one; mimic pallets lunge from the aisles; kobolds pursue; the Compliance Officer walks after the party, never hurrying, never stopping, until they leave CostCo-op property.

When the party carries Four out of the doors, every Five Wights in Brandmere snaps back into reality at once. The brothers, wherever they are, say together: “Thank you.”

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Outrunning the closing doors[[/check skill=ath dc=14]] @FWCheck[S09|skill=ath dc=14|Beat the closing vault doors]{Request}Through. Failure: trapped for a round.
Navigating out[[/check skill=sur dc=14]] @FWCheck[S09|skill=sur dc=14|Find the way out of the aisles]{Request}A shortcut.

Developments

  • Four is returned; the oath holds.
  • Four becomes a witness.

Scaling & Pacing

3 rounds of pursuit; end when the party exits.

Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-06.public-face]{Doris Plank}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.benny-abacus]{Benny Abacus}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S10]{The Wand-Mart Cost Ledger}

Synopsis

Wand-Mart, the vast supercentre on the city’s edge, sells everything for less than it costs: healing potions, spell scrolls, rations, torches—all rolled back. An anonymous shareholder wants to know how. The party arrives on Rollback Day, the biggest sale of the year, and watches customers grow a few days older with every purchase.

In the stockroom, invoices show every item costs more than it sells for; a clerk mentions “time payments”. A heist into the cash office brings the party face to face with General Manager Doris Plank, cheerfully unmoved, with a Folio on her desk whose entries rewrite themselves. She explains how it works—and offers them lifetime free shopping.

Then Veronique Salt, the anonymous shareholder, reveals the truth: “C&C doesn’t stand for Crown & Cleaver. It stands for Creation & Company. We all belong to it. So do you.” She offers the party a partnership against the Board.

Background — DM Only

A Folio is a branch-ledger: a page of the Grand Ledger delegated to a subsidiary. Anything written in it is true, but every line is paid for in the writer’s—or the customer’s—time. Wand-Mart’s “@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-65.rollback]{Rollback}” prices are real: the difference is debited from customers in days of their lives, recorded in the Folio and remitted to the Counting House.

The Adventure Retail Consortium is fronted by Doris Plank and controlled by SKÜ, the Warehouse Mind—a colony of mimics grown through IKEA Mimic’s furniture into a single intelligence. The shelves of Wand-Mart are, in places, alive.

Veronique hired the party as “anonymous shareholder” to gain leverage over ARC—and the Board. She has decided the party is worth recruiting.

Running This Mission

  • Rollback Day is crowd chaos. Use the ageing effect as horror-comedy: a teenager buys a sword and comes out with a moustache.
  • The cash office is a heist with a twist: Doris isn’t hiding anything; she’s proud of it.
  • End Act II on Veronique’s confession. It reframes the whole campaign.
  • The Folio has a page for the party. Show it to them.

Threads In and Out

  • In: Veronique’s leverage plans (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S08]{S08}).
  • Out: end of Act II; the party learns C&C means Creation & Company; a Folio (@FWLink[Item|fw.item.magic.01]{Folio}) in hand; the Mandate Progress meter.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The job slip is unsigned, printed on heavy cream card, and paid in advance in a sealed purse. Pip turns it over twice. “An anonymous shareholder,” he says. “That’s… fancy. Wand-Mart, though! Rollback Day! You could pick up some potions while you’re there.”

pages.name: Scene 1 — Rollback Day
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-21-wand-mart-supercentre]{Open battlemap}
When: Morning — doors open
Present: shoppers, greeters
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S10|Wand-Mart Rollback Day Flyer]{Wand-Mart Rollback Day Flyer} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S10|Wand-Mart Rollback Day Flyer]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The doors of the Wand-Mart Supercentre open at the first bell, and the crowd surges in like the sea through a broken dam. Inside, the store is enormous: forty aisles under a roof of lanterns, yellow ROLLBACK! signs on every shelf, a smiling greeter in a blue vest at the door with a basket of stickers.

A young man in a College Ward scarf grabs a discounted longsword off a shelf, pays at the nearest till, and turns away grinning. He is a few steps from the door when you notice his chin: a faint shadow of stubble that wasn’t there before. By the time he reaches the exit, he has a moustache.

DM Description

Rollback Day is chaos: crowds, sales, fights over the last cheap potion. Customers age a few days per purchase (a week for a big item); nobody notices except the party.

Run a short crowd scene: the party can observe purchases, talk to shoppers (an old woman who has shopped here weekly for thirty years and is, she thinks, about forty), follow staff into the back, and avoid buying anything. If a character buys something, they age too (a day per gold piece saved—roll [[/r 1d6]] days for a small item).

Features of the Area

Aisles
Forty aisles of gondola shelving. Some shelves are mimics (SKÜ).
Checkouts
Eight tills with queue ropes. Each till has a small brass plate: TIME PAYMENTS ACCEPTED.
Customer service
A desk where complaints are “noted”.
Stockroom
Back doors marked STAFF; pallets of goods.

Resisting a bargain[[/save ability=wis dc=14]] @FWSave[S10|ability=wis dc=14|Resist the Rollback!]{Request}Failure: you buy something (and age).

The stockroom is a canyon of pallets under bare lanterns. A tired gnome clerk with ink to the elbows sits at a desk surrounded by invoices, muttering sums.

Invoices show every Rollback item costs Wand-Mart more than it sells for: a healing potion that costs 50 gp to make sells for 20. Where’s the difference? Clerk Benny Abacus, if befriended, mentions “time payments”—“it all balances in the Folio; upstairs takes care of it”—and that the cash office is where the Folio lives.

Some of the stockroom shelves are mimics (SKÜ’s extensions) and listen to everything.

pages.name: Scene 3 — The Cash Office
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-22-wand-mart-cash-office]{Open battlemap}
When: After close
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-06.public-face]{Doris Plank}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.mimic]{shelf mimics}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.helmed-horror]{helmed horrors}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The cash office is quieter than the store and much colder. Rows of counting tables with neat piles of coin. Brass scales. Filing cabinets to the ceiling. And at the far end, behind a broad desk on a blue rug, a silver-haired woman in a blue blazer with a killer smile, writing in a thick book bound in grey.

She looks up, unsurprised. “Contractors! Come in, come in. I’m Doris. Would you like a coffee? We have a rollback on coffee.”

DM Description

Doris Plank is not hiding anything. She is proud of the system. She explains, cheerfully, how it works: Wand-Mart sells below cost; the customer pays the difference in time, which is written in the Folio and remitted upstairs; everyone gets a bargain; “and honestly, who misses a few days?”

She offers the party lifetime free shopping (a card that debits nothing—or rather, debits someone else). If they refuse and try to take the Folio, she calls security: four shelf mimics, two helmed horrors and a SKÜ drone (a giant mimic) from the vault.

Features of the Area

Doris’s desk
The Folio, a glowing lamp, a rug.
Counting tables
Coin piles and scales—scattering coins creates difficult terrain.
Vault
A round vault door; inside, treasure and the SKÜ drone.
Corridor
Back to the stockroom.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-06.public-face]{Doris Plank}. Radiantly friendly; treats the heist as a sales opportunity. She never loses her smile, even in combat.

Checks & Roll Requests

Reading Doris[[/check skill=ins dc=14]] @FWCheck[S10|skill=ins dc=14|Is Doris lying?]{Request}Never. She believes every word.
Talking her down[[/check skill=per dc=18]] @FWCheck[S10|skill=per dc=18|Convince Doris it’s wrong]{Request}She hesitates—“Oh, but the numbers are so good”—and offers a 10% discount instead.

Developments

  • Fight or bargain for the Folio.

Scaling & Pacing

Level 8: Doris (Veronique’s stat block, reskinned) + 4 mimics + 2 helmed horrors + 1 SKÜ drone.

pages.name: Scene 4 — The Folio
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-22-wand-mart-cash-office]{Open battlemap}
When: Immediately

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Folio is heavier than a book should be. Its pages are grey and soft, like ash pressed flat. As you watch, the entries rewrite themselves in neat clerical script: names, purchases, prices, and a column headed DEBITED, filled with numbers of days. Then the pages turn by themselves, and stop on one with your names at the top.

DM Description

The Folio’s entries rewrite themselves as the party watches. Writing in it makes things true—but uses the writer’s time (a line costs 1d4 years for a small change, more for a large one). It is a delegated page of the Grand Ledger.

The party’s page reads: Representatives of the Commons — Rating: 3 stars — Mandate Progress: 60%. Their Rabbit Rating is also a mandate.

The Folio is a magic item (@FWLink[Item|fw.item.magic.01]{Folio}) and, its pages of debited years, the Receipt.

Writing in it[[/save ability=con dc=15]] @FWSave[S10|ability=con dc=15|Pay the Folio’s price]{Request}The line is written. Failure: it costs double.

pages.name: Scene 5 — Veronique’s Confession
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-22-wand-mart-cash-office]{Open battlemap}
When: Dawn
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S10|Veronique’s Partnership Card]{Veronique’s Partnership Card} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S10|Veronique’s Partnership Card]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Veronique is waiting in the empty Wand-Mart car park, leaning against her black carriage, smoking a thin cigarette. She takes the Folio from you—or doesn’t—and looks at your page for a long time.

“I’m your anonymous shareholder,” she says. “I wanted leverage on ARC. Now I have it.” She drops the cigarette and grinds it out. “You’ve been very patient with me, so I’ll be honest, once. C&C doesn’t stand for Crown & Cleaver. It stands for Creation & Company. We all belong to it. So do you.” She holds out a gloved hand. “I’d like a partnership. Against the Board.”

DM Description

Veronique reveals the truth: Creation & Company owns everything—every umbrella corporation, every franchise, QuestRabbit too—and it is buying the Material Plane. She wants to depose Baron Cleave and take his Board seat, and she wants the party as allies. She will share information if they share Receipts.

This ends Act II. The party learns what C&C means and sees the Mandate Progress meter beside their Rabbit Rating.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Reading Veronique[[/check skill=ins dc=16]] @FWCheck[S10|skill=ins dc=16|Can you trust Veronique?]{Request}She means the partnership—for now. She will betray it if it suits her.
Negotiating terms[[/check skill=per dc=16]] @FWCheck[S10|skill=per dc=16|Negotiate the partnership]{Request}She agrees to share Cleave’s secrets (S15) in exchange for one Receipt’s copy.

Developments

  • End of Act II.

Scaling & Pacing

A quiet, devastating finale.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

The Twist

The Folio has a page for the party: “Representatives of the Commons—Rating: 3 stars—Mandate Progress: 60%.” Their Rabbit Rating is a mandate; every good deed brings them closer to being able to sign for everyone.

Rewards

  • 1,200 gp less 30%.
  • A Folio (see Magic Items).

Receipt — @FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S10]{The Wand-Mart Cost Ledger}

The Wand-Mart Cost Ledger. Pages of the Folio showing years debited from customers. Proof that Creation & Company’s purchases are not made at fair value.Voids Clause 2 — Consideration in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.finalcontract]{the Final Contract}.

@FWReceipt[S10|fw.item.receipt.S10]{Award Receipt & announce}

Outcomes

If the party…Then…
accepted Veronique’s partnershipShe shares information through Act III.
refusedShe remains a wary ally of convenience.
accepted Doris’s cardFree shopping—debited from strangers. A moral weight to carry.

Forward

pages.name: DM Overview
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Mission at a Glance

Code / ActS11 · Act III
Grade / LevelGold · Level 9
Client@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-03]{Starkfucks} / @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-57]{Bean There, Summoned That} (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-04]{Arcane Beverage International})
Session length1–2 sessions; a planar expedition with a moral fork
Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11|Scene 1 — The Portal]{Scene 1 — The Portal} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-v-coffee-04-bean-there-summoned-that]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11|Scene 2 — The Plantations]{Scene 2 — The Plantations} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-24-pandemonium-bean-plantations]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11|Scene 3 — The Harvesters]{Scene 3 — The Harvesters} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-24-pandemonium-bean-plantations]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11|Scene 4 — The Overseer]{Scene 4 — The Overseer} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-25-pandemonium-overseers-station]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11|Scene 5 — Sabotage or Harvest]{Scene 5 — Sabotage or Harvest} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-25-pandemonium-overseers-station]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.ada-fairweather]{Ada Fairweather}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.skarrow-vane]{Skarrow Vane}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.thaddeus-quell]{Thaddeus Quell}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-04.public-face]{Sebastian Brew-Hartley}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S11]{The Harvesters’ Testimony}

Synopsis

Arcane Beverage International—unaware the party has turned, or hoping they haven’t—hires them through QuestRabbit for the Seasonal Premium harvest. Pip calls it “a big step up!” The portal is in the back room of Bean There, Summoned That, and the wind starts before anyone opens it.

Pandemonium is a plane of endless wind-carved tunnels. In them grow glowing beans tended by harvesters who remember nothing but their shifts. One, Ada, remembers only her daughter’s name—and she is Agnes Fairweather’s sister, lost when ABI broke the Starkfucks union.

A cambion overseer rides a howler between the rows. Beyond him is the processing shed, where the beans are packed as Compliance: the secret ingredient in every ABI drink, a mild, constant agreeableness poured into the whole city every morning. The party can harvest as contracted, poison the crop, or free the harvesters and lead them home.

Background — DM Only

Compliance is ABI’s great secret. Ulth’Arabica, the aboleth in the Roastery Spire, found that beans grown in Pandemonium’s madness absorb it in reverse: the drinker becomes calmer, more reasonable, more willing to sign. Every latte in Brandmere carries a trace. It is why nobody complains about the purple awnings.

The harvesters are workers who signed ABI “retention” contracts—people from broken unions, debtors, the missing. Pandemonium’s wind scours their memories until only the shift remains. They are not chained; they simply cannot remember anywhere else to be.

The overseer, Skarrow Vane, is a cambion on an ABI performance bonus. He is cruel because cruelty hits targets.

Running This Mission

  • The wind is the star. Describe it constantly: it howls, whispers, sings, mocks, and says the characters’ own names back to them.
  • The memory-loss save is player-facing: let players choose what their characters forget (a name, a favourite food, how they met). Write them down. They return when the party leaves Pandemonium—mostly.
  • Ada is the emotional centre. If Agnes Fairweather is alive and allied (S04), bring a letter from her.
  • Make the fork clear: harvest (paid, complicit), burn (ABI knows), or free (no fee, the harvesters’ testimony).

Threads In and Out

  • In: the Marchetti Memo (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S06]{S06}) named Pandemonium; Agnes’s union (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S04]{S04}).
  • Out: ABI’s supply is cut; Ulth’Arabica takes notice; Compliance wears off across the city. The harvesters guide the party through Pandemonium again in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S22]{S22}.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Pip slides the contract across the table with both paws, ears up, whiskers trembling. “Gold grade,” he whispers. “Gold! Planar procurement for ABI—that’s a big step up! There’s hazard pay. And ear protection, apparently.” He frowns at the line. “Why would you need ear protection to pick beans?”

pages.name: Scene 1 — The Portal
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-v-coffee-04-bean-there-summoned-that]{Open battlemap}
When: Before dawn
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.thaddeus-quell]{Thaddeus Quell (ABI procurement)}, barista summoners
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S11|ABI Procurement Order]{ABI Procurement Order} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S11|ABI Procurement Order]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Bean There, Summoned That is quiet at this hour: chairs upturned on tables, the espresso machines cold, a chalkboard reading TODAY’S FAMILIAR: OWL. But the back room is loud. Behind a door marked STOCK, something is howling.

The door opens on a summoning circle chalked in coffee grounds, ringed with burlap sacks. In the centre, the air is torn like a sheet of paper, and through the tear pours wind—cold, dry, and full of voices. Your hair stands on end. Somewhere inside the wind, something says your name, and laughs.

DM Description

Thaddeus Quell, ABI’s procurement manager (the union-breaker from S04, if the party met him), briefs the party with a clipboard and earmuffs. Twelve sacks; the overseer will sign for them; the portal stays open for twelve hours.

The baristas maintaining the circle are summoners on minimum wage. One, a tired tiefling named Jory, mutters: “Nobody who goes for the harvest comes back the same. Some don’t come back.”

Coffee-ground chalk; disturbing it collapses the portal in 1 minute.

pages.name: Scene 2 — The Plantations
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-24-pandemonium-bean-plantations]{Open battlemap}
When: On-plane (hours pass strangely)
Present: harvesters
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S11|What I Have Forgotten (player tracker)]{What I Have Forgotten (player tracker)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S11|What I Have Forgotten (player tracker)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

You step into a tunnel the width of a cathedral, carved by wind through black rock. Its walls are terraced, and on every terrace grow bean bushes whose pods glow a soft, sick gold, lighting the tunnel like a thousand lanterns. The wind never stops. It pours down the tunnel in waves, and every wave carries voices: whispers, sobs, laughter, snatches of song.

Along the terraces, figures in grey sacking move slowly, picking, humming. They do not look up. They hum the same four notes, over and over, and you realise the wind is humming them too.

DM Description

Pandemonium’s madness: every hour on-plane, each creature makes [[/save ability=wis dc=14]] @FWSave[S11|ability=wis dc=14|Pandemonium’s wind]{Request}. On a failure, the character forgets one thing (the player chooses: a name, a place, a skill they learned, the face of a loved one). Three failures: the character starts humming and must be led.

The plantations are a maze of tunnels; the harvesters, the overseer’s station and the processing shed are deeper in. Harvesting a sack takes 1 hour per character.

Features of the Area

Terraces
Climbing between them: [[/check skill=ath dc=13]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=ath dc=13|Climb the terraces]{Request}.
Wind gusts
At initiative 20, roll [[/r 1d6]]: on a 1, a gust; each creature in the open makes [[/save ability=str dc=15]] @FWSave[S11|ability=str dc=15|Brace against the gust]{Request} or is pushed 15 ft.
Glowing pods
Tasting a bean: [[/save ability=wis dc=15]] @FWSave[S11|ability=wis dc=15|Resist Compliance]{Request} or become agreeable (disadvantage on checks to refuse a request) for an hour.
Echo-vents
Shouting into one carries a message through the tunnels.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Navigating[[/check skill=sur dc=15]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=sur dc=15|Navigate the wind tunnels]{Request}You find the harvesters’ camp.
Identifying the beans[[/check skill=nat dc=16]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=nat dc=16|What are these beans?]{Request}Not coffee. They drink in madness and give back calm.

Developments

  • The party reaches the harvesters.

Scaling & Pacing

Weak party: madness save every two hours.

pages.name: Scene 3 — The Harvesters
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-24-pandemonium-bean-plantations]{The harvesters’ terraces}
When: Deeper in
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.ada-fairweather]{Ada Fairweather}, harvesters
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S11|The Scratched Wall]{The Scratched Wall} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S11|The Scratched Wall]{Show to players} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S11|Agnes’s Letter (if allied)]{Agnes’s Letter (if allied)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S11|Agnes’s Letter (if allied)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

One harvester has stopped humming. She is thin, with grey sacking for a dress and a sack of glowing beans over her shoulder, and she is staring at a scratch in the rock wall. She has scratched one word, over and over, hundreds of times, until the stone is pale with it: MOLLY.

“That’s my daughter,” she says, when she sees you looking. “I think that’s my daughter. I can’t remember anything else.”

DM Description

Ada Fairweather is Agnes Fairweather’s sister (S04), taken when ABI broke the Starkfucks union. She remembers only her daughter’s name—Molly—and nothing else. Agnes has looked after Molly since.

If the party carries Agnes’s letter, or describes Agnes, Ada weeps and starts to remember. She knows the harvest routine, the overseer’s patrol and the way to the processing shed. She also knows how many harvesters there are: forty-one. “We can’t leave. Where would we go?”

Playing the NPCs

Ada Fairweather. Quiet, careful, holding onto one word. As memories return she becomes braver and angrier. She will lead the harvesters out if someone gives her a reason.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Reaching Ada[[/check skill=per dc=13]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=per dc=13|Reach Ada through the fog]{Request}She remembers her name and Agnes’s.
Rousing the harvesters[[/check skill=prf dc=15]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=prf dc=15|Wake the harvesters from their hum]{Request}They stop humming and listen. (Advantage with Ada’s help.)
Healing a mindlesser restoration / greater restorationRestores one harvester’s memory (or the character’s own).

Lines to Steal

Ada: “That’s my daughter. I think that’s my daughter.”
A harvester: “Where would we go? The shift is all there is.”

Developments

  • The harvesters will follow if the overseer is dealt with.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The overseer’s station sits on a stone spur over a great wind-chasm: a watchtower, a whipping post, a quota board chalked with harvester numbers, and a long shed with brass doors from which comes the smell of roasting. Riding up the spur on a howler—a hound with too many teeth and a mouth that screams—comes a tall, handsome figure in an ABI quality-control tabard, horns polished, whip coiled on his hip.

“Contractors!” Skarrow Vane says. “Wonderful. You’re behind quota.”

DM Description

Skarrow Vane, a cambion, oversees the harvest for a bonus. He signs for the sacks and can be bargained with (he is greedy) or fought. If the party tries to free the harvesters, he whistles: four howlers and a living storm (two air elementals) come down the chasm.

Beating him opens the processing shed: brass roasters, packing tables and crates stamped COMPLIANCE — FOR ALL ABI BRANCHES.

Features of the Area

The chasm
Falling: 6d6 bludgeoning (the wind slows the fall—roll [[/r 6d6]]); the wind can hurl a creature back up on a gust.
The watchtower
Height advantage; Vane’s ledger of quotas.
The quota board
Each harvester as a number.
Processing shed
Roasters (fire hazard), crates of Compliance, an ABI shipping manifest.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.skarrow-vane]{Skarrow Vane}. Smooth, mocking, bonus-motivated. Will sell out ABI for a better offer but always try to take both payments.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Bribing Vane[[/check skill=per dc=16]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=per dc=16|Make Vane a better offer]{Request}He looks away for an hour (and later reports it).
Intimidating Vane[[/check skill=itm dc=17]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=itm dc=17|Make Vane back down]{Request}He flees on his howler.
Disabling the roasters[[/check skill=inv dc=14]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=inv dc=14|Sabotage the roasters]{Request} (or tinker’s tools)The shed can’t process the crop.

Developments

  • The processing shed is open.

Scaling & Pacing

Level 9: cambion + 4 howlers + 2 air elementals. Weak: 2 howlers, 1 elemental.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The processing shed is warm and smells like the best cup of coffee you have ever had—which makes it worse. Crate after crate stands ready for shipping, each stamped with the names of ABI branches across Brandmere. Behind you, forty-one harvesters stand in the doorway, waiting to see what you will do.

DM Description

Three choices, which can be combined:

Harvest as contracted. Twelve sacks back through the portal; full fee; Compliance keeps flowing.Burn or poison the crop. Ends Compliance for the season. ABI will know who did it.Free the harvesters. Lead forty-one people back through the portal before it closes. They give testimony—signed with handshakes, not quills—and join the Commons Tally.

Returning through the portal restores most forgotten memories. Each character who failed three or more saves loses one memory permanently (the player chooses).

Checks & Roll Requests

Burning the crop[[/check skill=sur dc=12]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=sur dc=12|Set the fields alight with the wind]{Request}The terraces burn for a day.
Leading the harvesters out[[/check skill=per dc=14]] @FWCheck[S11|skill=per dc=14|Keep forty-one people moving]{Request}Everyone makes it. Failure: [[/r 1d6]] are lost to the wind.
Getting through the closing portal[[/save ability=dex dc=14]] @FWSave[S11|ability=dex dc=14|Dive through the closing portal]{Request}Through.

Developments

  • Back in Brandmere: Ada and Agnes reunited; Molly meets her mother.

pages.name: DM Overview
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Mission at a Glance

Code / ActS12 · Act III
Grade / LevelGold · Level 9–10
Client@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-34]{Goodberry’s} (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-04]{ABI Wellness}) — opposed by the temples
Session length1–2 sessions: a crisis, a heist and a court case
Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S12|Scene 1 — Temples in Crisis]{Scene 1 — Temples in Crisis} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-26-temple-healing-hand]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S12|Scene 2 — The Shrine]{Scene 2 — The Shrine} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-26-temple-healing-hand]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S12|Scene 3 — Goodberry’s Head Office]{Scene 3 — Goodberry’s Head Office} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-27-goodberrys-head-office]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S12|Scene 4 — The Trademark Hearing]{Scene 4 — The Trademark Hearing} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-28-guild-arbitration-court]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S12|Scene 5 — Freeing Healing]{Scene 5 — Freeing Healing} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-27-goodberrys-head-office]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.brother-allard]{Brother Allard}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.sister-wren]{Sister Wren}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.maud-penhallow]{Arbiter Maud Penhallow}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.sallow-and-tine]{Messrs Sallow & Tine}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S12]{The Healing Deed}

Synopsis

Brother Allard of Death Save Delivery sends word: clerics across Brandmere cannot heal. Cure wounds fizzles; potions taste of chalk; prayers get a polite refusal. Outside every temple stands a Goodberry’s licensing booth selling HEALING™ by the prayer. People are dying on temple floors.

At the oldest shrine, Sister Wren confesses: years ago she signed away Healing’s deed to save her dying son. It was a Goodberry’s wellness contract. The deed is now in ABI Wellness’s vault at Goodberry’s Head Office—alongside the deeds to Sleep, Courage and Weekends.

The party can steal the deed in a heist through a wellness-themed office of meditation rooms and juice bars, or force a trademark hearing at the Guild Arbitration Court and argue that Healing cannot be owned. Either way, writing “owned by nobody” on the deed sets Healing free.

Background — DM Only

In the Ledger, a concept can be owned like land. Creation & Company’s subsidiaries have spent decades acquiring them quietly: Rest (Nine Circles), Weekends (Planar Hospitality), Sleep and Courage (ABI). Healing was the boldest purchase: obtained from its keeper under duress, it is now licensed back to the world.

Concepts that are owned but unused are stored in the Third Place, the grey limbo where the Company keeps what it has acquired and forgotten. Healing itself—a thin, kind presence—is there now (S17).

Goodberry’s is ABI’s wellness brand: berries, juice cleanses and smiling druids who “heal 1 hp per berry, terms apply”.

Running This Mission

  • Open on the crisis: someone dies who shouldn’t. Make the stakes personal (a recurring NPC injured in an earlier mission).
  • Sister Wren is not a villain. Let her confession land.
  • Offer both routes—heist or hearing. The hearing is a structured debate with three arguments.
  • Party healers are affected too. Their spells require a licence (see the Licence handout). Paying is an option—and a moral cost.

Threads In and Out

  • In: Brother Allard (Death Save Delivery); ABI after @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11]{S11}.
  • Out: Healing, the personified concept, remains in the Third Place until @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S17]{S17}; Allard’s temple becomes a Last Independents sanctuary.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The message comes by a temple runner, a boy of ten with blood on his sleeves that isn’t his. “Brother Allard says come,” he gasps. “The prayers don’t work. Nobody can heal. There’s a man at the Lantern who fell off a roof and they’ve been praying over him all night and nothing’s happening, and there’s a booth outside selling—” he swallows— “selling healing. For money. Please come.”

pages.name: Scene 1 — Temples in Crisis
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-26-temple-healing-hand]{Open battlemap}
When: Morning
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.brother-allard]{Brother Allard}, the wounded, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.fennel]{a Goodberry’s licensing druid}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S12|HEALING™ Trademark Notice]{HEALING™ Trademark Notice} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S12|HEALING™ Trademark Notice]{Show to players} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S12|HEALING™ Licence (per prayer)]{HEALING™ Licence (per prayer)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S12|HEALING™ Licence (per prayer)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Temple of the Healing Hand is full. Pews have been pushed aside to make room for pallets, and on every pallet lies someone hurt: a roofer with a broken back, a child burning with fever, a guardsman with a sword-cut that will not close. Clerics kneel among them, praying, hands glowing—and the glow flickers and dies, again and again, like a candle in a draught.

Outside, on the temple steps, stands a neat green booth with a striped awning and a smiling young druid in a Goodberry’s apron. A sign reads: HEALING™ — LICENSED BY THE PRAYER. FIRST CONSULTATION FREE.

DM Description

Every healing spell cast without a licence fails unless the caster succeeds on a [[/check skill=rel dc=18]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=rel dc=18|Force a prayer through the trademark]{Request} (the spell slot is spent either way). Potions of healing heal only the minimum. A licence costs 10 gp per spell level, per cast, paid to Goodberry’s.

Brother Allard has spent all the temple’s coin on licences and run out. He asks the party to find out who owns Healing and how it was sold. The druid at the booth, Fennel, is cheerful and honestly thinks this is good business.

Features of the Area

Pallets of wounded
Stabilising: [[/check skill=med dc=12]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=med dc=12|Stabilise a wounded patient]{Request} (no magic needed).
The altar
An old hand-shaped altar; the shrine beneath it is older still.
Licensing booth
Ledger, receipts, a cash box, berry samples.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.brother-allard]{Brother Allard}. Big, kind, exhausted, his hands shaking from praying all night. He runs Death Save Delivery, the temple’s ambulance service. He is furious and too tired to show it.
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.fennel]{Fennel (Goodberry’s druid)}. Sunny, sincere, completely misguided. Will refund a licence if shown someone dying because of it—and quit, if pushed.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Questioning Fennel[[/check skill=per dc=13]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=per dc=13|Question the licensing druid]{Request}The trademark was “acquired from the shrine”—Sister Wren’s shrine.
Studying a failed spell[[/check skill=arc dc=15]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=arc dc=15|Why do the spells fail?]{Request}The word has been taken. Spells reach for Healing and find a locked door.
Shaming Fennel[[/check skill=itm dc=14]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=itm dc=14|Show Fennel the dying]{Request} or PersuasionShe quits and gives the party her ABI keycard.

Developments

  • Allard sends the party to Sister Wren’s shrine.
