pages.name: Scene 2 — The Shrine
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-26-temple-healing-hand]{The shrine beneath the temple}
When: Midday
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.sister-wren]{Sister Wren}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S12|Wren’s Copy of the Wellness Agreement]{Wren’s Copy of the Wellness Agreement} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S12|Wren’s Copy of the Wellness Agreement]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Beneath the temple, down worn stone steps, is a shrine no bigger than a cottage kitchen: a spring in a stone basin, a single lamp, a wall of handprints pressed into old plaster—every one a healing given here, over centuries. The spring has stopped. The lamp is out. An old woman in a grey habit sits beside the dry basin with her hands in her lap.

“You’ve come about the deed,” Sister Wren says. “I know. I’m the one who sold it.”

DM Description

Sister Wren was the keeper of Healing’s shrine. Twelve years ago her son Tobin was dying of the grey fever. A Goodberry’s wellness consultant offered a cure in exchange for “a simple licensing agreement”. She signed. Tobin lived. Healing became a trademark.

She explains: the deed to Healing is held by ABI Wellness in a vault of trademarks at Goodberry’s Head Office. If someone writes “owned by nobody” on the deed, Healing returns to the world. She cannot do it herself—her signature is the problem.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.sister-wren]{Sister Wren}. Small, upright, unflinching. She does not ask for forgiveness and does not justify herself. She would do it again. Her son Tobin, now twenty-two, works at Goodberry’s Head Office as a juice-bar attendant and knows nothing.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Comforting Wren[[/check skill=ins dc=14]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=ins dc=14|Understand Sister Wren]{Request}She would do it again, and she knows what it cost.
Reading her copy of the contract[[/check skill=inv dc=16]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=inv dc=16|Read Wren’s copy of the contract]{Request}Clause 3: the deed is “held in trust at the Licensor’s principal office”—and a hearing may be demanded by any “affected party”.

Lines to Steal

Sister Wren: “I’m the one who sold it. I’d do it again.”

  • Two routes: the heist (Scene 3) or the hearing (Scene 4).

pages.name: Scene 3 — Goodberry’s Head Office
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-27-goodberrys-head-office]{Open battlemap}
When: After hours (or during the day, in disguise)
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.knight]{wellness security}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.tobin]{Tobin, juice-bar attendant}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S12|Goodberry’s Floor Directory]{Goodberry’s Floor Directory} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S12|Goodberry’s Floor Directory]{Show to players} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S12|Vault of Trademarks — Inventory]{Vault of Trademarks — Inventory} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S12|Vault of Trademarks — Inventory]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Goodberry’s Head Office looks like a garden that has been told to behave: white stone, living walls of green, a lobby with a burbling fountain and a smell of crushed mint. A sign by the lifts lists the floors: MEDITATION · JUICE BAR · NUTRITIONAL ALIGNMENT · LEGAL. Somewhere a harp is playing. The security guards wear plate armour painted a calming sage green.

DM Description

A heist. The vault of trademarks is on the Legal floor, behind the meditation rooms (which are silence-enchanted—useful) and the juice bar (where Tobin works). Security: four knights in sage plate, wards on the vault, and the ABI legal team—two rakshasas in lawyer suits—working late.

The vault holds the deeds to Healing, Sleep, Courage and Weekends, each a thick vellum document under glass. The party can take Healing’s—or more.

Features of the Area

Meditation rooms
Permanent silence; perfect for sneaking.
Juice bar
Tobin; a blender loud enough to cover a break-in.
Nutritional Alignment
Druid offices; a living wall that is also a shambling mound (optional).
Legal
Rakshasa offices; the vault of trademarks.
The vault
Glass cases; wards ([[/check skill=arc dc=17]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=arc dc=17|Disarm the vault wards]{Request}).

Playing the NPCs

Tobin. Twenty-two, cheerful, a little lost. If told the truth about his mother, he is horrified and helps—he has a staff keycard.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Guild Arbitration Court is a round hall of dark wood under a dome painted with scales. The public gallery is packed: clerics in torn robes, the families of the wounded, curious guild-folk. At one table sit two impeccable lawyers in charcoal suits, with gloves on and smiles a little too wide. At the bench, Arbiter Maud Penhallow, a dwarf with spectacles and a gavel the size of a hammer, peers down.

“The matter of ABI Wellness against the Commons,” she says. “Regarding the ownership of Healing. Counsel for the Commons, you may begin.”

DM Description

A debate in three rounds. Each round, the party makes an argument and a check (DC 16); evidence grants advantage. The ABI lawyers counter each round with a rebuttal (which the party can undercut with Insight).

Round 1 — Can a concept be owned? [[/check skill=rel dc=16]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=rel dc=16|Argue that Healing belongs to no one]{Request} or History. Evidence: the shrine’s handprints.Round 2 — Was the sale fair? [[/check skill=per dc=16]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=per dc=16|Argue the sale was made under duress]{Request}. Evidence: Sister Wren’s testimony.Round 3 — Public harm. [[/check skill=ins dc=16]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=ins dc=16|Show the court the harm]{Request} or Persuasion. Evidence: the wounded, the licences, Fennel’s testimony.

Two successes win the hearing; the arbiter orders the deed released. Three successes and the arbiter also voids Sleep, Courage and Weekends.

The gallery
Can be roused (Performance DC 14) for advantage on Round 3.
The rakshasas
Will try to cast suggestion on the arbiter—spotted with [[/check skill=prc dc=17]] @FWCheck[S12|skill=prc dc=17|Spot the lawyers’ spell]{Request}.

SituationRollResult

Developments

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The deed to Healing is a single sheet of thick, soft vellum, warm to the touch, like a hand that has been holding another. At the top, in a hand older than the city: Healing, given freely, to whoever has need. Beneath it, newer ink: Assigned to ABI Wellness Ltd. All Rights Reserved. And beneath that, a shaky signature: Wren.

DM Description

Writing “owned by nobody” on the deed frees Healing. The moment the ink dries, every healing spell in Brandmere works again; the spring in the shrine flows; across the city, people who were dying sit up. Healing itself—thin, kind, very tired—does not return to the world immediately: it has been in the Third Place too long, and lingers there until S17.

The other deeds (Sleep, Courage, Weekends) can be freed the same way if the party has them. Each freed concept goes on to the Commons Tally.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Writing the words—No roll. Anyone can write it. Sister Wren asks to—it releases her too.

Developments

  • Healing is free; the licensing booths close by noon; Fennel quits.

The Twist

The deeds to Sleep, Courage and Weekends are also in the vault. The party can free one more—or all, if they’re brave. ABI will remember.

Rewards

  • The clerics’ gratitude: free healing from any temple in Brandmere, forever.
  • Brother Allard’s temple becomes a Last Independents sanctuary.

Receipt — @FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S12]{The Healing Deed}

The Healing Deed. The original deed to Healing, proving the concept was never lawfully owned by Creation & Company’s subsidiaries.Voids Clause 9 — Non-Infringement in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.finalcontract]{the Final Contract}.

@FWReceipt[S12|fw.item.receipt.S12]{Award Receipt & announce}

If the party…Then…

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Mission at a Glance

Code / ActS13 · Act III
Grade / LevelGold · Level 10
Client@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-31]{Chick’n Familiar} (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-08]{Nine Circles Hospitality})
Session length1 session; a ticking clock and a legal thriller
Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S13|Scene 1 — The Franchisee]{Scene 1 — The Franchisee} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-29-chickn-familiar-midnight-kitchen]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S13|Scene 2 — The Midnight Invoice]{Scene 2 — The Midnight Invoice} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-29-chickn-familiar-midnight-kitchen]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S13|Scene 3 — Counsel Ixabeth Vorr]{Scene 3 — Counsel Ixabeth Vorr} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-29-chickn-familiar-midnight-kitchen]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S13|Scene 4 — The Due-Diligence Report]{Scene 4 — The Due-Diligence Report} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-30-nine-circles-legal-floor]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S13|Scene 5 — The Offer]{Scene 5 — The Offer} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-30-nine-circles-legal-floor]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-31]{Wendel Clasp}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.counsel-ixabeth-vorr]{Counsel Ixabeth Vorr}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-08.controlled-by]{Duke Malphas Vellichor}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.chickadee]{Chickadee}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S13]{Infernal Due-Diligence Report}

Synopsis

Wendel Clasp, a human wizard who swears he read the franchise agreement, runs the Magus Ward Chick’n Familiar. Ten years ago he signed with Nine Circles Hospitality. The consideration was “one soul, payable on maturity”. Maturity is midnight tonight. He begs the party for help.

At midnight a barbed devil collector arrives with a contract and a bucket. The contract has a loophole—the payment is “the first soul that enters the restaurant after midnight”—and the party can send in a chicken. Or argue. Or fight.

Then Counsel Ixabeth Vorr, an erinyes attorney, appears, amused. She’ll enforce the loophole if the party carries her due-diligence report to someone who can use it. The report says something astonishing: Creation & Company’s claim on the Material Plane is contested under infernal law—because Hell is being acquired too. Duke Vellichor wants an alliance. “Even Hell has antitrust concerns.”

Background — DM Only

Nine Circles Hospitality is Creation & Company’s infernal umbrella: Seven-Eleven Hells, Chick’n Familiar, the Long Rest Inn. Duke Malphas Vellichor, a pit fiend, signed a partnership with the Company centuries ago and has discovered—through Ixabeth’s due diligence—that the partnership terms let Tallis Vend absorb the Nine Hells on the same night he takes the Material Plane.

Infernal law is strict about contracts and very strict about jurisdiction. If Hell has a competing claim on the Material Plane, then the Final Contract’s Governing Law clause is false. Vellichor needs someone mortal and credible to carry that into the Counting House.

Chickadee, the Chick’n Familiar mascot, is an actual quasit in a chicken suit. It is loyal to nobody and will do whatever is funniest.

Running This Mission

  • Run it in real time if you can: a candle clock on the table counting to midnight.
  • The loophole is a gift. Let the players feel clever.
  • Ixabeth is the best lawyer in the multiverse and knows it. She enjoys the party.
  • Vellichor’s offer is a genuine choice with long consequences.

Threads In and Out

  • In: Chick’n Familiar’s franchise contract; @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-08]{Nine Circles}.
  • Out: Hell is an uneasy ally. Ixabeth Vorr represents the party at the AGM (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S20]{S20}); Vellichor’s vote in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S23]{S23}; Avernus in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S22]{S22}.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Wendel Clasp is waiting outside the QuestRabbit office when you arrive, in a wizard’s robe with a Chick’n Familiar name badge pinned crookedly to the front. He is clutching a document in both hands and he has clearly not slept.

“I read it,” he says, before anyone can speak. “I swear I read it. Everyone said read the small print and I read the small print. But there’s smaller print. Under the small print. In red.” He holds it out. “It’s due at midnight. Please.”

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Magus Ward Chick’n Familiar is a red-and-white shop on a corner full of wizards’ towers. Inside: buckets stacked on the counter, fryers hissing, a menu board of FAMILIAR MEALS (“Owl Wings”, “Toad-in-the-Bucket”), and a mascot in a fuzzy yellow chicken suit dancing by the door to a tune only it can hear. As you pass, the mascot turns its head all the way round, and its eyes behind the mesh glow red.

DM Description

Wendel explains: the contract’s consideration is “one soul, payable on maturity”; ten years; tonight. He has tried to cancel, sell, and dissolve the franchise. Nothing works.

The party has six hours to prepare: read the contract, research devils, set traps, consult lawyers. Chickadee (a quasit) watches everything and reports to whoever bribes it best.

Features of the Area

Fryers
Boiling oil: 3d6 fire to anyone pushed in—roll [[/r 3d6]].
The bucket stack
Hundreds of empty buckets.
Wendel’s office
Spellbooks, a framed franchise certificate, a hidden magic circle he drew badly.
Walk-in cooler
Crates of chicken—and live chickens for “freshness”.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-31]{Wendel Clasp}. Anxious, pedantic, desperate. A competent wizard with terrible judgement. He will do anything except lose.
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.chickadee]{Chickadee}. Chaotic. Will steal the contract, swap it, hide it, or give it to the devil—whatever is funniest. Can be bought with a bucket of chicken and a promise of mischief.

pages.name: Scene 2 — The Midnight Invoice
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-29-chickn-familiar-midnight-kitchen]{Open battlemap}
When: Midnight
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.collector-grix]{Collector Grix (barbed devil)}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.imp]{imps}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.chain-devil]{a chain devil}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

At the twelfth stroke the lights go out. The fryers stop hissing. The smell of chicken becomes the smell of sulphur. The front door, which was locked, swings open, and in walks a devil covered in barbs, eight feet tall, in a tidy waistcoat, carrying a briefcase in one hand and an empty Chick’n Familiar bucket in the other.

“Collector Grix, Nine Circles Accounts Receivable,” it says. “I’m here for the consideration.” It sets the bucket on the counter. “Who’s first?”

DM Description

Grix must take the first soul to enter after midnight. If the party sent a chicken in at 12:00:01, Grix glares, checks the contract, and—bound by the letter—puts the chicken’s soul in the bucket. Furious, it then tries to provoke a breach (if anyone attacks it, the contract is “disputed” and it can call for enforcement: four imps and a chain devil).

If the party has no loophole, Grix claims Wendel. The party can argue (see checks), fight, or bargain.

Features of the Area

The doorway
Whoever crosses first after midnight is the payment.

Lights out; the devils see in it.

pages.name: Scene 3 — Counsel Ixabeth Vorr
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-29-chickn-familiar-midnight-kitchen]{Open battlemap}
When: Immediately after
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.counsel-ixabeth-vorr]{Counsel Ixabeth Vorr}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S13|Ixabeth Vorr’s Card]{Ixabeth Vorr’s Card} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S13|Ixabeth Vorr’s Card]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

A woman steps out of the dark beside the counter as if she had always been there: tall, black-winged, in a perfectly cut suit the colour of dried blood, with a silver pen behind one ear. She looks at the chicken in the bucket and laughs—a real, delighted laugh.

“Oh, that’s good,” she says. “That’s very good. Grix, go home.” The barbed devil goes, without a word. She turns to you. “Counsel Ixabeth Vorr. Nine Circles. I’d like to hire you.”

DM Description

Ixabeth enforces the loophole (Wendel is free; the franchise is dissolved) in exchange for a favour: carry her due-diligence report to “someone who can use it”. She explains its contents with relish.

She is an erinyes, a fallen angel of law, and the best attorney in the multiverse. She respects precision and cleverness and despises cruelty that isn’t billable.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.counsel-ixabeth-vorr]{Counsel Ixabeth Vorr}. Delighted by good arguments; bored by bad ones. Never lies; omits beautifully. She treats the party as promising junior associates.

Checks & Roll Requests

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Nine Circles legal floor is reached by a lift that goes down further than the building should. Its doors open on an open-plan office of black marble, lit by braziers: hundreds of desks, each with a quill scratching by itself and an imp clerk filing. Along one wall, a window looks out—not onto Brandmere but onto a red plain under a burning sky.

DM Description

Ixabeth shows the party the report. Its findings: under infernal law, Creation & Company’s claims on the Material Plane are not recognised; Hell itself has a competing jurisdictional claim (by ancient treaty); and the Nine Circles partnership allows Tallis Vend to absorb the Nine Hells on Acquisition Night. Hell is being acquired. Hell does not like it.

The report is the Receipt. Whoever carries it into the Counting House can contest the Final Contract’s Governing Law.

Self-writing desks

A view of Avernus (a preview of S22).
Ixabeth’s office

pages.name: Scene 5 — The Offer
pages.html:

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Duke Vellichor’s office is the size of a cathedral and almost empty: a desk of black iron, two chairs, and behind the desk a pit fiend in a tailored suit, wings folded, sipping something that steams. He does not stand.

“Sit,” he says, in a voice like a furnace door opening. “You’ve read the report. You understand my position. Creation & Company intends to own the Nine Hells by the end of the year. Even Hell has antitrust concerns.” He sets down his cup. “I propose an alliance.”

DM Description

Vellichor offers an alliance against Tallis Vend: Nine Circles will vote against the Final Acquisition (S23), block the road through Avernus (S22) and lend Ixabeth to the party at the AGM (S20). In exchange: the party carries the report, and—small print—grants Nine Circles “first refusal” on any franchise the party ever owns.

The party can accept, refuse or negotiate. If they refuse, he offers a smaller deal: his vote in S23 in exchange for the report reaching the Counting House.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-08.controlled-by]{Duke Malphas Vellichor}. Enormous, calm, reasonable—terrifyingly so. He never threatens. He states facts. He keeps every bargain to the letter.

Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.dobbs]{Dobbs}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.clerk-of-the-first-sale]{The Clerk of the First Sale}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-01]{Hollis Quench}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S14]{The First Entry}

Synopsis

Hollis Quench calls the party: the iron door in THAC0 Spell’s cellar—sealed since before the party’s first job, the one Dobbs went missing near—is open. Beyond it, stairs go down for too long. And at the bottom, behind a counter, stands Dobbs, the missing line cook, calm and blank, serving customers.

The First Shop is every shop: a counter, a scale, a till, a bell. Customers who have waited centuries queue patiently. Ghostly clerks from every era work behind the counter. They are not hostile. They will serve the party. But buying anything means signing.

Behind the counter, on a lectern, is a page torn from the Grand Ledger’s first volume: Entry 1. Tallis Vend owns Tallis Vend, in perpetuity. Witnessed by: Tallis Vend. The party can take it—and four Compliance Officers will come for it. Beyond the lectern is a grey door marked STAFF ONLY. Behind it, a quill scratches.

Background — DM Only

Four hundred years ago a mortal clerk named Tallis Vend kept the books at the first shop: the first place where something was bought and sold. One night he wrote himself into the shop’s ledger as its owner, and himself as his own witness. That self-witnessed entry became the foundation of the Grand Ledger and of Creation & Company.

The First Shop never closed. Its customers are the first people ever to be sold something; they are waiting for change. The clerks are every shop worker who ever signed a contract of employment with a Company subsidiary and died in service.

Dobbs wandered through the door on the party’s first night at THAC0 Spell (S01) and took a shift. He has been working for what feels to him like an afternoon.

Running This Mission

  • This is the campaign’s quietest, eeriest mission. Slow everything down. No music.
  • The Clerk of the First Sale is the shop’s conscience, not a boss monster. Fight only if the party is careless.
  • Buying anything means signing: make it clear the moment anyone reaches for a coin.
  • The Staff Only door cannot be opened yet. Let them hear the quill.

Threads In and Out

  • In: the iron door and Dobbs (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S01]{S01}).
  • Out: the party knows where the Counting House is; the Staff Only door opens in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S20]{S20}; Entry 1 is the key to @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S24]{S24}.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Hollis Quench sounds strange on the speaking-stone: not panicked, but hushed, as if afraid of being overheard in his own kitchen. “The door’s open,” he says. “The iron one. In the cellar. I went down to fetch a keg and it was just… open.” A long pause. “There are stairs. I didn’t go down. But I could hear a bell. A shop bell. And Dobbs. I heard Dobbs say, ‘Next, please.’”

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

THAC0 Spell’s cellar is as you remember it: kegs, crates, the smell of old ale and dragon-pepper. But at the far end, the iron door—the door that has been rusted shut since the tavern was built—stands open a hand’s width. Cold air breathes through the gap. It smells of dust, old coins and candle-wax.

Beyond, a stone staircase spirals down. You count a hundred steps before you lose sight of it. Far below, so faint you are not sure you heard it, a small bell rings: ting.

DM Description

The stairs go down for too long: roughly an hour of descent, though only a few minutes pass above. Time behaves oddly—each hour below is a minute above.

Along the walls, carved into the stone, are tally marks: millions of them, the oldest worn smooth.

The stairs

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The stairs end in a room that is every shop you have ever been in. A wooden counter, worn into a dip by centuries of elbows. A brass scale. A till with a crank. A bell on a spring above the door. Shelves of jars and bolts of cloth and loaves and lamps, all faintly translucent, like memories of goods.

A queue stretches from the counter, out of the room and into the dark: men and women in clothes from every century, holding coins, waiting patiently. At the counter, wearing a THAC0 Spell apron, stands Dobbs. He looks well. He looks calm. He looks right through you.

“Next, please,” he says.

DM Description

The customers are the first people ever sold something. They are waiting for change, and have been for centuries. They will talk, softly, if spoken to: about the price of bread, about a town long gone.

Dobbs believes he started his shift an hour ago. He is under the shop’s spell; he will serve the party courteously and does not recognise them. He can be freed (see Twist): if someone pays for his shift with a coin that means something to them.

Features of the Area

The counter
Worn; behind it, the lectern and the Staff Only door.
The scale
Weighs whatever is placed on it—including a soul.
The queue
Endless.
The bell
Rings when anyone enters or leaves. Every ring is a sale.

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.dobbs]{Dobbs}. Polite, calm, blank. Responds to THAC0 Spell orders by habit: “one pepper-mash, extra crit”. A flicker of recognition if someone uses his nickname or mentions Hollis.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

From the back of the shop come the clerks: dozens of them, pale and translucent, in uniforms from every age—a Murder King paper crown, a Wand-Mart blue vest, a medieval guild apron, a Starkfucks green one. They are not hostile. They are busy. They smile the same tired smile.

An old, old clerk in a black coat steps to the counter, ink-stained fingers folded. “Welcome,” says the Clerk of the First Sale. “What can I get you?”

DM Description

The clerks will serve the party anything they ask for—a memory, a lost thing, a future—at a price. Buying anything means signing: the purchase is entered in the shop’s ledger, binding the buyer to the Company. (A purchase made here gives a real boon of the DM’s choice—and a real Ledger entry that Tallis Vend can use in S24.)

The Clerk of the First Sale was Tallis Vend’s apprentice. He saw what Vend wrote and said nothing. He has stood behind this counter for four centuries out of guilt.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.clerk-of-the-first-sale]{The Clerk of the First Sale}. Courteous, ancient, sorrowful. Tells the truth if asked directly. He will not stop the party from taking the page, but the shop will.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Behind the counter, under a single candle, stands a lectern of black wood. On it lies a single page, torn from a very large book: yellowed, brittle, written in a small, precise hand. You lean close to read it.

Entry 1. Tallis Vend owns Tallis Vend, in perpetuity. Witnessed by: Tallis Vend.

As you read, the candle flame bends toward you, and somewhere far away, a bell rings that is not the shop bell.

DM Description

Taking the page triggers the shop’s defence: four Compliance Officers step out of the walls. The Clerk of the First Sale, weakened (lich statistics at half hp, no legendary actions), defends the lectern only if the party threatens the customers or Dobbs; otherwise he steps aside—“I said nothing once. I will say nothing again.”

The page is the First Entry, the Receipt: proof that Creation & Company’s founding act was a circular claim that no one else witnessed.

The lectern

Behind the lectern is a second door: plain, grey, flush with the wall, without a handle. A small brass plate reads STAFF ONLY. You press your ear to it. On the other side, very faint, very steady, a quill is scratching—line after line after line, never pausing.

The Staff Only door opens onto the Counting House, but not yet: it has no handle until the party is invited (S20). Nothing opens it now—not knock, not force, not wish.

Dobbs can be freed before leaving if someone pays for his shift with a coin that means something to them (a first wage, a lucky penny, a gift). The Clerk accepts it, rings the till, and says: “Shift over.” Dobbs blinks, sees the party, and starts to cry.

pages.name: DM Overview
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Mission at a Glance

Code / ActS15 · Act III
Grade / LevelPlatinum · Level 12
Client@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-02]{Murder King} (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-03]{Crown & Cleaver})
Session length1–2 sessions; a tower siege and a three-way showdown; ends Act III
Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S15|Scene 1 — The Throne Tower]{Scene 1 — The Throne Tower} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-32-throne-tower-boardroom]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S15|Scene 2 — The Revenant King]{Scene 2 — The Revenant King} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-32-throne-tower-boardroom]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S15|Scene 3 — Baron Cleave]{Scene 3 — Baron Cleave} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-32-throne-tower-boardroom]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S15|Scene 4 — The Choice]{Scene 4 — The Choice} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-32-throne-tower-boardroom]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S15|Scene 5 — Aftermath]{Scene 5 — Aftermath} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-33-revenant-kings-crypt]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.aldric-the-unkind]{King Aldric the Unkind}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-03.controlled-by]{Baron Ossian Cleave}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S15]{Aldric’s Testimony}

Synopsis

Veronique Salt calls in a panic: “He’s in the Throne Tower. He’s eating everyone.” King Aldric the Unkind—the original Murder King, murdered four centuries ago by his steward, Ossian Cleave—has risen as a revenant, wearing the Promotional Crown from S05. He has fought his way to the top floor of Crown & Cleaver headquarters and is eating executives.

Aldric is proud, cruel and correct: his kingdom was stolen, his face turned into a mascot, his murder made into a brand. He demands his kingdom back and Cleave’s death. Then Baron Ossian Cleave—a death knight, controller of Crown & Cleaver—arrives with his guards, intending to kill Aldric and every witness.

The party can ally with Aldric against Cleave, stop both, or broker a deal: Aldric gets his revenge and relinquishes his claim. Veronique wants Cleave dead so she can take his seat; she helps—until she doesn’t.

Background — DM Only

Four hundred years ago Aldric was king of the land where Brandmere now stands: cruel, vain, and lawful. His steward, Ossian Cleave, murdered him with a meat cleaver at the royal feast and sold the kingdom—its land, its crown, its very name—to Tallis Vend in exchange for a Board seat and undeath. The Murder King brand was built from Aldric’s face as a joke.

Revenants rise to avenge a wrong. Aldric rose when the Promotional Crown (his real crown, recast as merchandise) was worn in the Throne Tower—an event the party may have triggered in S05.

Veronique has spent years undermining Cleave. If he is destroyed, Crown & Cleaver loses its Board seat and she becomes CEO.

Running This Mission

  • Aldric is not a misunderstood hero. He was a bad king. He is still right.
  • Cleave is the true villain of the piece: courteous, cold, and utterly without remorse.
  • Veronique’s turn should be telegraphed: she helps against Cleave until Aldric wins, then tries to kill Aldric to end the claim.
  • If the Rabbit Rating reaches five stars here, go straight to S16.

Threads In and Out

  • In: the Promotional Crown and the Vault Inventory (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S05]{S05}); Veronique’s partnership (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S10]{S10}).
  • Out: end of Act III; Crown & Cleaver’s seat in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S23]{S23}; Aldric as a witness in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S24]{S24}.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Veronique Salt has never sounded like this. Her voice on the speaking-stone is high and quick and there is screaming behind it. “He’s in the Throne Tower,” she says. “The king. The real one. He’s wearing the crown and he’s—” a crash, a wet sound— “he’s eating everyone. Budget unlimited. Come now. Please.”

Then, more quietly, almost to herself: “Cleave’s on his way. Get there first.”

pages.name: Scene 1 — The Throne Tower
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-32-throne-tower-boardroom]{The Throne Tower (lower floors → boardroom)}
When: Night
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.wight]{risen executives (wights)}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.helmed-horror]{tower security}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S15|Throne Tower Evacuation Notice]{Throne Tower Evacuation Notice} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S15|Throne Tower Evacuation Notice]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Throne Tower is Crown & Cleaver’s headquarters: forty storeys of black glass and gold, shaped like a crown, its spires lit red. Tonight the red light is flickering. Executives in torn suits are fleeing out of the revolving doors into the square. One of them has a bite out of his shoulder. Another is not fleeing; he is shuffling, grey-faced, eyes glowing, back toward the tower.

Veronique meets you at the doors, her crimson coat spattered with something dark. “Top floor,” she says. “The boardroom. He’s turning them as he eats them. Go.”

DM Description

A siege up the tower. Aldric’s victims rise as wights (risen executives) and hold the stairs. Tower security (helmed horrors) is malfunctioning: they attack anything that isn’t wearing a Crown & Cleaver lanyard.

Run it as three short floors: Marketing (wights among mascot costumes), Accounts (a helmed horror; filing cabinets for cover), Executive (a corridor of portraits of Cleave through the centuries—and one of Aldric, with the face scratched out).

Features of the Area

Lifts
Stopped. The stairs are the only way up.
Mascot costumes
Murder King suits; a wight hides in one.
Portrait gallery
Cleave in every century, never ageing.
Lanyards
Wearing a C&C lanyard makes the helmed horrors ignore you.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}. Shaken, then very quickly composed. She comes with the party, staying behind them, and helps. She wants Aldric to kill Cleave, and then Aldric to die.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult

Studying the portraits[[/check skill=his dc=15]] @FWCheck[S15|skill=his dc=15|Study the portrait gallery]{Request}Cleave was Aldric’s steward. The scratched face is the king.
Climbing fast[[/save ability=con dc=14]] @FWSave[S15|ability=con dc=14|Forty storeys of stairs]{Request}Failure: a level of exhaustion.

Developments

  • The boardroom doors are ahead.

Scaling & Pacing

Level 12: 6 wights across the floors; 2 helmed horrors.

pages.name: Scene 2 — The Revenant King
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a3-32-throne-tower-boardroom]{Open battlemap}
When: The top floor
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.aldric-the-unkind]{King Aldric the Unkind}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S15|Decree of King Aldric]{Decree of King Aldric} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S15|Decree of King Aldric]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The boardroom has been redecorated. The long table is overturned and dragged to the head of the room to make a dais. The chairs are piled into a throne. On the throne sits a figure in rotted royal robes, gaunt and grey, with burning eyes and a crown of gold that you have seen before—in a vault, on a velvet cushion, labelled PROMOTIONAL.

He is eating. He stops. He looks at you, and wipes his mouth with the back of a hand.

“More of Cleave’s servants,” says King Aldric the Unkind. “Kneel, or join the meal.”

DM Description

Aldric is proud, cruel and correct. He tells his story—he was murdered by his steward at his own feast, his kingdom sold, his face made a mascot—and makes his demands: his kingdom back, and Cleave’s death. He does not care how many people work here.

He can be talked to. He respects courage, despises grovelling, and will bargain with anyone who acknowledges that he was wronged. He will not relinquish his claim easily.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.aldric-the-unkind]{King Aldric the Unkind}. Regal, contemptuous, dangerous. He speaks like a king and expects to be addressed as one. He was never kind; he was always lawful. His one weakness: he wants his name back more than his kingdom.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Addressing him as king[[/check skill=per dc=17]] @FWCheck[S15|skill=per dc=17|Parley with the revenant king]{Request}He listens.
Understanding a revenant[[/check skill=rel dc=16]] @FWCheck[S15|skill=rel dc=16|What drives a revenant?]{Request}It cannot rest until its murderer is destroyed. After that, it will fade.
Spotting his weakness[[/check skill=ins dc=17]] @FWCheck[S15|skill=ins dc=17|What does Aldric really want?]{Request}His name restored, more than the throne.

Lines to Steal

Aldric: “Kneel, or join the meal.”
Aldric: “I was a bad king. I was still the king.”

Developments

  • Cleave arrives.

Scaling & Pacing

pages.html:

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The lift, which was stopped, chimes. The doors slide open, and Baron Ossian Cleave steps out: tall, armoured in black plate under a perfectly tailored coat, a meat cleaver the size of a greatsword across his back. He takes in the room—the throne of chairs, the bodies, the king—and inclines his head politely.

“Your Majesty,” he says. “Again.” Then, to you, without turning: “Thank you for containing him. You may go. You were never here.”

DM Description

Cleave intends to destroy Aldric and kill every witness—including the party, Veronique, and any surviving executives. He is a death knight with a hellfire orb and absolute confidence.

Now there are three sides: Aldric, Cleave and the party (with Veronique wavering). The party chooses.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-03.controlled-by]{Baron Ossian Cleave}. Courteous, cold, utterly without remorse. He refers to the murder as “the transaction”. He is not afraid of anything except the Ledger.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

For a moment nobody moves: the dead king on his throne of chairs, the murderer by the lift with his cleaver drawn, and you between them. Behind you, Veronique Salt says, very softly, “Choose.”

DM Description

The party’s options:

Ally with Aldric against Cleave. Two against one. When Cleave falls, Aldric’s purpose is fulfilled—and Veronique tries to kill the weakened king to end his claim. The party must stop her or let her.Stop both. A three-way fight. Hardest; most chaotic.Broker a deal. [[/check skill=per dc=19]] @FWCheck[S15|skill=per dc=19|Broker the king’s bargain]{Request} (advantage with the Vault Inventory or Cleave’s confession): Aldric gets his revenge on Cleave and relinquishes his claim to the kingdom and brand in exchange for his name restored—his testimony given freely. The party then helps (or watches) Aldric destroy Cleave.

If Cleave is destroyed, Crown & Cleaver loses its Board seat and Veronique becomes CEO.

Difficult terrain; collapsing it: [[/check skill=ath dc=16]] @FWCheck[S15|skill=ath dc=16|Topple the throne]{Request}.

High ground.

  • Aldric fades after vengeance, leaving his testimony.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The crypt beneath the Throne Tower was a royal tomb long before it was a basement: a vaulted chamber of old stone, with an empty sarcophagus carved with a king’s face—the real one, stern and unhandsome, not the cartoon on the burger boxes.

Aldric lowers himself onto the stone lid. The fire in his eyes is guttering. “Write it down,” he says. “All of it. My name, and what was done. Then let me sleep.”

DM Description

If Aldric’s vengeance is complete, he gives his testimony—the first acquired king, describing how his kingdom was sold—and fades. The party writes it down (the Receipt). He can return as a witness in S24 if called by name.

If Cleave is destroyed, Veronique is CEO of Crown & Cleaver by morning. She thanks the party, sincerely, and adds: “I’ll remember this.” She means both halves.

pages.name: DM Overview
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Mission at a Glance

Code / ActS16 · Act IV
Grade / LevelPlatinum · Level 13
Client@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-59]{Long Rest Inn} (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-08]{Nine Circles Hospitality})
Session length1 session; a mystery, a revelation, and a fight in a hotel corridor
Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S16|Scene 1 — The Room]{Scene 1 — The Room} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-v-inn-01-long-rest-inn]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S16|Scene 2 — The Sleepers]{Scene 2 — The Sleepers} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-34-long-rest-inn-room-303]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S16|Scene 3 — The Truth]{Scene 3 — The Truth} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-34-long-rest-inn-room-303]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S16|Scene 4 — The Compliance Officers]{Scene 4 — The Compliance Officers} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-v-inn-01-long-rest-inn]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S16|Scene 5 — The Choice]{Scene 5 — The Choice} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-35-sleepers-dream]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.cadwyn-lark]{Cadwyn Lark}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.tomas-brand]{Tomas Brand}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.ysolde-fenn]{Ysolde Fenn}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.hark]{Hark}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-02.public-face]{Harriet Hopwell}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S16]{The Five-Star Testimony}

Synopsis

Pip, nervous, hands over a contract printed on black card: “They said you’re the only ones qualified.” Room 303 of the Long Rest Inn has displayed DO NOT DISTURB for ninety-four years. Corporate wants it cleaned and the guests checked out.

Behind the door is a time-stop field, a century of dust, and four legendary heroes asleep: Cadwyn Lark, Tomas Brand, Ysolde Fenn and Hark—the Last Five-Star Party, the only adventurers before the party to reach five stars on QuestRabbit. They went to sleep rather than sign.

Cadwyn explains the truth: the Rabbit Rating measures public trust. At five stars, a party can sign for the commons. Every good deed brought the party closer. Then the Counting House notices the room has been opened, and Compliance Officers arrive to escort someone to the signing—the old heroes, or the new ones.

Background — DM Only

Clause 77-B of every QuestRabbit Contractor Agreement appoints any five-star party as Representatives of the Commons: authorised to sign on the world’s behalf. Harriet Hopwell built QuestRabbit believing she was helping adventurers; Tallis Vend built Clause 77-B into it. Ninety-four years ago the Last Five-Star Party reached five stars, saw the Final Contract and fled into Room 303.

Ysolde Fenn cast a time-stop sleep on the room. As long as they sleep, they cannot sign—and nobody else can reach five stars while their rating stands. Their rating has begun to decay. The party’s is rising. The Ledger needs only one five-star party.

The Long Rest Inn is Nine Circles’ hotel chain; its staff are bearded devils in bellhop uniforms.

Running This Mission

  • The reveal is the point. Let Cadwyn tell it, slowly.
  • Each of the four sleepers can be woken separately; each has a different reaction.
  • Make the corridor fight feel like an escort mission gone wrong: the Compliance Officers are not trying to kill, they are trying to take.
  • The Twist—passing signature authority—is a real decision.

Threads In and Out

  • In: QuestRabbit and Pip; the party’s Rabbit Rating; the Sleeper (Plane Inn, “@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-61.late-checkout]{Late Checkout}”).
  • Out: the party knows what it is; Harriet Hopwell can help if persuaded; the Last Five-Star Party’s allegiance for @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S24]{S24}.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Pip slides the contract across the table without looking at it. It is printed on heavy black card with silver letters, and he holds it by the very corner as if it might bite. “I’m not supposed to say,” he says. “But they said you’re the only ones qualified. On the whole system. Nobody else can even see the job.” His ears flatten. “Who else has ever been qualified for something like this?”

pages.name: Scene 1 — The Room
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-v-inn-01-long-rest-inn]{Long Rest Inn — third floor}
When: Evening
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-59]{the night manager}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.bearded-devil]{bellhops}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S16|Housekeeping Request — Room 303]{Housekeeping Request — Room 303} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S16|Housekeeping Request — Room 303]{Show to players} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S16|The Do Not Disturb Card]{The Do Not Disturb Card} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S16|The Do Not Disturb Card]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Long Rest Inn is plush and very quiet: thick red carpets, brass lamps, a lobby that smells of lavender and sulphur. The bellhops are bearded devils in pillbox hats who carry luggage as if it weighed nothing and smile with too many teeth.

The third floor corridor ends at a door unlike the others. The paint is a century out of date. The brass numbers—3 0 3—are green with age. On the handle hangs a card, its ink faded to brown: DO NOT DISTURB. Dust lies on the carpet before it in a perfect drift, untouched, a finger deep.

DM Description

The night manager briefs the party: ninety-four years; no room service; housekeeping has tried everything; three staff aged forty years in a second trying to force the door. The door is held by a time-stop field.

Getting in requires a counterspell or dispel magic against 9th level (DC 19), a wish, or Cadwyn’s song (from the side contract Authenticity Guaranteed): singing it through the keyhole makes the field part.

Features of the Area

The door
Time-stop field: touching it, [[/save ability=con dc=18]] @FWSave[S16|ability=con dc=18|The field brushes your hand]{Request} or age [[/r 1d10]] years.
The dust
Undisturbed for a century; a tiny footprint, weeks old (Pip’s—he came to look).
Room 302 and 304
Both empty and booked “indefinitely” by QuestRabbit.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult

Spotting Pip’s footprint[[/check skill=prc dc=16]] @FWCheck[S16|skill=prc dc=16|Study the dust]{Request}Pip was here. He is more scared than he admits.

Developments

pages.name: Scene 2 — The Sleepers
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-34-long-rest-inn-room-303]{Open battlemap}
When: Inside Room 303
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.cadwyn-lark]{Cadwyn Lark}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.tomas-brand]{Tomas Brand}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.ysolde-fenn]{Ysolde Fenn}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.hark]{Hark}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S16|The Last Five-Star Party’s Rating Card]{The Last Five-Star Party’s Rating Card} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S16|The Last Five-Star Party’s Rating Card]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The room is frozen in a single moment. A candle on the nightstand burns with a flame that does not flicker. Dust hangs in the air in a sunbeam from a window that shows a sky ninety-four years old. And on the beds and chairs, four people sleep.

A half-elf with a lute across her chest, her lips still parted mid-song. A grey-bearded human in a paladin’s plate, sitting upright in a chair with a sword across his knees. An old woman in star-embroidered robes, a wand slipping from her fingers. A lean ranger curled by the window, one eye half-open, as if keeping watch even in sleep.

On the dresser, in a frame, is a QuestRabbit rating card: five gold stars.

DM Description

The Last Five-Star Party. They can be woken one at a time (touch them and speak their names; each wakes with a gasp).

Cadwyn Lark (bard) wakes first and best: she understands immediately and starts talking. Tomas Brand (paladin) wakes reaching for his sword. Ysolde Fenn (wizard) wakes furious: waking ends her spell, and she is very old now. Hark (ranger) wakes silently and is already at the window watching for what will come.

Features of the Area

The frozen candle
Starts burning once Ysolde wakes; when it gutters, the Counting House knows.
Dust in the air
Falls all at once when Ysolde wakes.
The rating card
Five stars, dated ninety-four years ago.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.cadwyn-lark]{Cadwyn Lark}. Warm, wry, quick; a storyteller who has had nearly a century to rehearse this.
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.tomas-brand]{Tomas Brand}. Grave, honourable, guilty: he wanted to stay and fight.
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.ysolde-fenn]{Ysolde Fenn}. Sharp, imperious, frightened of how old she has become.
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.hark]{Hark}. Silent; speaks only to warn.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Waking a sleeper gently[[/check skill=med dc=13]] @FWCheck[S16|skill=med dc=13|Wake a sleeper gently]{Request}They wake without panic.
Recognising them[[/check skill=his dc=16]] @FWCheck[S16|skill=his dc=16|Who are these people?]{Request}The Last Five-Star Party: the most famous adventurers of the last century, vanished.

Developments

  • Cadwyn tells the truth.

Scaling & Pacing

pages.name: Scene 3 — The Truth
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-34-long-rest-inn-room-303]{Open battlemap}
When: As the candle burns
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.cadwyn-lark]{Cadwyn Lark}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.last-five-star-party]{the Last Five-Star Party}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S16|Clause 77-B (Contractor Agreement)]{Clause 77-B (Contractor Agreement)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S16|Clause 77-B (Contractor Agreement)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Cadwyn sits on the edge of the bed, strokes the strings of her lute once to see if they still work, and looks at you for a long moment.

“How many stars?” she asks. When you tell her, she closes her eyes. “Then you’re nearly there. I’m sorry. Let me tell you what the stars are for.”

DM Description

Cadwyn explains: the Rabbit Rating measures public trust. Every five-star review, every rescued cat, every grateful client is a vote. At five stars, under Clause 77-B, a party becomes Representatives of the Commons and can sign for everyone. The Final Contract needs that signature. Ninety-four years ago it was theirs. They saw the contract and chose to sleep rather than sign or be made to sign.

She tells the party what they saw at the Counting House (the AGM; their names on the line). And she says: “Every good deed you did brought you closer. That’s the cruelty of it. It was meant to.”

The four will testify to this: the Five-Star Testimony, the Receipt.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Understanding the mandate[[/check skill=ins dc=14]] @FWCheck[S16|skill=ins dc=14|Understand what the Rating really is]{Request}You are a mandate.
Taking the testimony[[/check skill=his dc=13]] @FWCheck[S16|skill=his dc=13|Record the testimony formally]{Request} (or Investigation)A complete, signed testimony.

Lines to Steal

Cadwyn: “Every good deed you did brought you closer. That’s the cruelty of it. It was meant to.”
Tomas: “We ran. I’ve regretted it every second of ninety-four years.”

Developments

  • The candle gutters. The Counting House knows.

pages.name: Scene 4 — The Compliance Officers
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-v-inn-01-long-rest-inn]{Long Rest Inn — third-floor corridor and stairs}
When: The moment the candle gutters
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.compliance-officer]{Compliance Officers}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.senior-auditor]{a Senior Auditor}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.bearded-devil]{bellhop devils}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S16|Escort Order]{Escort Order} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S16|Escort Order]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Every door along the corridor opens at once. From every room step figures in grey suits with grey faces and lanyards with no names, carrying clipboards. At the far end of the hall, the lift chimes, and something enormous ducks out of it: a towering figure of ledger-grey stone with an abacus for a chest, its beads clicking.

“Representatives,” says the Senior Auditor, in a voice like a vault door. “Your escort has arrived.”

DM Description

The Counting House sends four Compliance Officers and a Senior Auditor to escort “the Representatives” to the signing. They will take whichever five-star party they can—the old heroes or the new ones. The Long Rest Inn’s bellhop devils join them (staff obey corporate).

The Officers try to grapple and carry; anyone grappled and carried to the lift is taken to the Counting House (they return, shaken, an hour later—unsigned this time, because the Final Contract isn’t ready). The Last Five-Star Party fights beside the party if woken: but they are ninety-four years out of practice (each has half hp).

Features of the Area

The corridor
Long, narrow, red carpet; doors on both sides.
The lift
The Auditor’s exit.
The stairs
Down to the lobby; bellhops come up.
Laundry chute
A quick way down: [[/save ability=dex dc=14]] @FWSave[S16|ability=dex dc=14|Slide down the laundry chute]{Request}.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Breaking a grapple[[/check skill=ath dc=17]] @FWCheck[S16|skill=ath dc=17|Break free of a Compliance Officer]{Request}Free.
Objecting formally[[/check skill=per dc=18]] @FWCheck[S16|skill=per dc=18|Object to the escort on procedural grounds]{Request}One Officer pauses for a round to consult its clipboard.

Developments

  • Survive, hold the corridor, or escape the inn.

Scaling & Pacing

Level 13: 4 COs + Senior Auditor + 4 bearded devils. Weak: no Auditor. Strong: 6 COs.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

When it is over, Ysolde Fenn sits down heavily on the stairs, her robes grey with dust, and laughs without humour. “Well,” she says. “We’re awake now. That was the only thing we were good at—being asleep.”

Cadwyn looks at the four of them, and then at you. “There’s one more thing we can do,” she says. “We can give you our stars. All of them. Or we can keep them, and go back to sleep, and stand in your way.”

DM Description

The Last Five-Star Party can:

Go back to sleep (Ysolde can recast the spell once). Their rating stands; the party’s cannot reach a full five—but the Ledger will find a way (S20).Pass their signature authority to the party. The party becomes the only Representatives—and gains the old heroes as allies and witnesses for S24.Refuse to pass it and fight beside the party as equals.

Optionally, the Sleeper’s dream (Plane Inn, Room 13) can be entered from here—a vision of the Third Place.

Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S17|Scene 1 — The Way In]{Scene 1 — The Way In} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-v-retail-12-ikea-mimic]{map}

@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S17|Scene 5 — The Site Office Folio]{Scene 5 — The Site Office Folio} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-37-third-place-construction-site]{map}
Key NPCsHealing, Courage, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.gerrit-hask]{Foreman Gerrit Hask}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-04.controlled-by]{Ulth’Arabica}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S17]{The Third Place Folio}

Synopsis

ABI, reeling from S11 and S12, still needs contractors, and QuestRabbit hires the party on autopilot. Or Healing itself leaves a donut hole on the party’s pillow with a note: “Help.” Starkfucks is building a branch in the Third Place.

The Third Place is grey: a café that goes on forever, with tables of lost things arranged by acquisition date. The party finds items from their own past—taken by the Ledger as “onboarding consideration” when they signed their first QuestRabbit agreement. Every hour, the grey takes a proper noun.

In the grey live the exiled concepts: Healing, Weekends, Courage, Sleep and Rest. ABI’s crews are building a Starkfucks around a pillar of compressed concepts, overseen by a thrall of Ulth’Arabica. In the site office is a Folio listing everything in the Third Place. Writing “owned by nobody” beside a name frees it—at a cost in blood.

Background — DM Only

The Third Place is where Creation & Company keeps what it owns but does not use: concepts, places, people, small treasured things. It is not home, not work: the place between, drained of colour and name.

ABI’s “Branch 1 of ∞” is an attempt to make the Third Place profitable—to sell coffee to everything that has been forgotten—by grinding concepts into bricks. Ulth’Arabica watches through its thrall, the site foreman Gerrit Hask.

If Healing was freed in S12, it has been sheltering the others and knows a hidden exit to Plane Inn’s Room 13, where the Sleeper waits.

Running This Mission

  • Drain colour from your descriptions as the session goes on. End in greyscale.
  • The proper-noun save is a player-facing horror: players pick which name they lose. Write them down.
  • The concepts are gentle, frail and funny. Courage hiding is a joke that becomes moving.
  • The Folio choice is a resource problem: hit points for freedom.

Threads In and Out

  • In: Healing (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S12]{S12}); ABI after @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11]{S11}; the Sleeper (“@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-61.late-checkout]{Late Checkout}”); IKEA Mimic (“@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-68.assembly-required]{Assembly Required}”); Dungeon Donuts (“@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-12.the-hole-problem]{The Hole Problem}”).
  • Out: Ulth’Arabica has seen the party; the Board considers the party a threat; concept boons for @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S24]{S24}; the chase in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S22]{S22}.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

You wake to find a donut hole on your pillow: a small, perfect sphere of fried dough, dusted with sugar, still warm. Beneath it, a scrap of grey paper in very faint handwriting, as if written by someone with almost no strength left.

Help.

Within the hour, QuestRabbit sends an automatic job offer: Starkfucks Real Estate, Platinum grade, pocket-dimension site clearance. Pip has added a note at the bottom: “I didn’t send this. The system did. I don’t like it.”

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

There are three ways in. In the IKEA Mimic showroom, the back of a flat-pack wardrobe named GRÅVÄRLD opens onto nothing. In the storeroom of a Dungeon Donuts, there is a crack in the wall the exact shape of a donut hole. And on Corporate Row, overnight, a new Starkfucks door has appeared on a blank wall: grey, with a sign reading BRANCH 1 OF ∞ — COMING SOON.

Whichever you choose, the moment you step through, the colour drains out of you like water from a sink. Your clothes go grey. Your skin goes grey. Your voice sounds further away.

DM Description

Choose an entrance (or let the party). Each leads to a different edge of the grey café: the wardrobe to the furniture district (lost homes), the donut crack to the concepts’ refuge, the Starkfucks door to the construction site.

From the first step, every hour, each creature makes [[/save ability=wis dc=15]] @FWSave[S17|ability=wis dc=15|The grey takes a name]{Request} or forgets one proper noun until they leave (the player chooses: a friend’s name, their god, their home town, their own surname).

Features of the Area

GRÅVÄRLD wardrobe
From “@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-68.assembly-required]{Assembly Required}”: assembled correctly, it opens; incorrectly, it eats a hand ([[/save ability=dex dc=15]] @FWSave[S17|ability=dex dc=15|Snatch your hand back]{Request}).
The donut crack
From “@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-12.the-hole-problem]{The Hole Problem}”: only fits if you hold a donut hole.
Branch 1 of ∞
Opens to anyone with an ABI contractor badge.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

It is a café that goes on forever. Grey tables, grey chairs, grey cups on grey saucers, in rows that vanish into a grey haze in every direction. There is no counter. There is no barista. There is only the faint smell of coffee that has gone cold, and the sound of a spoon stirring somewhere far away.

Every table holds things. A child’s wooden horse. A wedding ring. A letter tied with string. A pair of boots. A key. Each has a small grey card beside it, and on each card, a date and a word: ACQUIRED.

DM Description

The tables are arranged by acquisition date. Searching the right era, each character can find something of their own: a toy, a letter, a keepsake, a memory, taken by the Ledger when they signed their first QuestRabbit agreement as “onboarding consideration”.

Retrieving one’s own item grants inspiration and restores one proper noun lost to the grey. It also makes the item’s colour return—a single point of colour in all that grey.

Tables of lost things

The spoon sound
Following it leads to the concepts.

pages.name: Scene 3 — The Concepts
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-36-third-place-grey-cafe]{The concepts’ table}
When: Deeper in
Present: Healing, Weekends, Courage, Sleep, Rest
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S17|The Concepts’ Table]{The Concepts’ Table} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S17|The Concepts’ Table]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

At a table a little apart from the others sit five figures who are not quite people. One is thin, kind and very tired, with gentle hands: Healing. One is slumped with its head on the table, wearing slippers: Weekends. One is asleep in its chair, breathing slowly: Sleep. One, translucent and stiff, sits very still as if it has been told to: Rest. And under the table, trembling, hiding behind a chair leg, is Courage.

Healing looks up and smiles at you. “You came,” it says. “I hoped. That was the last of my hope.”

DM Description

The concepts explain in soft voices: they were bought and stored here. Without them, the world has had less of each—less rest, worse sleep, shorter weekends, fragile courage. ABI is grinding the others into bricks for its pillar.

Healing is grateful (and weak, if not freed in S12). Weekends is exhausted. Sleep dozes and talks in its sleep. Rest was sold by Nine Circles. Courage asks the party to lend it some: any creature that does gains advantage on saves against being frightened for the rest of the mission—and Courage comes out from under the table.

Playing the NPCs

Healing. Gentle, generous, frail. If freed in S12 it knows the hidden exit to Plane Inn, Room 13.
Courage. Terrified—the joke is the point. Becomes brave when someone is brave for it.
Weekends. Groans; wants a lie-in; surprisingly good at stalling time.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Comforting Courage[[/check skill=per dc=14]] @FWCheck[S17|skill=per dc=14|Lend Courage some of your own]{Request}Courage stands; advantage vs. fear for the mission.
Waking Sleep[[/check skill=med dc=15]] @FWCheck[S17|skill=med dc=15|Rouse Sleep (gently)]{Request}Sleep tells you, sleepily, where the site office is.

Lines to Steal

Healing: “You came. That was the last of my hope.”
Courage: “I’m not hiding. I’m… strategically elsewhere.”

Developments

  • To the construction site.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Out of the grey rises scaffolding: a skeleton of timber and iron around a pillar of something that glows faintly—a hundred colours pressed so tight they look like grey. Stone golems in hard hats lay bricks cut from it, one by one, building the walls of a café. A sign on the scaffold reads: STARKFUCKS — BRANCH 1 OF ∞ — NOW HIRING (ETERNALLY).

On the top platform stands a man in a high-visibility tabard with a clipboard. His eyes are milky white. When he speaks, a second voice speaks beneath his—wet, vast and very old. “Contractors. You were supposed to clear the tenants.”

DM Description

A fight on scaffolding over nothing. The foreman, Gerrit Hask, is a thrall of Ulth’Arabica (knight statistics; the aboleth can cast dominate person through him once). Four stone golems are the construction crew. Two grey concept-eaters—wraith-like things that feed on concepts—guard the pillar.

Stopping the build means defeating or freeing Hask, toppling the scaffolding or reaching the site office.

Features of the Area

Scaffolding
Three levels; falling off: into the grey—[[/save ability=wis dc=16]] @FWSave[S17|ability=wis dc=16|Find your way back from the grey]{Request} or lost for 1d4 rounds (roll [[/r 1d4]]).
The pillar
Compressed concepts; touching it shows a vision of everything the world has lost.
Cranes
Swinging a crane load: [[/check skill=ath dc=17]] @FWCheck[S17|skill=ath dc=17|Swing the crane]{Request}, 4d10 bludgeoning in a line.
Site office
A portable cabin at the base; the Folio inside.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Breaking the thrall[[/check skill=arc dc=18]] @FWCheck[S17|skill=arc dc=18|Break Ulth’Arabica’s hold on Hask]{Request} (or dispel/remove curse)Hask collapses, free; the aboleth sees who did it.
Talking to Ulth’Arabica[[/check skill=ins dc=18]] @FWCheck[S17|skill=ins dc=18|Read the aboleth through its thrall]{Request}It wants to own memory itself. It will remember you.

Developments

  • To the site office.

Scaling & Pacing

Level 14: Hask + 4 stone golems + 2 concept-eaters (wraiths, 150 hp, Annihilating Aura 1d6). Weak: 2 golems.

pages.name: Scene 5 — The Site Office Folio
pages.html:
GM ONLY

When: After the fight
Present: the concepts
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S17|The Third Place Folio (excerpt)]{The Third Place Folio (excerpt)} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S17|The Third Place Folio (excerpt)]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The site office is a portable cabin with a desk, a kettle, a calendar for a year that never happened, and a grey book open on the desk. It is a Folio: a page of the Grand Ledger, delegated to this site. Its lines run on and on, page after page: Healing — concept — held. Weekends — concept — held. The River Brande (upper) — place — held. Molly Fairweather’s first word — memory — held…

DM Description

Writing “owned by nobody” against a name frees it. Each line costs the writer 1 hit point per level of the thing freed—a concept counts as level 10 (10 hp), a place 5, a person 3, a memory 1. Hit points spent this way cannot be healed until the party leaves the Third Place.

The party chooses what to free with the time and blood they have. Each freed concept grants a boon usable once in S24: Healing (every creature regains 50 hp), Courage (immunity to fear), Sleep (one Compliance Officer falls asleep), Weekends (an extra round in the clause debate), Rest (a short rest in a moment).

If Healing was freed in S12, it knows a hidden exit that drops the party into Plane Inn’s Room 13, where the Sleeper waits.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Writing a line[[/save ability=con dc=14]] @FWSave[S17|ability=con dc=14|Pay the Folio in blood]{Request}Success: the cost is as listed. Failure: double.

Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-11]{Granny Quean}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.auntie-curdle]{Auntie Curdle}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-04]{Bettina Soft}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.the-mother-culture]{The Mother Culture}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S18]{Sample Zero}

Synopsis

Bettina Soft calls in hysterics: every cube in the Canal Street Creamery is humming the freezer’s lullaby, and the gelato is crawling out of the display. Across Brandmere, every Sweet Covenant shop is leaking. Desserts are going home.

Home is the Deep Dairy, beneath the Dairy Quean farm, where the Mother Culture—a primordial ooze, the starter of every dessert the Sweet Covenant ever sold—has woken. Granny Quean, the night hag who runs the Covenant, is trying to force Sample Zero, the first starter ever taken from the Mother, back into her to re-establish control.

The party herds the desserts through the city, bargains past Auntie Curdle at the glamoured farm, frees the workers taken by the Retention Clause in S03, and faces Granny Quean at the heart of the dairy. Then the Mother rises, and listens.

Background — DM Only

The Mother Culture was old when the first god woke. The Sweet Covenant’s founder—Granny Quean—stole a single starter from her, Sample Zero, and from it grew every gelato, donut, blizzard and cube in the portfolio. Granny kept the Mother asleep in the deep cold beneath her farm.

The Mother has woken because her children are being used up faster than ever: the Acquisition needs dessert in every corner of the Material Plane. She is calling them home. If Sample Zero is returned, she will be whole, and calm, and withdraw.

The Retention Clauses (S03) sent workers who “left” the Covenant down to the Deep Dairy to stir the vats forever.

Running This Mission

  • The Crawling City is slapstick horror: gelato oozing up gutters, donuts rolling like wheels, the city watch glazed and sticky.
  • Auntie Curdle is the hinge: desperate, funny, treacherous.
  • Granny Quean is charming and terrifying. Her offer—youth for service—should tempt.
  • The Mother should not be fought. Make her vast and patient. She listens.

Threads In and Out

  • In: Gelli, Bettina and Auntie Curdle (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S03]{S03}); the CostCo-op samples (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S09]{S09}).
  • Out: the Sweet Covenant breaks; the Board convenes emergency sessions; Hal Grundy calls about the dragons (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S19]{S19}).

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Bettina Soft’s voice comes through the speaking-stone in a shriek, over a strange sound—a low, sweet, many-voiced humming, like a choir of jellies. “They’re all humming!” she cries. “Every cube! The lullaby! The one the freezer plays! And the gelato’s—oh gods—the gelato’s getting out of the display! It’s going down the drain! It’s going home, it says! How can gelato say anything?!”

pages.name: Scene 1 — The Crawling City
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-38-crawling-city]{Open battlemap}
When: Morning, city-wide
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-04]{Bettina Soft}, the glazed city watch, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.gelli]{Gelli (if allied)}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S18|Sweet Covenant Continuity Alert]{Sweet Covenant Continuity Alert} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S18|Sweet Covenant Continuity Alert]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Brandmere is sticky. From every Sweet Covenant shop—Gelatinous Cube, Dairy Quean, Dungeon Donuts, Baskin Liches—desserts are pouring into the streets. Gelato oozes along the gutters in rivers of pistachio and raspberry. Donuts roll down the hills like cartwheels. A blizzard from a Dairy Quean drifts down Market Street, a small snowstorm with a spoon in it.

They all go the same way: down, toward the canals, toward the old docks, toward the farmland north of the city. And everywhere, softly, they hum.

The city watch is trying to stop them with swords. It isn’t working. Half the watch is glazed from Dungeon Donuts and keeps stopping to lick their blades.

DM Description

Run a city crisis in three short beats: the Creamery (Bettina, the humming cubes, Gelli if allied), Market Street (the blizzard and a crowd), the canals (where the desserts are heading).

The party can herd the desserts into the canals—they know the way home and will flow north through the old drainage to the Dairy Quean farm. Fighting them is pointless and messy. Gelli (if befriended in S03) can lead them, humming.

Features of the Area

Rivers of gelato
Difficult terrain; [[/save ability=dex dc=14]] @FWSave[S18|ability=dex dc=14|Don’t slip in the gelato]{Request} or fall prone.
Rolling donuts
Each round, roll [[/r 1d6]]: on 1–2, a donut stampede crosses the area (2d6 bludgeoning, [[/save ability=dex dc=15]] @FWSave[S18|ability=dex dc=15|Leap the donut stampede]{Request} halves).
The canals
Where the desserts go; the way north.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Herding the desserts[[/check skill=ani dc=15]] @FWCheck[S18|skill=ani dc=15|Herd the desserts toward the canals]{Request} (yes, Animal Handling)They flow toward the canals; the streets clear.
Calming the watch[[/check skill=per dc=14]] @FWCheck[S18|skill=per dc=14|Get the glazed watch to stand down]{Request}They stop attacking gelato.
Calming Bettina[[/check skill=ins dc=12]] @FWCheck[S18|skill=ins dc=12|Calm Bettina down]{Request}She blinks, finally. She tells you about the farm.

Developments

  • Everything is going north, to the Dairy Quean farm.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Dairy Quean farm sits on gentle hills north of the city: white fences, red barn, a pretty farmhouse with lace curtains, cows grazing that are slightly too perfect. And then the farmhouse flickers. For a heartbeat, where it stood is a sinkhole of churning cream, a hundred feet across, steaming with cold. Then it is a farmhouse again.

On the porch, in a rocking chair, sits a green-skinned hag in a frilled apron, knitting very fast. “Oh, it’s you,” says Auntie Curdle. “Thank goodness. I need protecting.”

DM Description

The farm’s glamour is failing: the farmhouse flickers into the sinkhole that leads to the Deep Dairy. Auntie Curdle (from S03) guards the way down. She is bargaining desperately: she’ll open the path in exchange for protection from Granny Quean, who blames her for the Mother’s waking.

She will betray the party to Granny if a better offer comes. If she sides with Granny in Scene 4, she fights.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.auntie-curdle]{Auntie Curdle}. Panicky, flattering, scheming, funny. Knits constantly (the knitting is a curse in progress). Will sell anyone for safety—including Granny, if the price is right.

Seeing through the glamour[[/check skill=inv dc=16]] @FWCheck[S18|skill=inv dc=16|See through the farm’s glamour]{Request}The sinkhole, the path down, and the cows (they are illusions over sheep).
Intimidating Curdle[[/check skill=itm dc=16]] @FWCheck[S18|skill=itm dc=16|Frighten Auntie Curdle]{Request}She opens the way—and runs to Granny.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The path spirals down through cold white rock into a cavern so large you cannot see its far wall. It is full of vats: vats the size of lakes, each brimming with living cream that moves slowly, as if breathing. Faces rise in the cream and sink again—faces of people, animals, things that never had faces—smiling, sleeping.

On walkways above the vats, workers in white overalls stir with long paddles, slowly, endlessly. Some have been stirring for years. One looks up as you pass, and you recognise the name embroidered on his overalls from a list you saw long ago: a Gelatinous Cube employee who “left”.

DM Description

The workers from S03’s Retention Clause are here, alive, stirring. Each freed worker is +1 Commons Tally. They are not chained—they are retained: the clause makes them unable to stop. A remove curse, the Retention Clauses Receipt, or a successful check frees one.

Ochre jellies guard the walkways (the vats’ “quality control”).

Features of the Area

The vats
Living cream; falling in: [[/save ability=con dc=16]] @FWSave[S18|ability=con dc=16|Resist the living cream]{Request} or be restrained and pulled under.
Walkways
Narrow, slippery.
Paddles
Long; usable as improvised reach weapons.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Freeing a worker[[/check skill=per dc=15]] @FWCheck[S18|skill=per dc=15|Talk a retained worker into stopping]{Request} (advantage with the Retention Clauses)They put down the paddle.
Reading the cream[[/check skill=arc dc=17]] @FWCheck[S18|skill=arc dc=17|Read the faces in the cream]{Request}Every dessert ever made, remembering being part of something.

Developments

  • Deeper, at the heart: Granny Quean.

Scaling & Pacing

Level 14–15: 4 ochre jellies across the walkways.

pages.name: Scene 4 — Granny Quean
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-40-deep-dairy]{The heart of the Deep Dairy}
When: Climax
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-11]{Granny Quean}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.auntie-curdle]{Auntie Curdle (if she turns)}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.black-pudding]{black puddings}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S18|Granny’s Offer]{Granny’s Offer} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S18|Granny’s Offer]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

At the heart of the dairy is a pool of cream wider than a town, glowing faintly blue from beneath. On a stone jetty above it stands a small, round, rosy-cheeked old woman in a frilled pinafore, holding a jar no bigger than a jam jar. Inside the jar something pale and alive turns slowly.

She is trying to pour it into the pool, and the pool is refusing: the cream pulls back from the jar like a child from medicine.

Granny Quean turns and smiles at you, the sweetest smile you have ever seen. “Visitors! Oh, how lovely. Come and help Granny, dears. Granny will make it worth your while.”

DM Description

Granny Quean (a night hag, 150 hp, casting as a 15th-level warlock: hold monster, dominate person, banishment) is trying to force Sample Zero back into the Mother to re-establish control. She offers each party member one day of their youth back per year they serve her.

If refused, she fights, with two black puddings rising from the pool and Auntie Curdle (if Curdle sided with her). Defeating or deposing Granny removes the Sweet Covenant’s Board vote.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-11]{Granny Quean}. Sweet, doting, and absolutely monstrous. Calls everyone “dear”. Never raises her voice. Her offers are real.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Resisting Granny’s offer[[/save ability=wis dc=17]] @FWSave[S18|ability=wis dc=17|Resist Granny’s offer of youth]{Request}You see the hag behind the smile.
Turning Curdle[[/check skill=per dc=17]] @FWCheck[S18|skill=per dc=17|Turn Auntie Curdle against Granny]{Request}Curdle hexes Granny mid-fight.
Taking the jar[[/check skill=slt dc=18]] @FWCheck[S18|skill=slt dc=18|Snatch Sample Zero from Granny]{Request} or [[/check skill=ath dc=18]] @FWCheck[S18|skill=ath dc=18|Wrestle the jar away]{Request}You hold Sample Zero.

Lines to Steal

Granny: “Come and help Granny, dears.”
Granny: “One day of youth for every year. Isn’t that generous?”

Developments

  • The Mother rises.

Scaling & Pacing

Weak: Granny at 100 hp; Curdle stays out.

pages.name: Scene 5 — The Mother
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-40-deep-dairy]{Open battlemap}

Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.the-mother-culture]{the Mother Culture}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S18|Sample Zero]{Sample Zero} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S18|Sample Zero]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The pool rises. Not a wave: the whole pool, lifting, slow and enormous, a wall of pale living cream that fills the cavern from floor to roof. Faces swim in it by the thousand. And then every face turns to look at you, and the Mother Culture speaks—through the pool, through the vats, through the gelato in the canals and every donut in Brandmere, all at once, in a voice so deep you feel it in your teeth.

“…child. You hold my child. Give it back.”

DM Description

The Mother Culture will listen. Returning Sample Zero makes her whole and calm: she withdraws beneath the earth, taking her children, and the Sweet Covenant’s product lines collapse overnight. The Deep Dairy empties. The freed workers walk out.

Destroying her is possible (see the Bestiary) but ends every dessert in the world forever, and she is the oldest living thing the party will ever meet.

Keeping Sample Zero (refusing the Mother) is possible: she sinks, grieving, and the party keeps the Receipt. Either way, the Mother offers a gift: one drop of Sample Zero, which dissolves any written contract it touches (see Twist).

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Speaking to the Mother[[/check skill=rel dc=17]] @FWCheck[S18|skill=rel dc=17|Address the Mother Culture]{Request} or NatureShe hears you as a person, not a dessert.
Withstanding her voice[[/save ability=con dc=15]] @FWSave[S18|ability=con dc=15|Withstand the Mother’s voice]{Request}Failure: deafened for an hour, and you dream of being cream.

Developments

  • The Sweet Covenant breaks.
