pages.name: Twist, Rewards & Aftermath
pages.html:
GM ONLY

The Twist

The Mother offers the party a gift: one drop of Sample Zero, which dissolves any written contract it touches. It can be used once in S24 to void any single clause without its Receipt.

Rewards

  • Bettina Soft’s grateful testimony; the freed workers; the Mother’s drop.
  • The Sweet Covenant’s Board vote is removed if Granny is defeated or deposed.

Receipt — @FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S18]{Sample Zero}

Sample Zero. The first starter taken from the Mother Culture. Proof that every product in Creation & Company’s portfolio began as something the Company never owned—and that nothing it holds is perpetual.Voids Clause 12 — Perpetuity in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.finalcontract]{the Final Contract}.

@FWReceipt[S18|fw.item.receipt.S18]{Award Receipt & announce}

Outcomes

If the party…Then…
returned Sample ZeroThe Mother withdraws; desserts vanish overnight; the party keeps a drop and a written record (the Receipt).
kept Sample ZeroThe Mother sinks, grieving; desserts remain, wild.
destroyed the MotherNo desserts, anywhere, ever. A heavy cost.

Forward

  • With ABI wounded and the Sweet Covenant broken, the Board convenes emergency sessions.
  • Hal Grundy of CostCo-op calls QuestRabbit: the dragons must meet in person.

Next mission: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S19]{S19 — Executive Membership}

@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S19|Scene 4 — The Motion]{Scene 4 — The Motion} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-41-crucible-dragon-boardroom]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S19|Scene 5 — The Vote]{Scene 5 — The Vote} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-41-crucible-dragon-boardroom]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-67]{Hal Grundy}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-10.controlled-by]{Auntie Vermillia}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.aurum]{Aurum}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.frostmother-ysk]{Frostmother Ysk}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.old-tar]{Old Tar}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.grandmother-slate]{Grandmother Slate}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.pyrrhax]{Pyrrhax}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S19]{The Board Minutes}

Synopsis

Hal Grundy, sweating, explains: the Counting House requires a quorum of the Hoard Syndicate’s owners to ratify its vote in the Final Acquisition. If the dragons don’t show, the Hoard’s vote defaults to Tallis Vend. If they do, the party gets a chance to speak.

The party delivers seven invitations—each a short scene: a riddle with Aurum, a bluff with the Twins, a gift for Frostmother Ysk, a legal notice for Old Tar. Grandmother Slate insists on seeing the party’s Rabbit Rating; Auntie Vermillia, the chair, must be persuaded to attend at all.

Then the party caters the meeting in the cleared CostCo-op warehouse—with dragonroot hidden in the gravy, if they dare—and moves that the Hoard Syndicate withdraw from the Final Acquisition. Robert’s Rules of Order among apex predators.

Background — DM Only

The Hoard Syndicate is seven ancient dragons who bought into Creation & Company for a share of everything. They have voted by proxy—through Auntie Vermillia—for four centuries, because dragons do not attend meetings. Hal Grundy has the bylaws: an in-person meeting overrides every proxy.

Each dragon has a grievance: Old Tar resents Vermillia; Aurum hates the whole business; Frostmother Ysk wants her youngest back from the Hoots & Owlbears farm; the Twins (Verdigris and Azhure) want whatever the other doesn’t; Grandmother Slate respects stars.

Dragonroot (@FWLink[Item|fw.item.magic.03]{Dragonroot}): each dose binds one dragon to whatever it says during the meeting.

Running This Mission

  • Seven invitations is a lot—run three or four in full and summarise the rest.
  • The meeting is a skill challenge with a parliamentary procedure. Hand out the Agenda.
  • Track votes openly on a board. Four carry the motion.
  • If Vermillia loses, she attacks; the others will not help her if the vote was fair.

Threads In and Out

  • In: the CostCo-op vault and Hal Grundy (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S09]{S09}); Pyrrhax (“@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-45.delivery-territory]{Delivery Territory}”, Dragon Express); Kessik’s royalty debt (“Finger-Lichin’ Good”); the Five Colours receipts.
  • Out: the Hoard’s proxy for @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S23]{S23}; dragons fly to the Golden Tusks in @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S21]{S21}.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Hal Grundy is sweating so hard his lanyard is wet. He has a binder under one arm, as thick as a paving slab, and he opens it on your table to a page flagged in red. “Bylaws,” he says. “Section forty. An extraordinary meeting of the executive board, in person, overrides all standing proxies.” He swallows. “They’ve never come. Four hundred years. If they don’t, their vote goes to the Chairman by default. If they do…” He looks at you. “You get to speak. I need seven invitations delivered. Personally. To seven ancient dragons. Please don’t be eaten. I’d have to do the paperwork.”

The invitations are thick cream card, gold-edged, sealed with the CostCo-op crest. Each is addressed in Hal Grundy’s best handwriting. The Executive Board of the Hoard Syndicate requests the honour of your presence…

Seven names. Seven lairs. Seven of the oldest and most dangerous creatures in the world, none of whom has opened a letter in four centuries.

DM Description

Each invitation is a short scene:

Aurum (gold) — a riddle at the door of a sunken temple: [[/check ability=int dc=17]] @FWCheck[S19|ability=int dc=17|Answer Aurum’s riddle]{Request}. He hates the business and attends only to say so.The Twins (green and blue) — a bluff: tell each the other has already accepted. The warehouse has been cleared of aisles. In the middle of the vast concrete floor stands a table built of shipping pallets, three hundred feet long, set for seven. Seven chairs the size of houses. Seven name cards. Kobolds in white aprons scurry about with trays. In the kitchen, a whole owlbear turns on a spit as big as a ship’s mast.

DM Description

The party runs catering: the Entire Roast Owlbear (or not, if they freed the owlbears in “Hoots & Owlbears”), the Potion Barrel, a mountain of gold-leaf pastries. Dragons judge hospitality harshly: a good table grants advantage on one meeting check.

If the party has dragonroot, they can hide it in the gravy. Each dose binds one dragon to whatever it says during the meeting. Being caught means disaster.

300 ft long.
The kitchen
Spit, ovens, the Potion Barrel.
Kobold staff
Loyal to Vermillia; spying.

pages.name: Scene 3 — The Meeting
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-41-crucible-dragon-boardroom]{The CostCo-op boardroom (warehouse floor)}
When: Noon
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-10.controlled-by]{Auntie Vermillia, Chair}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.aurum]{Aurum}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.frostmother-ysk]{Frostmother Ysk}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.old-tar]{Old Tar}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.grandmother-slate]{Grandmother Slate}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.verdigris]{the Twins}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.compliance-officer]{a Compliance Officer observer}
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S19|Agenda]{Agenda} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S19|Agenda]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

They come one by one, and the warehouse shakes with each arrival. A wind of fire through the loading bay: Auntie Vermillia, red and vast, wearing reading glasses on a chain. A gleam of gold: Aurum, already scowling. Frost spreads across the floor: Frostmother Ysk. A reek of the marsh: Old Tar. Twin shadows, green and blue, arguing as they land. And last, quietly, a silver dragon so old her scales are white, who looks at each of you in turn and counts your stars.

Vermillia lowers herself into the chair at the head of the table. She bangs a gavel made from a giant’s thighbone. “This extraordinary meeting of the Executive Board is called to order. Who moves?”

In the corner, a grey figure with a clipboard writes everything down.

DM Description

Robert’s Rules of Order among apex predators. Every dragon has a grievance (see Scene 1). Each speaks once on any motion. Insults are permitted; eating members is not (Section 12).

The Compliance Officer observer records the result and may try to annul it on a technicality (see Scene 5).

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-10.controlled-by]{Auntie Vermillia}. Grandmotherly, imperious, ruthless. Chairs like a tyrant. Has voted for all seven for four hundred years and enjoyed it.
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.aurum]{Aurum}. Disgusted by commerce; wants out; too proud to say so first.
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.old-tar]{Old Tar}. Procedural, petty, delighted by points of order.
@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.grandmother-slate]{Grandmother Slate}. Kind, grave; votes with the stars.

“The chair recognises the… caterers,” says Vermillia, with enormous distaste.

DM Description

The party moves that the Hoard Syndicate withdraw from the Final Acquisition. Debate is a skill challenge: each character speaks once, making a DC 18 check (Persuasion, History, Insight, Intimidation) aimed at one dragon. Each Receipt and Leverage point against the Hoard grants advantage on one check. Kessik’s royalty debt (“Finger-Lichin’ Good”) and the Five Colours receipts are especially potent; Four’s Collateral Tag (S09) shows the Company holds the Hoard’s collateral too.

A success wins that dragon’s vote. A dragon bound by dragonroot votes as it spoke. Pyrrhax votes with the party if they helped him in “@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-45.delivery-territory]{Delivery Territory}”.

“All those in favour,” says Vermillia through her teeth.

For a long moment the warehouse is silent except for the slow breathing of seven dragons. Then, one by one, claws rise.

DM Description

Four votes carry it. If the motion carries, the Hoard Syndicate withdraws; Hal Grundy writes the Minutes with shaking hands.

If Vermillia loses, she attacks—ancient red dragon, in a warehouse. The others will not help her if the vote was fair; Aurum and Slate may even help the party. Her kobold loyalists (20 kobolds, 4 dragonshields) swarm from the kitchens.

The Compliance Officer tries to annul the vote (“the motion was moved by a non-member”): [[/check skill=per dc=18]] @FWCheck[S19|skill=per dc=18|Defend the vote’s validity]{Request} (advantage if the party signed up for real membership in S09!) or defeat the Officer to validate it.

Checks & Roll Requests

SituationRollResult
Holding the line[[/check skill=ath dc=16]] @FWCheck[S19|skill=ath dc=16|Hold the doors against the kobolds]{Request}The kobolds are bottled up.

Developments

  • The Board Minutes are signed.

Scaling & Pacing

Vermillia at full strength is deadly at Level 15—if the vote was fair, Aurum and Slate fight beside the party; she flees at half hp.

@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S20|Scene 5 — The Final Contract]{Scene 5 — The Final Contract} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-43-counting-house-boardroom]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.tallis-vend-chairman]{Tallis Vend}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.pip-ashworth]{Pip-copy}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.counsel-ixabeth-vorr]{Counsel Ixabeth Vorr}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-02.public-face]{Harriet Hopwell}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S20]{The Final Contract (Courtesy Copy)}

Synopsis

An embossed invitation arrives, addressed to each character by full name, with the Rabbit Rating printed beside it. The Franchise Below’s grey door now has a handle.

Beyond it is the Counting House. A receptionist who is Pip Ashworth—except it isn’t; it is a Pip from a Ledger-page, a copy made when Pip signed—gives directions. The lift stops at floors the party didn’t press: Acquisitions, Collateral, Human Resources.

In the Boardroom every director is present or represented. Tallis Vend welcomes the party. Counsel Ixabeth Vorr (if allied) moves for an audit; the party reads the Grand Ledger. Then Item 7: the Final Contract is read aloud. Thirteen clauses. The signing date is the night the Golden Tusks are lit. The party’s names are typed on the signature line.

Background — DM Only

The Counting House is Creation & Company’s headquarters: a building outside every plane, reached through the first shop. Its floors are filing systems for everything the Company owns. Its Boardroom seats the ten umbrella directors and the Chairman.

Tallis Vend needs the party to sign willingly—or as willingly as Clause 77-B requires. He is courteous, patient and certain. He has been waiting four hundred years; he can wait a few more weeks.

Veronique Salt, if CEO of Crown & Cleaver, sits on the Board. She is planning an Extraordinary General Meeting.

Running This Mission

  • Make it clear through Ixabeth or Pip-copy that attacking in the Boardroom is suicide.
  • Each floor is a short vignette of dread and dark comedy.
  • The Final Contract reading is a set piece: read the clauses aloud, slowly, from the handout.
  • End with the party escorted out holding a courtesy copy—shaken, informed, and with a plan.

Threads In and Out

  • In: the Staff Only door (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S14]{S14}); Ixabeth (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S13]{S13}); Harriet Hopwell (S16); every director the party has met.
  • Out: end of Act IV. Three things must happen: break the seal (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S21]{S21}), stop the delivery (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S22]{S22}), turn the Board (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S23]{S23}).

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The invitation is waiting on your pillow when you wake: heavy grey card, embossed, with your full name—your real, full name, including the parts you never use—printed in silver, and beside it, your Rabbit Rating in stars.

Creation & Company requests your attendance at its Annual General Meeting. Attendance is not optional; it has been pre-recorded.

At THAC0 Spell, Hollis Quench meets you at the cellar steps, very pale. “The grey door,” he says. “It’s got a handle now.”

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The grey door opens onto a lobby of grey marble that goes up further than you can see. Filing cabinets line the walls, floor to unseen ceiling, with ladders on rails. Somewhere above, quills scratch, thousands of them, like rain. At the reception desk sits a harengon in a QuestRabbit cardigan, ears drooping, typing on a typewriter with no paper in it.

He looks up, and it is Pip. It is exactly Pip. Except his eyes are grey, and he does not recognise you.

“Welcome to the Counting House,” says Pip. “You’re expected. You’ve always been expected. Lifts are on the left.”

DM Description

The receptionist is a Pip from a Ledger-page: a copy made when Pip signed his QuestRabbit contract. The real Pip is at home, alive. This one is gentle and sad and gives directions. If asked, he knows he is a copy. He warns the party, quietly, not to attack anyone in the Boardroom: “Nobody leaves who does that. They become furniture.”

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.pip-ashworth]{Pip-copy}. Gentle, sad, helpful, grey-eyed. Everything Pip is, minus hope. He would like to be told about the real Pip.

The lift is a brass cage. You press BOARDROOM. The lift goes up—and stops at a floor you did not press. The doors open on a long grey corridor. A small brass sign reads ACQUISITIONS.

DM Description

The lift stops at three floors the party didn’t press. Each is a short scene of dread and dark comedy:

Acquisitions. The party’s own completed QuestRabbit contracts, framed, in a long gallery. Every job. Every star. A plaque: REPRESENTATIVES OF THE COMMONS — ONBOARDING (COMPLETE).Collateral. Rows of crates, like the CostCo-op vault but endless. Number Four’s box, empty, if rescued; a tag reading RELEASED (DISPUTED). Other boxes are labelled with names the party knows.Human Resources. A room full of blank five-star rating cards, thousands upon thousands, waiting to be filled—for whoever comes next, if the party fails or refuses.

Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S20|Board Seating Plan]{Board Seating Plan} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S20|Board Seating Plan]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Boardroom is a round grey room with a round grey table and a window onto nothing. Every director is here, in person or by proxy. Veronique Salt in crimson—or Baron Cleave in black. A glass tank of murky water in which something vast and eyed turns slowly: Ulth’Arabica. Papa Morvhal, grandfatherly and skeletal. The boardroom table itself breathes—that is SKÜ. Lady Crit, flipping a coin that always lands on its edge. Duke Vellichor, folded into a chair too small. Zafirah of the Brass Keys, smoke for hair. Auntie Vermillia, or Pyrrhax sweating in her chair. Deus Maxwell, wings folded, writing a plot twist on a napkin. Granny Quean’s chair—dripping cream, or empty. And the Mother Culture’s chair, dripping or empty.

At the head of the table, a small, precise man in a grey suit rises, smiling, and offers you each a chair with your name on it.

“Welcome,” says Tallis Vend. “We have been so looking forward to this.”

DM Description

Tallis Vend welcomes the party graciously and runs the meeting with perfect courtesy. Items 1–6 are routine (minutes, dividends, a moment of silence for the Sweet Covenant’s seat if broken). Each director reacts to the party according to what the party has done to them: hostility, interest, fear, respect.

Veronique (if present) passes a note under the table (the Twist).

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.tallis-vend-chairman]{Tallis Vend}. Small, precise, kind in manner, utterly certain. Never angry. He addresses each character by full name. He means everything he says.

Counsel Ixabeth Vorr rises from the Nine Circles delegation with a sheaf of papers and a silver pen. “Mr Chairman,” she says. “Under the Infernal Codex, Article Nine, I move for an audit of the Grand Ledger on behalf of the Representatives.”

Tallis Vend smiles, amused. “Granted. One minute each.” He gestures, and in the centre of the table, a book rises from nothing: grey, vast, its pages turning by themselves.

DM Description

If Ixabeth is allied, she moves for an audit; Vend grants it, amused. Each character may read the Grand Ledger for 1 minute. Each reader learns one true secret (DM’s choice—often a Receipt they missed, or where Tallis Vend’s weakness lies: Entry 1 has only one witness).

Harriet Hopwell, if persuaded (S16), confirms under oath that she did not write Clause 77-B, giving the party advantage on the Clause 77-B debate in S24.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

“Item seven,” says Tallis Vend. “Acquisition of the Material Plane. Progress.” He lays a single document on the table and reads it aloud, in his small, precise voice, clause by clause. Thirteen clauses. The room is silent except for the scratching of quills.

At the end, he turns the document around so that you can see the signature line. Your names are typed there. Your full names. Beside each, a small box, and in each box, five stars.

“The signing,” he says, “will take place on the night the Golden Tusks are lit. Do you have any questions?”

DM Description

Read the Final Contract aloud from the Courtesy Copy handout (or @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.finalcontract]{the Final Contract}). Then answer questions with Vend’s perfect courtesy. He will not be baited.

Compliance Officers escort the party out with a courtesy copy. If the party attacks, 10 Compliance Officers, a Senior Auditor and every hostile director act—they should not attack.

SituationRollResult

If they attack: 10 COs, a Senior Auditor and every hostile director. Make the consequence clear first.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Mission at a Glance

Code / ActS21 · Act V
Grade / LevelBlack Card · Level 17
Client@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-16]{The Golden Orcs} (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-01]{Creation & Company})
Session length1–2 sessions; a heist-planning war room and three simultaneous strikes against a clock
Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S21|Scene 1 — The War Room]{Scene 1 — The War Room} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-17-tallow-lane-tankard]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S21|Scene 2 — The Brandmere Grand Tusks]{Scene 2 — The Brandmere Grand Tusks} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a5-44-golden-orcs-grand-tusks]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S21|Scene 3 — The Summit Tusks]{Scene 3 — The Summit Tusks} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a5-45-golden-orcs-summit-tusks]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S21|Scene 4 — The Drowned Tusks]{Scene 4 — The Drowned Tusks} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a5-46-golden-orcs-drowned-tusks]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S21|Scene 5 — Midnight]{Scene 5 — Midnight} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a5-44-golden-orcs-grand-tusks]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-16]{Grukka Sweetfang}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-13.public-face]{Marda Hobb}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.cornelius-gaff]{Cornelius Gaff}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-43]{Centurion Marcus Crustus}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-07]{Don Pescatore Brine}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S21]{The Broken Seal}

Synopsis

Grukka Sweetfang—the Golden Orcs manager who is honestly great with kids—finds the party at the Tankard & Tallow. She has the survey maps. She’s been noticing for years: the golden tusk signs outside every branch are aligned, ley-line perfect, across the whole continent. They are a seal.

On Acquisition Eve, at midnight, every tusk will light, and whatever is signed in the Counting House will be notarised for all reality. Three tusks are anchors: the Brandmere Grand Tusks, the Summit Tusks in the mountains, and the Drowned Tusks beneath the harbour. Break two, and the seal cracks.

The Tankard & Tallow becomes a war room. Marda Hobb, Grukka, the Codfather families, kobold tunnel-runners and every ally the party has made gather. Three hours until midnight. Three anchors. Go.

Background — DM Only

Clause 6 of the Final Contract requires the Instrument to be “sealed under the Notarial Seal of the Company and witnessed by the Golden Tusks at the appointed hour.” The Golden Orcs chain was built as the seal: every branch’s sign is a node; the three anchor branches hold it together.

Each anchor tusk is a Golden Tusk construct when disturbed—a 40-foot golden iron golem. Compliance Officers guard each.

Pizza the Hutt’s land (“@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-44.the-hutt-below]{The Hutt Below}”) was meant to be a fourth, reserve anchor. If the party sided with Grubbo, the reserve doesn’t exist.

Running This Mission

  • Use real time in the war room if you can: 3 hours of game time, tracked on a clock.
  • Split the party only if your table enjoys it. Otherwise, allies handle one anchor while the party takes two.
  • Each ally group can hold, scout or distract one site. Tally them openly.
  • Midnight is the climax whatever happens: describe the tusks lighting across the continent.

Threads In and Out

  • In: Grukka (Golden Orcs); Marda and the Tankard (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S08]{S08}); the dragons (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S19]{S19}); “@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-13.tunnel-vision]{Tunnel Vision}”, “@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-07.sleeping-with-the-fishes]{Sleeping with the Fishes}”, “@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-44.the-hutt-below]{The Hutt Below}”, “Blizzard”.
  • Out: with the seal broken, Tallis Vend changes tactics. At dawn, Dominoancy’s diviners start screaming (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S22]{S22}).

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Grukka Sweetfang comes into the Tankard & Tallow with a crayon drawing from a child in one hand and a roll of survey maps under her arm. She is a big half-orc in a Golden Orcs polo shirt with a name badge that says GRUKKA — ASK ME ABOUT BIRTHDAY PARTIES. She spreads the maps on Marda’s table and pins the corners with tankards.

“I’ve been noticing for years,” she says. “The tusks. They’re all lined up. Every branch. Same angle, same height, perfect lines across the whole continent. I drew it out one night after a party.” She traces the lines with a thick finger, and you see it: a vast seal, drawn across the map in golden lines. “Midnight, tomorrow, they light them all at once. I think they’re going to stamp something.”

pages.name: Scene 1 — The War Room
pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-17-tallow-lane-tankard]{The Tankard & Tallow (war room)}
When: Acquisition Eve — 9 p.m.
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.corporate.CO-13.public-face]{Marda Hobb}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-16]{Grukka Sweetfang}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-07]{Don Pescatore Brine (the Codfather)}, kobold tunnel-runners, every ally
Handouts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S21|Grukka’s Survey Map]{Grukka’s Survey Map} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S21|Grukka’s Survey Map]{Show to players} · @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.handouts.S21|War Room — Ally Assignments]{War Room — Ally Assignments} @FWShow[fw.handouts.S21|War Room — Ally Assignments]{Show to players}

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Tankard & Tallow has never been so full. Every table is taken: Last Independents with their sleeves rolled up; Codfather families in dark coats, smelling of the sea; kobold tunnel-runners with lamps on their helmets; freed harvesters, freed workers, temple folk, old heroes, anyone who has ever shaken a hand with you. The fire roars. Marda Hobb stands behind the bar with her arms folded.

“Three hours,” she says. “Three tusks. Tell us where you want us.”

DM Description

A heist-planning scene. Lay out the three anchors and let the players assign allies. Each ally group can hold (keep reinforcements away), scout (advantage on the first check at a site) or distract (remove one enemy group) at one site. Typical allies:

Kobold tunnel-runners (if “@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-13.tunnel-vision]{Tunnel Vision}” preserved the tunnels): the party emerges beneath the Grand Tusks unseen. Codfather families: water breathing for the Drowned Tusks. Dragons who voted with the party in S19: fly the party to the Summit in minutes. Last Independents: hold the streets. The Last Five-Star Party: take an anchor themselves.

Track the time: travel between sites takes an hour without help.

Playing the NPCs

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The Grand Tusks stand in the heart of Brandmere, outside the city’s largest Golden Orcs: two curved golden tusks forty feet high, arching over the drive-thru like a gate. Tonight the square is cordoned off. Little Caesars Legion holds the perimeter in a shield wall three deep, torches burning. Two grey figures with clipboards stand beneath the tusks, waiting for midnight.

The gold hums. You can feel it in your teeth.

DM Description

If the kobold tunnels were preserved (“@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-13.tunnel-vision]{Tunnel Vision}”), the party emerges beneath the sign unseen. If not, they fight through Little Caesars Legion lines: 12 veterans and 2 centurions (Crustus leads, honourable as ever; he will accept a challenge).

Disturbing the tusk animates it: a Golden Tusk construct. Destroying it—or prying its core gem loose—breaks the anchor.

Features of the Area

The cordon
Shield wall; formation +2 AC.
The tusks
The construct; its core gem is in the arch’s keystone ([[/check skill=ath dc=18]] @FWCheck[S21|skill=ath dc=18|Climb the tusk to the keystone]{Request}).
The drive-thru
Cover; a speaker that plays the Golden Orcs jingle on loop.
Kobold tunnels
Exits in the drains.

Challenging Crustus[[/check skill=per dc=17]] @FWCheck[S21|skill=per dc=17|Challenge Crustus to single combat]{Request}If he loses, the Legion withdraws.

The Summit Tusks belong to a Golden Orcs at the top of a mountain pass—a branch that serves nobody, out of a blizzard that never stops. The tusks glow gold through the snow. Ice coats everything. And on the restaurant roof, coiled around the sign, is a white dragon, young and furious, chained to the tusks by a golden collar.

A mountain branch in a blizzard (Granny Quean’s, if the “Blizzard” contract wasn’t stopped). Dragons who voted with the party in S19 can carry them here in minutes; otherwise it’s a teleport or a very long night.

The young white dragon is chained to guard the anchor. It is Frostmother Ysk’s youngest, if she asked for it back in S19—freeing it (break the golden collar: [[/check skill=ath dc=19]] @FWCheck[S21|skill=ath dc=19|Break the dragon’s golden collar]{Request}) turns it against the construct.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Beneath the harbour, in the black water, there is a Golden Orcs. It sank with the old dock district a century ago and never closed. Its lights are still on, green and drowned. Its tusks glow gold through the murk. Through its windows, grey figures in waterlogged suits sit at desks, clocking in, clocking out, adding up columns that dissolve.

A pale figure drifts out of the dark toward you: a drowned man in a Crown & Cleaver suit, with a ledger tied to his ankle by a chain. “Cornelius Gaff,” he says, bubbles rising. “Former CFO. I asked about the Ledger. This way.”

DM Description

The Codfather families provide water breathing (or the party arranges it). Cornelius Gaff’s ghost (“@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-07.sleeping-with-the-fishes]{Sleeping with the Fishes}”) guides them. Drowned accountants (4 ghasts) still clock in. A kraken priest guards the anchor and calls the deep.

Underwater combat: disadvantage on most weapon attacks except piercing; fire spells don’t work.

Features of the Area

The drowned branch
Desks, tills, a drive-thru lane full of eels.
The tusks
Rising from the seabed.
The deep
Below; the kraken priest’s god listens.

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.cornelius-gaff]{Cornelius Gaff}. Mournful, precise, still an accountant. He would like his death recorded properly.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

At midnight, across the continent, the tusks light. From every town and crossroads and service station, two arches of gold blaze up into the night, and lines of light leap between them, mile after mile, drawing a seal across the sky like a signature on a page.

And where the anchors are broken, the lines falter. The light gutters. With a sound like paper tearing—a sound every person on the continent hears at once—the seal cracks across the sky.

DM Description

If two anchors are broken, the seal cracks: Clause 6 is void when the Broken Seal is presented in S24. If only one is broken, the seal holds but is flawed: the party gains advantage on Clause 6’s debate check in S24 instead of voiding it outright. If none, the seal holds.

If the party sided with Grubbo in “@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-44.the-hutt-below]{The Hutt Below}”, the reserve anchor doesn’t exist, and the seal cracks with one fewer anchor (only one needed).

A shard of golden tusk, still warm, is the Receipt.

@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S22|Scene 2 — Leg One: The Third Place]{Scene 2 — Leg One: The Third Place} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a5-47-last-slice-planar-route]{map}

@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S22|Scene 4 — Leg Three: Avernus]{Scene 4 — Leg Three: Avernus} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a5-48-avernus-delivery-toll-booth]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S22|Scene 5 — The Last Door]{Scene 5 — The Last Door} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a5-48-avernus-delivery-toll-booth]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.rook]{Rook}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-42]{Madame Olive Aspire}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.counsel-ixabeth-vorr]{Counsel Ixabeth Vorr}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S22]{The Undelivered Order}

Synopsis

Madame Olive Aspire bursts into the Tankard & Tallow with her hair on end. “It’s you. You ordered it. You haven’t yet, but you will have. You did.” Every diviner in Dominoancy has foreseen one pizza order ending the world. It printed at every branch at once. It is the Final Acceptance of Offer, in the party’s names.

With the seal broken, Tallis Vend needs the party’s acceptance delivered before the signing—and Clause 7 requires delivery “in good time and in good condition.” The courier is Rook, Dominoancy’s best, compelled by prophecy. Her route crosses four planes: the Third Place, Pandemonium, Avernus, and the Counting House’s loading bay.

The party gives chase. At the last door, Rook is sobbing; the prophecy compels her. The party can take the pizza by force, persuade her to break fate, or eat it. An order consumed cannot be delivered.

Background — DM Only

Dominoancy is Probability Brands’ divination pizza chain: every order foreseen, every delivery on time, guaranteed by fate. Lady Crit, its controller, lost a wager to Tallis Vend and is bound to deliver.

Rook is a courier who has never missed a delivery. She is foresighted—she sees every move a heartbeat before it happens. She is freed by any creature offering her a delivery she’d rather make.

Every ally and boon the party has gathered can matter here: freed concepts in the Third Place, harvesters in Pandemonium, Vellichor and Ixabeth in Avernus.

Running This Mission

  • Run each leg as a short chase with 3–4 rounds of checks and one complication.
  • Track Rook’s lead in “threshold steps”: if she crosses a threshold before being caught, she reaches the next plane.
  • Rook is not a villain. She is a victim of foresight. Make her sympathetic.
  • Eating the pizza should feel like a feast, a memory and a victory.

Threads In and Out

  • In: Olive Aspire (Dominoancy); freed concepts (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S17]{S17}); harvesters (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S11]{S11}); Vellichor and Ixabeth (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S13]{S13}).
  • Out: the contract can no longer be accepted in the party’s name; Veronique calls the Extraordinary General Meeting (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S23]{S23}).

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The door of the Tankard & Tallow bangs open at dawn and Madame Olive Aspire stumbles in, still in her Dominoancy apron, her hair standing straight up as if she has been struck by lightning. Her eyes are white from rim to rim. She points at you with a shaking finger.

“It’s you,” she says. “You ordered it. You haven’t yet, but you will have. You did.” She sits down hard on the floor. “Every diviner in the shop is screaming. One order. One pizza. And then everything is owned.”

pages.html:

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Every Dominoancy in Brandmere is in uproar. Order printers chatter out the same ticket, over and over, in every branch at once, spilling streamers of paper across the floor. The diviners at the ovens are on their knees, hands over their ears, seeing the same thing. The ticket reads: ONE (1) LARGE — FINAL ACCEPTANCE OF OFFER — DELIVER TO: THE COUNTING HOUSE — CUSTOMERS: and then your names.

Out in the yard, a lean woman in a Dominoancy jacket swings onto a delivery broom, a pizza box strapped to her back. She looks at you across the yard, and there are tears on her face. “I’m sorry,” says Rook. “I already saw you try.” And she is gone.

DM Description

Burning a copy of the ticket does nothing; the original is in Rook’s bag, inside the box. Olive Aspire can foresee the route: Brandmere, the Third Place, Pandemonium, Avernus, the Counting House. She gives the party a head start on each leg (advantage on the first check).

The party needs a way to follow: Olive knows each threshold (a Dominoancy oven that opens into the Third Place; the Bean There portal to Pandemonium; a Seven-Eleven Hells stockroom to Avernus).

Playing the NPCs

@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.staff.FR-42]{Madame Olive Aspire}. Foresees everything except her own divorce. Frantic, funny, brave. Speaks in mixed tenses.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Map: @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a5-47-last-slice-planar-route]{Planar route — the grey café}
When: Morning (grey)
Present: @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.rook]{Rook}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.core.quickling]{Brass Keys couriers}, freed concepts

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Through the oven and into the grey. The café again, endless tables, the cold-coffee smell. And ahead, weaving between tables at impossible speed, a smear of Dominoancy red on a broom, the only colour in the world.

DM Description

A chase through the grey café. Freed concepts from S17 can slow Rook: Weekends stalls her (she loses a round), Sleep makes her drowsy (disadvantage on her next check), Courage lends the party advantage, Healing restores them. Four quicklings of the Brass Keys (Counting House couriers) run interference.

Each round, each pursuer makes a chase check; three successes before Rook crosses the threshold (three rounds) catches her—briefly. She uses foresight to slip away, but loses the lead.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The wind hits you like a wall. The tunnels howl. The terraces are half-burned or half-harvested, depending on what you did here—and on the terraces, if you freed them, stand harvesters in grey sacking who have come back to tend what is left. They see you and start shouting, pointing down a side tunnel: “That way! The red one went that way!”

DM Description

The howling wind-tunnels, now half-harvested (S11). Freed harvesters shout directions (advantage on chase checks). The wind carries away anything not held tight—including, possibly, the pizza: each round, Rook makes a check to hold onto the box; if she fails, it tumbles and the party can catch it (an opportunity to end the chase early).

Pandemonium’s madness still applies.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The loading bay of the Counting House is grey concrete and a single grey roller door, with a Senior Auditor standing beside it holding a clipboard, its abacus-beads clicking. Rook has stopped in front of it. She is shaking. The pizza box is in her arms. She is sobbing.

“I don’t want to,” she says. “I’ve seen it. I’ve seen what happens after. But I have to. I’ve never missed one. I can’t miss one.” She looks at you. “Please. Do something I haven’t seen.”

DM Description

The party can:

Take the pizza by force: Rook (assassin with foresight: advantage on everything, attackers have disadvantage) and the Senior Auditor fight.Persuade her to break fate: Rook is freed by any creature offering her a delivery she’d rather make (a letter home, a gift for her mother, a pizza to an orphanage). [[/check skill=per dc=18]] @FWCheck[S22|skill=per dc=18|Offer Rook a delivery she’d rather make]{Request}.Eat it. An order consumed cannot be delivered. The Last Slice tastes like every meal the party ever shared. (Twist.)

The Senior Auditor tries to sign for the order: if it touches the box, it counts as delivered—protect the box.

pages.html:
GM ONLY

Mission at a Glance

Code / ActS23 · Act V
Grade / LevelBlack Card · Level 19
Client@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-01]{Creation & Company} (requisitioned by @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-03]{Crown & Cleaver})
Session length1–2 sessions: a vote count, one last holdout, and the meeting
Scenes@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S23|Scene 1 — Counting Votes]{Scene 1 — Counting Votes} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a2-17-tallow-lane-tankard]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S23|Scene 2 — The Last Holdout]{Scene 2 — The Last Holdout}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S23|Scene 3 — The Meeting]{Scene 3 — The Meeting} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-43-counting-house-boardroom]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S23|Scene 4 — The Vote]{Scene 4 — The Vote} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-43-counting-house-boardroom]{map}
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S23|Scene 5 — “I Own Myself”]{Scene 5 — “I Own Myself”} — @FWLink[Scene|fw.scene.fw-a4-43-counting-house-boardroom]{map}
Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.veronique-salt]{Veronique Salt}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.tallis-vend-chairman]{Tallis Vend}
Receipt@FWLink[Item|fw.item.receipt.S23]{The Minutes of Removal}

Synopsis

Veronique’s card arrives: “Six votes. Bring them. I’ll bring the room.” She has requisitioned an Extraordinary General Meeting of Creation & Company to remove Tallis Vend as Chairman. Proxies must be lodged in person.

The party tallies what they have: directors turned, destroyed or bargained with across the whole campaign. Then they choose the director they have not yet dealt with and run a compressed version of that umbrella’s Platinum contract—one strong scene, one fight—as the final push.

In the Boardroom, directors step forward to hand the party a slip of paper, or refuse. Compliance Officers try to annul proxies. If six seats are gone from Vend, the motion carries. Vend smiles: “You may remove the Chairman. You cannot remove what owns itself.” He walks to the Signing Room.

Background — DM Only

The Board has eleven seats besides the Chair. Removing the Chairman requires six seats voting against him (or vacant). Seats can be turned (a proxy given to the party), removed (the director destroyed or deposed), or bargained.

Common sources (from the spine and side contracts): Papa Morvhal (phylactery or “Papa’s Back”), Lady Crit (“@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.CO-07.the-big-game]{The Big Game}” or Loaded Dice), Duke Vellichor (S13 report or “@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-37.closing-time]{Closing Time}”), the Hoard (S19), Deus Maxwell (“@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-18.the-final-twist]{The Final Twist}”), Crown & Cleaver (Veronique, if Cleave is gone). Removed seats: ABI (“@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.CO-04.the-reservoir]{The Reservoir}”), ARC (“@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-68.the-showroom]{The Showroom}”), Sweet Covenant (S18).

Veronique will betray the party if they have no Leverage against her: she tries to take the Chair herself.

Running This Mission

  • Do the vote count with the players before the session—or as Scene 1, on a big board.
  • The Last Holdout is a compressed Platinum contract. Keep it to one scene and one fight.
  • The meeting is theatre: each director stands, speaks once, and hands over a proxy or refuses.
  • End on Vend’s line and the empty room.

Threads In and Out

  • In: everything. Every Receipt, Leverage point and director.
  • Out: the signing room is open. Tallis Vend waits with the Quill (@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.mission.S24]{S24}).

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The card is crimson, with one line in silver ink, and the faint smell of a thin cigarette.

Six votes. Bring them. I’ll bring the room. — V.

The Boardroom again. The round grey table. The window onto nothing. But this time, the gallery behind your chairs is full: the Commons Tally, every ally you have, standing in silence along the walls. Marda Hobb. Grukka. Ada and Molly. Sister Wren. The Harrow brothers, all five. They cannot vote. They can stare.

Tallis Vend sits at the head of the table, hands folded, unworried. Veronique Salt rises. “This Extraordinary General Meeting is called to order,” she says. “Sole item: removal of the Chairman. Proxies, please.”

DM Description

Directors step forward one by one to hand the party a slip of paper, or refuse. For each contested vote, a Compliance Officer tries to annul the proxy (“improperly lodged”)—defeating that Officer, or out-arguing it, validates the proxy.

Wavering directors can be persuaded with a check; Leverage gives advantage. Commons Tally allies watching grant +1 to each check (to a maximum of +5).

Key NPCs@FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.bestiary.tallis-vend-chairman]{Tallis Vend}, @FWLink[Actor|fw.actor.recurring.pip-ashworth]{Pip Ashworth}
Receipt—

Synopsis

There is no hook. The door is open. There is a table, a contract, a quill and a small grey man who has been waiting four hundred years.

Tallis Vend offers tea and explains, calmly and persuasively, that he will be a very good owner—no war, no hunger, everything managed. Then the Clause Debate: each round he reads a clause aloud, and a character presents the matching Receipt and argues. Success burns the clause off the page; failure lets him make a Ledger Entry.

When six clauses are voided, Vend stands, and the room becomes the whole Counting House. He cannot be killed while Entry 1 stands. When every clause is void, the Ledger falls open to Entry 1. The party presents the First Entry and says—any words will do—“We witness you.” Tallis Vend becomes a clerk in a grey suit: mortal, four hundred years old, and very tired. Then the Quill remains, and the signature line.

Background — DM Only

The Final Contract has thirteen clauses (77-B and 1–12), each voided by a Receipt earned across the campaign. A clause with no Receipt requires a DC 25 argument, three Commons Tally witnesses, or a unique exception (Sample Zero’s drop, the Sleeper’s testimony, Ixabeth Vorr’s motion).

Tallis Vend is CR 24. With the Minutes of Removal he has no Legendary Resistance and no directors’ protection. He cannot die while Entry 1 stands: reduced to 0, he rewrites himself (once per clause remaining).

Entry 1 has only one witness. A second witness makes it an ordinary claim—and ends him as an owner.

Running This Mission

  • Gather every Receipt the party holds. Use the strips from @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.finalcontract]{the Final Contract} and burn (or tear) them at the table.
  • Let Vend be genuinely persuasive. His offer is the most dangerous thing in the campaign.
  • Every ally present can testify, including Pip—the real one (Twist).
  • Give the endings room. The epilogue is one short scene per franchise the party touched.

Threads In and Out

  • In: every mission.
  • Out: the world, in whatever form the party leaves it.

The Hook

Read Aloud — The Hook@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

There is no hook. The door is open.

Beyond it is a small grey room: grey walls, a grey carpet, a single window onto nothing. A desk. Two chairs. On the desk, a book bound in grey, open to a blank page, and on the page a document, and beside the document a quill. A teapot steams gently. And in the far chair, hands folded, sits a small, precise man in a grey suit, who rises as you enter and smiles as if you are old friends.

“There you are,” says Tallis Vend. “Tea?”

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Tallis Vend lifts the contract, clears his throat, and begins to read. “Clause seventy-seven B. Signature Authority.” He looks at you over the page. “Do you object?”

DM Description

Run as structured combat. Each round, Vend reads a clause aloud (order: 77-B, then 1–12). On their turn, a character presents the matching Receipt and makes an argument: DC 18 Persuasion, Insight, History, Religion or Investigation, depending on how they make the case. Leverage against the umbrella involved, an allied witness, or a relevant boon grants advantage. Success voids the clause: it burns off the page.

A clause with no Receipt requires DC 25, three Commons Tally witnesses, or a unique exception (Sample Zero’s drop; the Sleeper’s testimony; Ixabeth Vorr’s motion; Weekends grants an extra round).

On a failure, Vend makes a Ledger Entry (see his stat block): he writes a line that becomes true—a character’s weapon was never theirs; an ally “resigned”; a wound “was always there”. Four Compliance Officers act on his turn as his hands.

Clause list and Receipts: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.finalcontract]{the Final Contract}. Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

Tallis Vend stands, and the room stands with him. The walls fall away like the sides of a box. You are in the Counting House—all of it, every floor at once, filing cabinets stacked into towers, ledgers flapping like birds, quills scratching in their millions. Every cabinet is a weapon. Every Compliance Officer is his hand.

“I have been very patient,” says Tallis Vend.

DM Description

Use Tallis Vend’s stat block (CR 24; without Legendary Resistance if the Minutes of Removal were earned). He cannot be killed while Entry 1 stands: reduced to 0 hp, he rewrites himself to full (once per clause remaining).

Keep voiding clauses mid-combat: a character can use their action to present a Receipt and argue (as above). Each voided clause removes one of his rewrites.

The Senior Auditor and Compliance Officers fight for him. Concept boons from S17 (Healing: every creature regains 50 hp; Courage: immunity to fear; Sleep: one Compliance Officer sleeps; Rest: a short rest in a moment) are spent here.

The Counting House folds back into the small grey room. The contract on the desk is a blank page, scorched at the edges. And the Grand Ledger, on its own, falls open to its very first page, where a single line in a small, precise hand reads:

Entry 1. Tallis Vend owns Tallis Vend, in perpetuity. Witnessed by: Tallis Vend.

Tallis Vend sits down in his chair. He looks at you, and for the first time, he looks afraid.

The party presents the First Entry (S14) and says—any words will do—“We witness you.” A second witness makes Entry 1 an ordinary claim. Tallis Vend becomes a clerk in a grey suit: mortal, four hundred years old, and very tired.

What happens to him is the party’s choice: imprisonment, a job, mercy, the Clerk of the First Sale’s counter, a bowl of soup at the Tankard & Tallow.

Read Aloud@FWChat[narrate]{Send to chat}

The contract is gone. But on the desk, the Grand Ledger is still open, and at the top of a fresh page, someone has written in a hand none of you recognise: The Material Plane. Current owner: Disputed.

The Quill lies beside it. It is waiting. It has always been waiting.

DM Description

The Material Plane’s title is still “Disputed”. The Quill remains. The endings:

Sign nothing. The Quill is left on the desk. The world stays disputed—messy, free, unowned.Write “owned by nobody” (as with Healing). The Ledger closes forever; every Folio crumbles; every Company contract in the world becomes paper.Sign for the Commons as Representatives—owning it in trust. A responsibility, not a prize.Break the Quill. No one can sign anything in the Ledger again.

Then: Epilogue. Run one short scene for each franchise the party touched, showing what became of it. End at the Tankard & Tallow, or at THAC0 Spell, at the table where it started.

Read one for each franchise the party touched. Use the first line if the party helped it, the second if they didn’t (or if it went badly).

FranchiseIf the party helpedIf not
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-01]{THAC0 Spell}Hollis Quench takes his first day off in twelve years. Dobbs runs the kitchen, singing. The iron door in the cellar is bricked up, and someone has chalked on the bricks: CLOSED. FOR GOOD.Hollis still works nights. The iron door hangs open, and on quiet evenings you can hear a shop bell, very far down.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-02]{Murder King}The Grand Throne changes its mascot. The new one is a baker in a paper crown. Duckworth Pym is allowed to stop smiling, and does, and then smiles anyway.The Murder King costume still walks after closing, pointing at the door marked STAFF ONLY.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-03]{Starkfucks}The Silent Roastery isn’t silent any more. Forty unseen servants have names on the rota, and a tea break every hour. Agnes runs the union from the window seat.The coffee is still very, very agreeable.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-04]{Gelatinous Cube}Bettina Soft blinks, slowly, for the first time in a year, and cries. Gelli lives in a tank by the door and hums to children.The freezer still hums its lullaby, and some nights the gelato tries to leave.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-05]{Wight Castle}Mortimer Pell takes down 143 Employee of the Month plaques and puts up one: a five-star review, framed, from a living customer.Mortimer is still on shift. He always will be.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-06]{Five Wights}Five pale brothers stand together behind every counter at once, finishing each other’s sentences with no gaps. Next door, Six Wights is fully booked.There is a gap in every sentence the brothers speak.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-07]{The Codfather}The Don hosts a wedding on the harbour wall, and nobody writes down the guest list. Cornelius Gaff’s bottle sits on the top table.The harbour is quieter. Too quiet.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-08]{Kobold’s Fried Chicken}Skritch Twice-Fried finally posts his letter to the dragon. The reply is a pay rise.The kobolds are still frying, and still writing letters nobody reads.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-11]{Dairy Quean}The Frost Lane Parlour sells honest ice cream made by a woman who used to stir vats in the dark. Granny Quean’s pinafore hangs in a museum.Some winters, it still snows indoors.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-13]{Krispy Kobold}Tikka Glaze-Snout opens a tea shop. It sells tea and nothing else. The HOT NOW sign hangs above the fryer, glowing contentedly.The queues still form whenever the rune glows, including people who aren’t hungry.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-16]{The Golden Orcs}The tusks are taken down and melted into a playground. Grukka Sweetfang throws the biggest birthday party Brandmere has ever seen.The tusks still stand, dark, aligned, waiting for another midnight.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-22]{Critical Wok}Lucky Oyelaran rolls a 3, and laughs until he cries.Everyone on Arena Street still rolls a little worse than they should.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-31]{Chick’n Familiar}Wendel Clasp sells chicken under his own name, on his own terms, and reads every contract twice.Every wizard in the Magus Ward still gets a chicken.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-34]{Goodberry’s}Bramble’s month-berries grow in every window box in the poor ward. Healing is free, and it stays that way.There is still a booth outside every temple. It is just quieter about what it sells.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-42]{Dominoancy}Madame Olive Aspire foresees nothing at all for a whole week, and finds it restful. Rook delivers a letter to her mother in the Quarter, and stays for tea.Every pizza still arrives exactly on time. Every single one.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-43]{Little Caesars Legion}Centurion Crustus finally eats a slice of the pizza. He is very moved.The Legion still marches, and the delivery zone keeps growing.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-44]{Pizza the Hutt}Grubbo’s mother sleeps peacefully beneath the floor, and the tusk site above her is a vegetable garden.ARC’s surveyors are still measuring.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-45]{The Crusty Dragon}Pyrrhax, healthy and free, makes the best pizza in the world, and does not tell his grandmother anything.The oven still sneezes.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-57]{Bean There, Summoned That}The portal in the back room is closed. Ada and Molly Fairweather sit in the window seat on Saturdays.The back room still howls.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-59]{Long Rest Inn}Room 303 is open to guests. Four old heroes stayed one last night there, on purpose, and checked out in the morning.Room 303 still says DO NOT DISTURB.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-61]{Plane Inn}The guest in Room 13 checks out at last, and the weather over Brandmere is perfect for a week.Room 13 is still occupied, and still asleep.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-65]{Wand-Mart}Rollback prices are just prices. The customers of Wand-Mart get their years back—most of them.Time payments are still accepted at all tills.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-67]{CostCo-op}Hal Grundy takes off his lanyard. There is a pale stripe round his neck. He wears a scarf over it, and whistles.Membership is still for life, and for your heirs.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.franchise.FR-68]{IKEA Mimic}The Showroom has an exit. It is clearly signposted. Björn Flatt is finally seen leaving.The arrows on the floor still lead inward.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-02]{QuestRabbit}Harriet Hopwell tears Clause 77-B out of every contract by hand. Pip Ashworth gives the party a five-star rating, and means it.QuestRabbit still counts the stars.
@FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.corp.CO-13]{The Tankard & Tallow}The fire is still burning. The table by the hearth has your names carved into it—not typed, carved. Marda pours. Nobody signs anything.Marda keeps a chair empty, in case.

End at the Tankard & Tallow, or at THAC0 Spell, at the table where it started.

pages.name: Twist, Rewards & Aftermath
pages.html:
GM ONLY

The Twist

Pip Ashworth—the real one—has followed the party in. He is holding his own QuestRabbit Contractor Agreement. “I checked,” he says. “Clause 77-B’s in mine too. Does that make me a representative? Can I sign as a witness?” He can. Any ally present can.

Rewards

  • The world, in whatever form the party leaves it.
  • Level 20.
  • A five-star rating from someone who means it.

Outcomes

If the party…Then…
signed nothingThe world stays disputed and free.
wrote “owned by nobody”The Ledger closes; every Company contract becomes paper.
signed for the CommonsThe party holds the world in trust.
broke the QuillNothing can be signed in the Ledger again.

Forward

  • Epilogue: run one short scene for each franchise the party touched, showing what became of it. End at the Tankard & Tallow, or at THAC0 Spell, at the table where it started.

Next mission: @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.flow]{Campaign Flow}

pages.name: Corporate Dossier
pages.html:
GM DOSSIER

Creation & Company

“Everything Is For Sale. Eventually.”

Parent of All0 franchisesBlack CardS24

Acquire the Material Plane. The Plane's title is Disputed because it has never been sold; a valid transfer needs signatures from trusted representatives of the people who live there.

Sigil Two interlocking C's closing into a ring, like a snake biting a ledger.
Headquarters The Counting House, a skyscraper-sized office outside reality, reachable through the Franchise Below.
Public Face None. Creation & Company has no public face. Its name appears only in fine print, on survey stones, and at the bottom of the Final Contract.
Controlled By Tallis Vend, Chairman. Four hundred years ago a mortal clerk wrote himself into the Grand Ledger as the owner of himself, in perpetuity, and the Ledger agreed. He has been buying since.
Culture Silent, patient, polite. Employees of the Counting House speak in minutes and memoranda. Nobody raises their voice. Nobody leaves.

Holdings & Assets

  • Ten Board Umbrellas. Crown & Cleaver Holdings, Arcane Beverage International, The Restaurant Necromancy Group, The Adventure Retail Consortium, Probability Brands Group, Nine Circles Hospitality, The Planar Hospitality Group, The Hoard Syndicate, McGuffin Narrative Holdings, Sweet Covenant Confectionery, plus QuestRabbit (via Human Resources).
  • Assets. The Grand Ledger; the Quill of Consideration; the Compliance Officers (inevitable-like auditors); the Golden Tusks seal; the Counting House itself.
  • Methods. Owns ten umbrella corporations through nested shells. Uses QuestRabbit to cultivate trusted heroes. Uses the Grand Ledger to make paperwork into reality.

DM Secret

Contracts

Black CardThe Final AcquisitionLevel 20Spine S24

BriefExecution of Instrument of Acquisition No. 1. Signatories to attend in person.

The Truth

The finale. The party is expected to sign.

Running It

Spine mission S24: Awaiting Signature****. The finale. In a small grey room at the heart of the Counting House, Tallis Vend lays the Final Contract before the party and hands them the Quill. They void it clause by clause with every Receipt they have gathered since level 1—and then decide what to sign, if anything. Run in full from Chapter 4.

Opposition

Tallis Vend, Chairman (see Bestiary), 4 Compliance Officers, 1 Senior Auditor, and whatever the Ledger writes into existence.

Pay

The world, in whatever form the party leaves it. Level 20. A five-star rating from someone who means it.

Thread

Epilogue: run one short scene for each franchise the party touched, showing what became of it. End at the Tankard & Tallow, or at THAC0 Spell, at the table where it started.

Leverage

+1 vs Creation & Company

GM DOSSIER

QuestRabbit Adventuring Solutions

“Adventure Is Dangerous. Employment Is Mandatory.”

Creation & Company0 franchisesCopperGold

Publicly: connect heroes with clients. Secretly: raise a party to five-star Rabbit Rating, the metaphysical threshold of public trust at which they qualify to sign for the commons.

Sigil A rabbit leaping through a star, inside a five-star rating bar.
Headquarters The Warren, a cheerful burrow-office tower on Guild Row in Brandmere, with job boards that glow when a contract is posted.
Public Face Harriet Hopwell, founder and CEO, a harengon who believes—truly—that she is helping adventurers find honest work.
Controlled By Creation & Company's Human Resources division. Hopwell sold QuestRabbit ninety-five years ago in a merger she was told was ‘friendly.’ She does not know what the Rabbit Rating measures.
Culture Relentlessly upbeat. Onboarding packs, team-building retreats, a newsletter called The Hop. Contractor liaisons like Pip Ashworth genuinely care.

Holdings & Assets

  • Assets. Enchanted job boards in every city. The Rabbit Rating. The Contractor Agreement. A newsletter.
  • Methods. Takes 30% of every contract. Records every contract in the Ledger. Every signed Contractor Agreement includes Clause 77-B, Signature Authority, in text too small to read without magic.

DM Secret

CopperOnboardingLevel 1

BriefWelcome to QuestRabbit! Please sign here, here, here and here.

The Truth

The Contractor Agreement. Every clause is harmless except Clause 77-B, which appoints the signatory as a ‘Representative of the Commons for purposes of future transactions.’

Running It

Played as the opening scene of S1. Pip walks the party through the agreement. Anyone who reads the fine print (Investigation DC 20 [[/check skill=inv dc=20]], or detect magic) sees the tiny clause shimmer; Pip has no idea what it means.

Opposition

None.

Pay

A QuestRabbit badge, a welcome hamper, and a 1-star rating.

Thread

Clause 77-B is voided at the end of the campaign by the very first Receipt (Incident Report 77-B, S1).

+1 vs Creation & Company

GoldPerformance ReviewLevel 12

BriefMandatory annual contractor assessment with a senior partner.

The Truth

Harriet Hopwell herself interviews the party—and slips them a note: ‘Don't reach five stars.’ She has started to suspect.

Running It

A tense comedic review in an office full of listening ears. Harriet gives the party the keys to QuestRabbit's archive if they convince her they're on her side.

Opposition

None—unless a Compliance Officer was watching.

Pay

A pay rise from 70% to 75%.

Thread

The archive holds records of the Last Five-Star Party. Leads to S16.

GoldThe Beans of PandemoniumLevel 9Spine S11

BriefSeasonal premium crop procurement on an adjacent plane. Standard hazard pay applies.

The Truth

The plantations grow Compliance, harvested by people who have forgotten who they were.

Running It

Spine mission S11: The Beans of Pandemonium****. A procurement run to Pandemonium's howling plantations reveals Compliance, the bean that makes the world agreeable, and the lost people who harvest it. Run in full from Chapter 4.

Opposition

Cambion overseer (cambion), 4 howlers, 1 wind-elemental storm (air elemental ×2), Pandemonium's madness (DC 14 Wisdom save [[/save wis dc=14]] each hour).

Pay

2,000 gp less 30% if harvested. The freed harvesters' gratitude if not.

Thread

ABI's supply is cut; Ulth'Arabica takes notice. Compliance starts wearing off across the city.

Leverage

+1 vs Arcane Beverage International

PlatinumThe Third PlaceLevel 14Spine S17

BriefNew branch construction in pocket dimensions encountering pre-existing tenancy.

The Truth

The pocket dimensions are where acquired concepts go. Something that used to be Healing lives there now.

Running It

Spine mission S17: The Third Place****. Starkfucks is building in the Third Place, the grey limbo where Creation & Company stores everything it has acquired and forgotten. The party finds the exiled concepts—Healing, Weekends, Courage—and a Folio that lists them all. Run in full from Chapter 4.

Opposition

Thrall foreman (use a knight, with Ulth'Arabica able to cast dominate person through him once), 4 stone golems (construction crew), 2 grey concept-eaters (nightwalker-lite: use a wraith with 150 hp and the Annihilating Aura trait at 1d6).

Pay

No fee (ABI will not pay after this). The concepts' blessings: each freed concept grants the party one boon usable in S24 (Healing: every creature regains 50 hp; Courage: immunity to fear; Sleep: one Compliance Officer falls asleep; Weekends: an extra round in the clause debate).

Thread

Ulth'Arabica has seen the party through its thrall. ABI's director will be waiting in The Reservoir. The Board now considers the party a threat, not an asset—but Tallis Vend still needs their signatures.

Leverage

+1 vs Arcane Beverage International

No. 04

GM DOSSIER

Gelatinous Cube

“There's Always Room for Dessert.”

Sweet Covenant ConfectioneryCopperSilverGoldS3S3S18

An artisan gelato chain serving perfectly cubical frozen desserts. Its mascot Gelli is supposedly a cartoon character. Several employees know otherwise. Everything is made in-house, from a culture older than the house.

Parent Company Sweet Covenant Confectionery
Flagship The Canal Street Creamery, managed by Bettina Soft (human, relentlessly positive, has not blinked in a disturbing while). The walk-in freezer hums a lullaby.
Contract Range Copper (L1) · Silver (L2) · Silver (L2) · Gold (L15)
Leverage Feeds Board seat of Sweet Covenant Confectionery — Removed if the Mother Culture is freed or destroyed (S18) and Granny's Blizzard is stopped.

Menu & Products

  • Gelato-nous Cube. Nine cubes, nine flavours. Engulfs your spoon if you are slow.
  • Ochre Jelly Lemon. Splits into two scoops when cut. Legally one purchase.
  • Black Pudding Chocolate. Dissolves wooden spoons. Metal spoons provided at a deposit.
  • Gray Ooze Stracciatella. Corrodes the bowl. Eat fast.
  • Oozeberry Sorbet. Resistance to acid damage for 10 minutes.
  • Neapolitan Mimic. The strawberry layer is not strawberry. It is fine.
  • Cube of Cold. DC 12 Con save or brain freeze: disadvantage on Int checks for 1 minute.
  • The Dungeon Floor Sundae. Contains 1d4 coins, a key, and a boot. Collect them all.
  • Slime Lime. Climb speed on smooth surfaces for 1 minute. Sticky.
  • Mint Condition. Restores 1 hit point and your dignity.

DM Secret

Contracts

CopperThe Runaway ScoopLevel 1

BriefExperimental product has exited premises via the drainage system. Recover prior to public awareness.

The Truth

A batch made with too much Mother Culture woke and fled into the sewers, where it has been eating rats and absorbing their memories.

Running It

Sewer crawl through three flooded junctions. The scoop is terrified and hides in a drain pipe; players who speak gently can coax it out (DC 13 Animal Handling). Killing it releases a rat's-eye memory of Bettina feeding a man into the vats.

Opposition

The Runaway Scoop (ochre jelly, 30 hp), 2 swarms of rats, 1 giant rat that the scoop has partially absorbed.

Pay

40 gp less 30%. Free gelato for a year (the gelato remembers you).

Thread

The rat memory is the first hint that employee retention is literal.

+1 vs Sweet Covenant Confectionery

The Truth

Gelli is an actual domesticated gelatinous cube—and several missing employees are still inside it, alive.

Running It

Spine mission S3: Gelli Goes Missing****. Missing workers, a missing mascot, and a gelatinous cube who is loyal to the wrong people. The party learns that the Sweet Covenant ‘retains’ employees literally. Run in full from Chapter 4.

Opposition

Gelli (gelatinous cube, 84 hp, friendly if fed), 4 Covenant handlers (bandits), 1 green hag supervisor, Auntie Curdle (if not met before).

Pay

150 gp less 30%. One star. Possibly a pet gelatinous cube.

Thread

The freed workers mention the Deep Dairy and ‘the Mother down below’. This sets up S18.

Resolved in the same spine contract as Gelli Goes Missing.

Spine mission S3: Gelli Goes Missing****. Missing workers, a missing mascot, and a gelatinous cube who is loyal to the wrong people. The party learns that the Sweet Covenant ‘retains’ employees literally. Run in full from Chapter 4.

Opposition

Gelli (gelatinous cube, 84 hp, friendly if fed), 4 Covenant handlers (bandits), 1 green hag supervisor, Auntie Curdle (if not met before).

150 gp less 30%. One star. Possibly a pet gelatinous cube.

The freed workers mention the Deep Dairy and ‘the Mother down below’. This sets up S18.

+1 vs Sweet Covenant Confectionery

BriefLegacy supplier awakening event. Continuity of dessert supply is the priority.

The Truth

The primordial ooze wakes. Its Sample Zero proves nothing in Creation & Company's portfolio is perpetual.

Running It

Spine mission S18: The Mother Culture****. The primordial ooze beneath the Sweet Covenant's vats wakes up and calls every dessert home. The party descends into the Deep Dairy, confronts Granny Quean, and decides the fate of Sample Zero—proof that nothing in the Company's portfolio is perpetual. Run in full from Chapter 4.

Opposition

Granny Quean (night hag, 150 hp, casts as a 15th-level warlock: hold monster, dominate person, banishment), Auntie Curdle (green hag, if she sides with Granny), 4 ochre jellies, 2 black puddings, the Mother Culture (see Bestiary; she should not be fought if avoidable).

Bettina Soft's grateful testimony; the freed workers; the Mother's drop (see twist). The Sweet Covenant's Board vote is removed if Granny is defeated or deposed (see Coven Politics).

With ABI wounded and the Sweet Covenant broken, the Board convenes emergency sessions. Hal Grundy of CostCo-op calls QuestRabbit: the dragons must meet in person.

GM DOSSIER

Wight Castle

“Sliders to Die For.”

Crown & Cleaver HoldingsCopperSilverGold

Cheap miniature burgers served twenty-four hours a day by unsettlingly pale employees. The lights are always slightly too bright. You always leave with more sliders than you ordered.

Parent Company Crown & Cleaver Holdings
Flagship The Old Gate Castle, a squat white keep of a restaurant. Night manager Mortimer Pell has been Employee of the Month for 143 consecutive years and has the plaques to prove it.
Contract Range Copper (L2) · Silver (L5) · Gold (L10)
Leverage Feeds Board seat of Crown & Cleaver Holdings — Baron Cleave will never flip. His vote is removed if he is destroyed (S15) or if Veronique takes his seat.

Menu & Products

  • Wight Sliders. Tiny, square, pale. Heals 1 hit point each, maximum six.
  • Graveyard Shift Six-Pack. Six sliders and a candle. Only sold after midnight.
  • Crypt Fries. Cold on arrival. Always cold. They were fried.
  • Spectral Shake. Passes through your hand on a 1 on a d6.
  • Dead-Onion Rings. Grey onions. Speak with dead for one question, answered by an onion.
  • The Coffin Box. Thirty sliders in a small coffin. The coffin is included.

DM Secret

Contract Guides

Each contract below has a full DM guide: hook, three scenes with read-aloud and roll requests, opposition linked to actors, a handout and a Record Leverage button.

  • Copper L2 — @FWLink[JournalEntry|fw.contract.FR-05.graveyard-shift]{Graveyard Shift}

Contracts

CopperGraveyard ShiftLevel 2

BriefNight-staff activities after 00:00 are not reflected in timesheets. Observe and report.

The Truth

After midnight the staff clock out of their bodies and haunt the back office, reconciling receipts for Crown & Cleaver's head office by moonlight.

Running It

A stakeout from a booth. Staff flicker; one ghost staffer tries to hand a receipt to the party (it's a receipt for the party's own future purchase, dated next year). Mortimer notices them and offers coffee and an honest conversation.

Opposition

2 specters (hostile only if the party disrupts the reconciling), 4 zombie line cooks.

Pay

50 gp less 30%.

Thread

The future-dated receipt is Ledger-backed. The party has been debited in advance.

Leverage

+1 vs Crown & Cleaver Holdings

SilverThe Employee of the MonthLevel 5

BriefRecognition programme integrity concern. The same team member has won for 143 years.

The Truth

Head Office wants Mortimer retired—destroyed—because an internal audit discovered he remembers everything. He does not want to die a second time. He wants a union rep.

Running It

The party is sent to ‘deliver his retirement package.’ Mortimer asks for a character reference instead. If they protect him, he becomes an ally who can recite any Crown & Cleaver purchase in the last century (an advantage die on any investigation of Crown & Cleaver).

Opposition

A Crown & Cleaver ‘retirement team’: 1 wight, 3 ghouls in visors, 1 Team Deliverables member for spite.

Pay

200 gp less 30%, or Mortimer's lifetime loyalty.

Thread

Mortimer recalls selling Crown & Cleaver ‘a kingdom, small, on credit’ in the ledger 90 years ago.

Leverage

+1 vs Crown & Cleaver Holdings

GoldSlider Into DarknessLevel 10

BriefMeat-processing facility ceased communication with Head Office. Restore supply chain.

The Truth

The facility processes offal from Pandemonium-fed herds; the herds ate the staff and began franchising. The Restaurant Necromancy Group sent zombies to fix it; they joined the herd.

Running It

Industrial horror crawl: conveyors, hook lines, cold stores. The herd leader, a chimera-like thing of stitched cattle, runs the plant with a clipboard. The plant's shipping ledger is a Folio fragment—entries written in it come true for meat.

Opposition

Stitched herd (2 chimeras reskinned, 1 flesh golem ‘Plant Manager’), 8 zombies, 1 hell hound in a delivery van.

Pay

1,200 gp less 30%. The Folio fragment.

Thread

First handled Folio: proof that ledger entries alter reality. Leverage against Crown & Cleaver and RNG.

Leverage

+1 vs Crown & Cleaver Holdings

Five undead brothers established the original restaurant. There are now thousands of branches. The same five brothers appear to personally operate every single one, simultaneously, with identical warmth and identical burns on their forearms.

SilverWhere's Number Four?Level 7Spine S9

BriefPartner availability concern affecting operational reality at all locations.

The Truth

Number Four is held as collateral in the CostCo-op executive vault. Freeing him proves collateral can be recovered.

Running It

Spine mission S9: Where's Number Four?****. One of the Five Wights is missing, and reality is fraying. He is being held as collateral by Creation & Company in the CostCo-op executive vault. Run in full from Chapter 4.

1 Compliance Officer (see Bestiary), 6 kobolds, 2 guard drakes, 4 mimic pallets.

700 gp less 30%. The Five Wights' eternal gratitude (a free meal at any branch forever).

The CostCo-op vault and its seven dragon directors return in S19. Four is a witness in S24.

PlatinumInfinite Franchise TheoryLevel 13

BriefUnauthorised independence sentiment among brand-continuity simulacra.

The Truth

To staff thousands of branches the brothers use simulacra. Some simulacra have developed souls and want their own restaurant. The brothers don't know what to do; Crown & Cleaver wants them unmade.

Running It

Mediate the first ever simulacrum strike, held in a branch where every staff member is a Harrow. A simulacrum called Four-and-a-Half runs the picket. The party can broker a franchise of their own for the simulacra—‘Six Wights’—which Crown & Cleaver will try to burn down that night.

Opposition

Crown & Cleaver enforcers: 1 death knight lieutenant, 4 wights, 2 helmed horrors. Or, if the party sides with Corporate, 12 simulacra fighting for their lives (guilt is free).

Pay

6,000 gp less 30%, or the loyalty of Six Wights (a safe house in every city).

Thread

Six Wights' existence is a legal precedent: a franchise that owns itself. It gives Leverage against Crown & Cleaver and advantage on the S23 proxy vote.

The Codfather

A seafood empire controlled by several extremely polite halfling families. They never raise their voices. They never forget a birthday. They never, ever sign anything with Creation & Company.

  • Capo's Cod & Chips. The Don's recipe. Complimented aloud, it grants advantage on the next Codfather favour.
  • Don Calamari. Tentacles, lemon, respect.
  • The Family Platter. Serves six. If one of the six betrays the others, the platter knows.
  • Sauce of Omertà. You cannot speak about anything you ate with it.

Contracts

CopperA Fishy BusinessLevel 2

BriefCommunity support contributions have gone missing between collection and deposit.

The Truth

The protection money was paid to protect the harbour from Crown & Cleaver arsonists, and a courier was bribed to lose it. The courier is terrified, and Murder King's local manager paid him.

Running It

Tail the courier through the fish market, a card game and a rooftop chase. He will confess if promised protection. The Don is grateful—and the party learns the halflings keep no written records at all.

Opposition

4 thugs, 1 bandit captain in a Murder King paper crown.

Pay

80 gp. The Codfather pays in full; there is no 30%. Pip is baffled.

Thread

The Don owes the party a favour. Favours from the Codfather are unrecordable by the Ledger—remember this in Act V.

+1 vs Crown & Cleaver Holdings

BriefNegotiate exclusive fishing rights with regional sahuagin interests.

The Truth

The Planar Hospitality Group has already promised the sahuagin a hotel on the reef. The sahuagin baron will take whichever deal feeds more of her young.

Running It

Undersea diplomacy with water breathing supplied (grudgingly) by the Don. A PHG efreeti negotiator arrives mid-meeting in a bubble. The best deal involves nobody signing anything.

Opposition

If it goes wrong: 1 sahuagin baron, 1 sahuagin priestess, 6 sahuagin, 2 reef sharks.

Pay

400 gp. Fishing rights make the party honorary family.

Thread

The sahuagin baron's account of the PHG deal names Zafirah of the Brass Keys. Leverage against PHG.
